sentences.en: This is the 99% Invisible Breakdown of The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 这是《权力掮客》的 99% 隐形解析。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And I'm Elliot Kalin.
sentences.zh: 我是埃利奥特·卡林。

sentences.en: Today, we're covering part four, the end of the section called The Use of Power.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲的是第四部分，即“权力的使用”这一章节的结尾。

sentences.en: That's chapters 21 through 24.
sentences.zh: 也就是第 21 到 24 章。

sentences.en: And in my book, those are pages 402 to 495.
sentences.zh: 在我的书里，对应的是第 402 到 495 页。

sentences.en: Later on, our guest for this episode will be Brandi Zdrozny.
sentences.zh: 稍后，本期节目的嘉宾将是布兰迪·兹德罗兹尼。

sentences.en: She's a senior reporter for NBC News who covers misinformation, conspiracy theories, and the internet.
sentences.zh: 她是 NBC 新闻的资深记者，负责报道虚假信息、阴谋论和互联网相关议题。

sentences.en: She recently finished The Power Broker, and she's got a great perspective on what the book says about the press and its relationship to power, what has changed in journalism,
sentences.zh: 她最近读完了《权力掮客》，对于书中关于媒体及其与权力关系的内容，以及新闻业发生了什么变化，她有着独到的见解，

sentences.en: and what remains the same.
sentences.zh: 同时也谈到了哪些东西依然如故。

sentences.en: So when we last left The Power Broker, the Depression is dawning.
sentences.zh: 上次我们讲到《权力掮客》时，大萧条正处于黎明前夕。

sentences.en: Robert Moses keeps opening state park projects to great public acclaim.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·摩西不断开启州立公园项目，并获得了巨大的公众赞誉。

sentences.en: He's just a hero.
sentences.zh: 他简直就是个英雄。

sentences.en: Moses gets Governor Lehman and Mayor LaGuardia to give him total control over anything remotely park-related in New York City.
sentences.zh: 摩西让雷曼州长和拉瓜迪亚市长授予他纽约市所有与公园相关事务的绝对控制权。

sentences.en: He passes a new law where a state person and a city person can do all this stuff at once.
sentences.zh: 他通过了一项新法律，让州政府官员和市政府官员可以同时处理所有这些事务。

sentences.en: He immediately refurbishes New York City's major parks.
sentences.zh: 他随即翻新了纽约市的主要公园。

sentences.en: He's unveiled this massive plan for building expressways and bridges through and around the city so that people don't have to go through Manhattan to get to places on either side anymore.
sentences.zh: 他公布了一项宏大的计划，要在城市内部及周边修建高速公路和桥梁，这样人们就不必再穿过曼哈顿去往两侧的目的地了。

sentences.en: And the Triborough Bridge Authority has begun to actually start building the Triborough Bridge,
sentences.zh: 三区大桥管理局也已经真正开始动工修建三区大桥，

sentences.en: which will become the centerpiece and provide all the funding for his empire as well.
sentences.zh: 这将成为他帝国的核心，并为他提供所有的资金来源。

sentences.en: But there's a little bit going on here where his pettiness is starting to seep out to people who are his staunchest allies.
sentences.zh: 但这里发生了一点小插曲，他的小家子气开始流露出来，甚至针对他最坚定的盟友。

sentences.en: So, you know, he destroys the Central Park Casino just because it was Jimmy Walker's playground, and he just, out of spite,
sentences.zh: 比如，他摧毁了中央公园赌场，仅仅因为那是吉米·沃克的地盘，他纯粹是出于恶意，

sentences.en: he just wants to level it instead of turning it into something equally good or better, you know?
sentences.zh: 他只想把它夷为平地，而不是把它改造成同样好甚至更好的东西，你懂吗？

sentences.en: And so that's where we are.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们目前所处的情况。

sentences.en: So he's still like in that phase where he's getting a lot done.
sentences.zh: 所以他依然处于那种干劲十足的阶段。

sentences.en: Most people are on his side.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都站在他这一边。

sentences.en: But that is about to take a turn right now with Chapter 21, The Candidate.
sentences.zh: 但随着第 21 章《候选人》的开始，一切即将发生转变。

sentences.en: And so, Elliot, I love this opening line.
sentences.zh: 埃利奥特，我太喜欢这一章的开篇了。

sentences.en: Could you read the opening line to The Candidate?
sentences.zh: 你能读一下《候选人》的开篇吗？

sentences.en: It's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 写得太棒了。

sentences.en: The Candidate begins thusly.
sentences.zh: 《候选人》是这样开头的。

sentences.en: There had been a day in 1934 on which the cheering had stopped.
sentences.zh: 1934 年的某一天，欢呼声停止了。

sentences.en: It was the day Robert Moses started running for governor.
sentences.zh: 那正是罗伯特·摩西开始竞选州长的那一天。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, boy, that's not a good sign.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，天哪，这可不是什么好兆头。

sentences.en: He's used to everyone loving him, and he's like, great, I'm going to run for public office.
sentences.zh: 他习惯了每个人都爱他，所以他觉得，太好了，我要去竞选公职。

sentences.en: And it is almost as if he decides to do everything he possibly can to undo every good thing about his reputation during this very brief run for governor.
sentences.zh: 而在这次短暂的州长竞选中，他几乎决定竭尽所能去毁掉自己声誉中所有好的方面。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: And this pettiness that you were talking about, it's starting to seep out.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到的那种小家子气，开始显露出来了。

sentences.en: It's almost like it starts gushing at this point.
sentences.zh: 到了这一步，简直就像是喷涌而出。

sentences.en: The faucet gets stuck open, and he'll fix that leaky pettiness faucet, but it takes him a little bit of time.
sentences.zh: 水龙头被卡住了，虽然他会去修那个漏水的小家子气水龙头，但这需要一点时间。

sentences.en: And it's just amazing.
sentences.zh: 这简直太神奇了。

sentences.en: So, Caro points out that in later years, Moses would tell people after he knew that he had lost the governorship.
sentences.zh: 卡罗指出，多年后，在摩西知道自己输掉州长竞选后，他会告诉别人。

sentences.en: Spoiler alert.
sentences.zh: 剧透预警。

sentences.en: He does not become governor.
sentences.zh: 他没当上州长。

sentences.en: I'll just tell you right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就告诉你。

sentences.en: He'll tell people later, I did it reluctantly.
sentences.zh: 他后来会告诉别人，我是勉为其难才参选的。

sentences.en: I was just trying to hold the party together.
sentences.zh: 我只是想维持党内的团结。

sentences.en: But the people around him tell Caro that he was hungry for it.
sentences.zh: 但周围的人告诉卡罗，他当时对权力渴望至极。

sentences.en: And he gets offered the nomination by our old friend Truby Davison, the wealthy young state legislature who years earlier,
sentences.zh: 他从我们的老朋友特鲁比·戴维森那里获得了提名，那位年轻富有的州议员，多年前，

sentences.en: Moses had tricked him into sponsoring his state parks bill that made him the most powerful man in New York State.
sentences.zh: 摩西曾诱骗他发起州立公园法案，这使摩西成为了纽约州最有权势的人。

sentences.en: And there's a little bit here about how Davison is working for the old guard of the state GOP, and those are the rich barons.
sentences.zh: 这里还提到戴维森是如何为州共和党的旧势力效力的，也就是那些富有的权贵们。

sentences.en: They want someone who will stand for them against the New Deal and against Mayor LaGuardia and that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一个能代表他们对抗“新政”、对抗拉瓜迪亚市长之类的人。

sentences.en: And they also – they want a governor who's finally going to take all these public power sources like Niagara and turn them over to private companies that just by an amazing coincidence,
sentences.zh: 而且他们还想要一位州长，最终能把尼亚加拉等所有公共电力资源转交给私人公司，而令人惊奇的巧合是，

sentences.en: many of the old guard GOP members own stock in.
sentences.zh: 许多共和党旧势力成员都持有这些公司的股份。

sentences.en: This is just regular government stuff.
sentences.zh: 这只是常规的政府运作而已。

sentences.en: It's fine.
sentences.zh: 没事的。

sentences.en: And Caro goes a little bit into the interior fighting between – in the GOP that Moses' old enemy, W.
sentences.zh: 卡罗还深入探讨了共和党内部的斗争，摩西的老对手 W·金斯兰·梅西正在与旧势力争夺提名人选。

sentences.en: Kingsland Macy, was fighting with the old guard about who was going to be the nominee.
sentences.zh: 这听起来就像是有八个人在掌控着城市和州政府，而且他们总是针锋相对。

sentences.en: And it makes it sound like there's like eight people who run the city and state government, and they're always butting heads.
sentences.zh: 情况确实如此。

sentences.en: And that's kind of what it's like.
sentences.zh: 就像你读到联邦政治时，也是同样的名字反复出现。

sentences.en: Like if you – when you read about even federal politics, it's the same names over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大国。

sentences.en: This is a big country.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 人竟然这么少。

sentences.en: There's so few people.
sentences.zh: 这里有一句话——虽然不是特别重要，

sentences.en: And there's one sentence here that – it's not super important,
sentences.zh: 但我还是想读一下，因为它可能是我书中个人最喜欢的一句话，仅仅是因为我不得不假设卡罗在这句话里融入了多少刻意的讽刺。

sentences.en: but I just want to read it because it's maybe my favorite sentence in the book just for how much I have to assume deliberate satire Caro gets into this one sentence.
sentences.zh: 他引用了特鲁比·戴维森多年后作为老人时告诉他的话，关于金斯兰·梅西如何想让西伯里法官成为州长候选人，

sentences.en: So he is relating a quote that Truby Davison as an older man years later is telling him about how Kingsland Macy wanted Judge Seabury to be the nominee for governor,
sentences.zh: 而西伯里甚至不是共和党人，而且他还是个改革派。

sentences.en: and Seabury is not even a Republican, and he's a reformer anyway.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我们只要听到这些就够了，”特鲁比·戴维森三十年后咆哮道，

sentences.en: Well, that was all we had to hear, Truby Davison would growl three decades later,
sentences.zh: 他坐在位于孔雀角豪宅 30 英尺高的书房里，一条患痛风的腿架在脚凳上，吃着樱桃朱比利甜点，

sentences.en: sitting with one gouty leg propped on a footstool in the 30-foot-high study of his mansion on Peacock Point, topping off with cherries jubilee,
sentences.zh: 那是穿着白外套的管家端上来的简餐，他凝视着戴维森庄园半英里长的露台槌球场。

sentences.en: a light lunch served by a white-coated butler, and staring out across the Davison compound's half-mile-long terraced croquet court.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是——这只是一句描述他房子的句子，当时我猜卡罗去采访了他。

sentences.en: That's just – it's one sentence just describing his house when Caro, I assume, went to talk to him.
sentences.zh: 这一句话里塞进了太多的社会阶层信息。

sentences.en: And there's so much succession just crammed into that one sentence.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I love it so much.
sentences.zh: 这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It's just amazing.
sentences.zh: 这很好地说明了，这些人就是当时支持摩西的人。

sentences.en: And a good way of getting across, these are the people who are backing Moses at this point.
sentences.zh: 是的，而这些人正是摩西当初建立声誉时所对抗的人，事实上，完全是同一批人。

sentences.en: Yeah, and these are the people where he built his reputation fighting these very same people, in fact, the exact same people.
sentences.zh: 正是那些他曾经说“他们是权势，而我代表人民”的人。

sentences.en: The exact same people who he was like, they're the power and I'm for the people.
sentences.zh: 现在这些人却说，嘿，你为什么不当我们的州长候选人呢？

sentences.en: These are the same people who are now like, hey, why don't you be our candidate for governor?
sentences.zh: 因为他们开始意识到关于罗伯特·摩西的一点：他早年对他们充满敌意，并不是因为他是什么激进的自由派，

sentences.en: Because they've started to realize something about Robert Moses, that when he was hostile to them earlier, it wasn't because he was this like radical liberal,
sentences.zh: 而是因为他是一个知道自己有权势的人，因为阿尔·史密斯在支持他。

sentences.en: but because he was a man who knew he had power because Al Smith was backing him.
sentences.zh: 当他失去那种支持时，他开始变得更加顺从。

sentences.en: And when he lost that backing, he started becoming more accommodating.
sentences.zh: 而旧势力意识到这家伙也讨厌罗斯福。

sentences.en: And the old guard realizes this guy also hates Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 他也认为底层阶级应该安分守己，而上层阶级应该享受特殊待遇。

sentences.en: He also thinks the lower classes need to stay in their place and the upper classes need to get special stuff.
sentences.zh: 但是——这简直是州政治史上最伟大的礼物，你会这么想。

sentences.en: But – and this is the greatest gift in the history of state politics, you would think.
sentences.zh: 他是一个反动的保守派，而投票的公众却认为他是激进的自由派。

sentences.en: He is a reactionary conservative who the voting public believes is a radical liberal.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 他花了这么多年把自己塑造成一股自由派力量。

sentences.en: He spent all these years building himself up as this liberal force.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他并不是。

sentences.en: But in reality, he's not.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，这太棒了。

sentences.en: And they're like, this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 摩西接受了提名，媒体完全被蒙蔽了。

sentences.en: And Moses accepts the nomination and the press is fully taken in.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这是一个令人惊讶的转折。

sentences.en: They say, this is a surprising turn of events.
sentences.zh: 旧势力的自由派敌人现在成了他们的候选人，哈？

sentences.en: It's the liberal enemy of the old guard is now their candidate, huh?
sentences.zh: 这本该进行得非常完美。

sentences.en: It should have worked beautifully.
sentences.zh: 但有一个大问题。

sentences.en: There's only one big problem.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有两个大问题。

sentences.en: I mean, there's two big probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这是新政时期。

sentences.en: It's a New Deal year.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大萧条还在持续。

sentences.en: You know, the depression is still going on.
sentences.zh: 但最大的问题是，罗伯特·摩西可能是美国历史上最糟糕的政治竞选人。

sentences.en: But the big problem is that Robert Moses is maybe the worst political campaigner in American history.
sentences.zh: 他太不擅长这个了。

sentences.en: He's so bad at it.
sentences.zh: 这是旧式的竞选，竞选期只有五周。

sentences.en: And this is old-style campaigning where the campaign is only five weeks long.
sentences.zh: 所以你没有那种漫长的积累期，不像我们现在这样可以花钱压倒对手，谢天谢地。

sentences.en: So you don't have this long buildup where you can outspend your opponent like we have now, thankfully.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，我们现在已经到了只有富人才能参选的地步，因为你需要这么多钱才能做到。

sentences.en: Thankfully, we've gotten to the point where only rich people can run because you need so much money to do it.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们远离了那个竞选只有五周然后你就必须做决定的时代。

sentences.en: I'm so glad we're away from this time when the campaign was only five weeks and then you just made a decision.
sentences.zh: 他把那五周时间全花在激怒所有人上了，从他自己的支持者开始。

sentences.en: And he spends all those five weeks antagonizing everybody, starting with his own supporters.
sentences.zh: 卡罗谈到他去向一群对他充满热情的年轻共和党人发表演讲。

sentences.en: And Kara talks about how he goes to speak to an audience of young Republicans who are enthusiastic about him.
sentences.zh: 结果不知怎么的，演变成了摩西和他的支持者之间的对骂，他们互相辱骂。

sentences.en: And it somehow turns into a shouting match between Moses and his base where they're calling each other names.
sentences.zh: 而且他是在和他的老板雷曼州长竞选。

sentences.en: And he's running against his boss, Governor Lehman.
sentences.zh: 所以他认为的同事们，大多是民主党人。

sentences.en: So the people he considers colleagues, they're mostly Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他们忠于州长。

sentences.en: They're loyal to the governor.
sentences.zh: 他们不会支持他，但他还是期待他们的支持，当他们不这么做时，他会很生气。

sentences.en: They will not support him, but he expects their support anyway, and he gets mad when they don't do it.
sentences.zh: 卡罗谈到亨利·莫斯科维茨，他说，我支持雷曼州长。

sentences.en: And Kara talks about how Henry Moskowitz, he goes, I'm supporting Governor Lehman.
sentences.zh: 摩西从此再也没和他说过话，甚至没参加他的葬礼，这可是件大事。

sentences.en: And Moses never talks to him again and doesn't even attend his funeral, which is pretty big.
sentences.zh: 就像媒体一样，他们曾经很爱摩西。

sentences.en: Like the press, they used to love Moses.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: We know that, right?
sentences.zh: 媒体总是谈论摩西有多伟大。

sentences.en: The press is always talking about how great Moses is in.
sentences.zh: 他出现在报纸上的频率比阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦还高。

sentences.en: He's in the paper more often than Albert Einstein.
sentences.zh: 他出现在报纸上的频率比 J·埃德加·胡佛还高。

sentences.en: He's in the paper more often than J.
sentences.zh: 他们爱他。

sentences.en: Edgar Hoover.
sentences.zh: 但就在他作为候选人召开的第一次新闻发布会上，第一个问题就是他是否是旧势力的门徒。

sentences.en: They love him.
sentences.zh: 摩西对他们发表了一通愤怒的演讲，说你们工作做得不对。

sentences.en: But literally after the first question in the first press conference he gives as a candidate, the question is whether he is a protege of the old guard.
sentences.zh: 你们需要问正确的问题。

sentences.en: Moses gives them an angry speech about you're not doing your job right.
sentences.zh: 你们需要说正确的话。

sentences.en: You need to ask the right questions.
sentences.zh: 这就像是《布鲁斯特的百万横财》那种孤注一掷的策略，就像是，哦，如果我没有选票，也许我能瞬间成为州长。

sentences.en: You need to say the right things.
sentences.zh: 这简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: And it's like a Brewster's Millions type shoot the moon strategy where it's like, oh, if I have no votes, maybe I'll instantly become governor.
sentences.zh: 摩西，他把一切都搞砸了。

sentences.en: It's just astounding.
sentences.zh: 他向媒体宣布。

sentences.en: Moses, he does everything wrong.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚会给我背书。

sentences.en: He announces to the press.
sentences.zh: 我要召开新闻发布会。

sentences.en: LaGuardia is going to give me his endorsement.
sentences.zh: 但他根本没费心先去和拉瓜迪亚确认。

sentences.en: I'm calling a press conference.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚很生气，他退出了竞选。

sentences.en: But he didn't bother to check with LaGuardia firSt.
sentences.zh: 摩西，他拒绝为争取少数族裔选票而竞选，而在纽约地区你必须这么做。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia is pissed off, and he stays out of the campaign.
sentences.zh: 纽约市特别棒的一点是，那里有来自世界各地的人，

sentences.en: Moses, he won't campaign for ethnic votes, which you have to do in the New York area.
sentences.zh: 他们希望你去参加他们的街头集市，品尝他们的当地美食。

sentences.en: One of the great things about New York City especially is there's people from every part of the world there,
sentences.zh: 而他拒绝这样做。

sentences.en: and they want you to go to their street fairs and eat their local foods.
sentences.zh: 他甚至不愿走出大城市。

sentences.en: And he reviews us to do that.
sentences.zh: 他整个公开露面策略就是 12 场正式演讲。

sentences.en: He won't even go outside of large cities.
sentences.zh: 卡罗引用了保罗·温德尔斯的话，他曾是纽约市公司法律顾问，

sentences.en: His entire public appearance strategy is 12 formal speeches.
sentences.zh: 这是一个——我不太清楚这个职位在纽约市等级制度中具体如何定位，但它非常——它很有权势且有影响力。

sentences.en: And Caro quotes Paul Wendels, who was the New York City Corporation Counsel,
sentences.zh: 他是一个在城市里处理事务的律师。

sentences.en: which is one of those – it's a job that I don't know exactly how it fits into the New York City hierarchy, but it's very – it's powerful and influential.
sentences.zh: 他告诉卡罗，他每次开口，就会失去 10,000 张选票。

sentences.en: He's a lawyer who does stuff in the city.
sentences.zh: 而且那些本该属于他的选票，他本应获得犹太人的选票。

sentences.en: He says to Caro, every time he opened his mouth, he lost 10,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，雷曼也是犹太人。

sentences.en: And votes that should have been his, he should get the Jewish vote.
sentences.zh: 但摩西——也许他们会瓜分犹太选票。

sentences.en: I mean, Laman is Jewish also.
sentences.zh: 他们都是犹太人。

sentences.en: But Moses – maybe they'll split the Jewish vote.
sentences.zh: 但摩西，他公开说，我不是犹太人。

sentences.en: They're both Jewish.
sentences.zh: 他没有受过割礼。

sentences.en: But Moses, he says publicly, I'm not Jewish.
sentences.zh: 他没有被割礼。

sentences.en: He hasn't been far misfed.
sentences.zh: 卡罗有一个关于这方面拉比观点的脚注，即这些事情是否是认定为犹太人的必要条件，

sentences.en: He hasn't been circumcised.
sentences.zh: 这可是——这是书中，在这本非常“纽约”的书里，最“犹太”的一个时刻。

sentences.en: And Caro has a footnote about the rabbinical aspects of this, whether those things are necessary to be considered Jewish or not,
sentences.zh: 这简直太不可思议了。

sentences.en: which is a – which is one of – which is the most Jewish moment in the book, in this very New York book.
sentences.zh: 这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It's that little footnote.
sentences.zh: 那只是个小注脚。

sentences.en: But he refuses to be considered Jewish or called Jewish, and this is at a time when New York Jews find it especially important to reaffirm their being Jewish.
sentences.zh: 但他拒绝被视为犹太人或被称为犹太人，而当时纽约的犹太人正觉得重申自己的犹太身份尤为重要。

sentences.en: This is the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪30年代。

sentences.en: This is maybe the most dangerous time for Jews in the world in centuries.
sentences.zh: 那或许是几个世纪以来全球犹太人最危险的时期。

sentences.en: And so for Moses to be denying that, they take that as a personal affront.
sentences.zh: 因此，摩西对此的否认被他们视为一种人身侮辱。

sentences.en: And so Moses is like, the only one route to becoming governor because I am so unliked and so unlikable.
sentences.zh: 所以摩西觉得，因为我太不受欢迎、太讨人厌，竞选州长的唯一途径就是……

sentences.en: I have to destroy the public image of Governor Herbert H.
sentences.zh: 我必须摧毁赫伯特·H·雷曼州长的公众形象。

sentences.en: Laman, who at this point is famous for both being a New Deal liberal and for his impeccable principles.
sentences.zh: 雷曼当时以新政自由派和无可挑剔的原则而闻名。

sentences.en: He is famous for his honesty.
sentences.zh: 他以诚实著称。

sentences.en: He's famous for how much he hews to the rules.
sentences.zh: 他以恪守规则而闻名。

sentences.en: And Moses launches just attack after attack that are clearly false.
sentences.zh: 于是摩西发起了一轮又一轮显然是虚假的攻击。

sentences.en: Like Laman is well-known as a reformer, and Moses is like, this Tammany puppet, he's stupid.
sentences.zh: 比如雷曼是著名的改革者，而摩西却说他是坦慕尼协会的傀儡，是个蠢货。

sentences.en: He is weak.
sentences.zh: 他很软弱。

sentences.en: He's bowing down to the Tammany bosses because he's afraid they're going to beat him up.
sentences.zh: 他向坦慕尼协会的头目低头，因为他怕被他们揍。

sentences.en: Like literally, he's physically afraid that they're going to beat him up.
sentences.zh: 字面意思，他从身体上害怕他们会揍他。

sentences.en: It is – it's bonkers.
sentences.zh: 这简直……简直是疯了。

sentences.en: And after the campaign, Carol is like, later on, Moses would say Laman was a distinguished governor, a fine character.
sentences.zh: 竞选结束后，卡罗说，后来摩西会称雷曼是一位杰出的州长，品格高尚。

sentences.en: Like Moses knows this is not true.
sentences.zh: 摩西明明知道这不是真的。

sentences.en: And Laman does the smart thing, which is he just ignores Moses, and he campaigns everywhere and campaigns on his own record.
sentences.zh: 而雷曼做了明智之举，他直接无视摩西，到处奔走竞选，并以自己的政绩作为竞选纲领。

sentences.en: And it's like this is how we want politics to work to a certain extent, which is that the guy who has a good record and his putting his all into it is doing well,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这正是我们希望政治运作的方式，即那个政绩良好且全力以赴的人表现出色，

sentences.en: and the guy who is a big liar who is just mean is doing poorly.
sentences.zh: 而那个只会撒谎且卑劣的人表现糟糕。

sentences.en: And he makes a lot of these baseless attacks.
sentences.zh: 他进行了许多毫无根据的攻击。

sentences.en: One example that he gives – this carries one of the examples I want to highlight.
sentences.zh: 他给出的一个例子——这引出了我想强调的其中一个例子。

sentences.en: He says, he accused Laman of being responsible for corruption in the court of claims,
sentences.zh: 他说，他指责雷曼应对索赔法院的腐败负责，

sentences.en: an accusation which ignored the fact that the court was not under the governor's control and which was not strengthened by the fact that to document the court's incompetence,
sentences.zh: 这一指控忽略了法院并不受州长控制的事实，而且为了证明法院的无能，

sentences.en: Moses accused of drunkenness a judge who actually had been dead for more than a year.
sentences.zh: 摩西指控一位实际上已经去世一年多的法官酗酒，这并没有让他的指控更有说服力。

sentences.en: So like Moses is just going – he's just throwing out wild things.
sentences.zh: 所以摩西简直是在……他简直是在胡言乱语。

sentences.en: He accuses Laman of being in bed with the utility companies, which is exactly what Moses is doing at this point.
sentences.zh: 他指责雷曼与公用事业公司勾结，而这正是摩西当时正在做的事情。

sentences.en: And finally, Moses goes a step too far, and he calls Laman a liar, which shocks people.
sentences.zh: 最后，摩西做得太过火了，他称雷曼为骗子，这震惊了所有人。

sentences.en: It's hard to overstate how strong Carroll makes the reaction to this charge or describes it where that's when he starts losing support.
sentences.zh: 很难夸大卡罗对这一指控的反应描述得有多强烈，那是他开始失去支持的时候。

sentences.en: Other Republicans say he's unfit for office,
sentences.zh: 其他共和党人说他不适合担任公职，

sentences.en: and there's a radio station service that says we will not run Moses' speeches unless the party takes out libel insurance that covers every time he speaks.
sentences.zh: 还有一家广播电台表示，除非政党购买涵盖他每次发言的诽谤保险，否则我们不会播放摩西的演讲。

sentences.en: And it all – I hate to look at the past with rose-colored glasses because there was a lot of bad stuff going on,
sentences.zh: 这一切——我不喜欢戴着玫瑰色眼镜看过去，因为当时发生了很多糟糕的事情，

sentences.en: and the political system was far from fully equitable or good or non-corrupt.
sentences.zh: 政治体制也远非完全公平、良好或廉洁。

sentences.en: But this whole section, it's just so hard to read it now and not be like, oh, things have really changed, huh?
sentences.zh: 但读到这一整段时，很难不感叹，哦，情况真的变了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what's interesting here to me is that even though Moses was a sort of lifelong Republican except for the time when he changed his party affiliation.
sentences.zh: 这里让我感兴趣的是，尽管摩西除了改变党籍的那段时间外，一直是个共和党人。

sentences.en: Briefly when he thought it would help him become governor.
sentences.zh: 在他短暂地认为这有助于他成为州长时。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the earlier time.
sentences.zh: 在早期的时候。

sentences.en: When Al Smith was running for president.
sentences.zh: 当阿尔·史密斯竞选总统时。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting because he has surrounded himself with Democrats.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，因为他身边都是民主党人。

sentences.en: He's always worked with Democrats up to this point.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他一直与民主党人合作。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, his mentor and big brother in all this is Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，他在这一切中的导师和老大哥是阿尔·史密斯。

sentences.en: You know, it's only recently in LaGuardia that he has worked with a Republican pretty much at all.
sentences.zh: 你知道，直到最近在拉瓜迪亚手下，他才算真正与共和党人共事过。

sentences.en: And everyone turns their back on him.
sentences.zh: 而每个人都背弃了他。

sentences.en: I mean they don't try to be mean about it, but they're just like, listen, you know, I'm a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们并不是想刻薄，他们只是说，听着，你知道，我是民主党人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Even when he goes to Al Smith, he goes to Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 即使他去找阿尔·史密斯，他去找阿尔·史密斯。

sentences.en: He will ask for support.
sentences.zh: 他会寻求支持。

sentences.en: And Al Smith says, I play this game like a regular.
sentences.zh: 而阿尔·史密斯说，我像个正规党员一样玩这场游戏。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Moses is stung by it.
sentences.zh: 摩西为此感到刺痛。

sentences.en: And Caro describes how someone tells him about Moses recalling this 30 years later and it's still clearly hurting him.
sentences.zh: 卡罗描述了有人告诉他摩西在30年后回忆起这件事时，显然仍然感到受伤。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的。

sentences.en: He's surrounded by – he's always called himself an independent Republican, but he has been a fixture in Democratic administrations and working with Democratic officials.
sentences.zh: 他被包围着——他一直称自己为独立共和党人，但他一直是民主党政府中的常客，并与民主党官员共事。

sentences.en: And it is foolish of him, this guy who understands the political mechanism so well, to expect that they like him so much personally,
sentences.zh: 对于这个非常了解政治机制的人来说，期望他们个人如此喜欢他，以至于他们会背弃自己的政党，而且老实说，在这种情况下，背弃他们一直坚持的原则，这真是愚蠢。

sentences.en: that they will turn their back on this party and also, to be honest, in this case, principles that they've stood by for all this time.
sentences.zh: 而且老实说，在这种情况下，背弃他们一直坚持的原则，这真是愚蠢。

sentences.en: And I wonder if this – I hadn't thought about this until just now, Roman.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否——罗曼，直到刚才我才想到这一点。

sentences.en: You've led me to this realization that one of the themes throughout the first parts of the book is Robert Moses finding sources of power that other people had discounted earlier or not noticed because they were outside of the official sources of power.
sentences.zh: 你引导我意识到，贯穿本书前几部分的主题之一是罗伯特·摩西找到了其他人早先忽视或未曾注意到的权力来源，因为它们处于官方权力来源之外。

sentences.en: And I wonder if here is one of those cases where he makes that gamble.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否就是他进行那场赌博的案例之一。

sentences.en: He says the Democratic Party is more powerful in this region than the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 他说民主党在这个地区比共和党更有权势。

sentences.en: I'm going to be able to go in there and turn that into my source of power then.
sentences.zh: 那么我将能够进入那里并将其转化为我的权力来源。

sentences.en: And that gamble doesn't pay off this time.
sentences.zh: 而那次赌博这次没有成功。

sentences.en: He's not able to do it.
sentences.zh: 他没能做到。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I also think that he – like you said, that is his superpower.
sentences.zh: 我也认为他——就像你说的，那是他的超能力。

sentences.en: It's like turning sort of ignored and positions that are not thought of as very powerful into powerful positions.
sentences.zh: 就像把那些被忽视的、不被认为非常有权力的职位变成有权力的职位。

sentences.en: Whereas running for governor is like good old-fashioned normal stuff.
sentences.zh: 而竞选州长就像是老派的正常事务。

sentences.en: Like he's not going to reinvent anything here.
sentences.zh: 他在这里不会重塑任何东西。

sentences.en: He's not going to find some law that he can write to make this better for him or easier for him.
sentences.zh: 他不会找到什么法律来让他变得更好或更容易。

sentences.en: He has to do all the things.
sentences.zh: 他必须做所有该做的事。

sentences.en: This stuff has been worked out.
sentences.zh: 这些事情都已经定型了。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: He's not going to get around it.
sentences.zh: 他无法绕过它。

sentences.en: And his unwillingness to play ball in the way that everyone else does to create a successful campaign is just – you know, he's just naive.
sentences.zh: 他不愿意像其他人那样按部就班地进行成功的竞选，这只是——你知道，他太天真了。

sentences.en: Like he's never walked a path that other people have, you know, walked ahead of him.
sentences.zh: 他从未走过别人走过的路。

sentences.en: He's only sort of forged his own way through all these like new ways of looking at the government and the world and municipal structures.
sentences.zh: 他只是通过所有这些看待政府、世界和市政结构的新方式开辟了自己的道路。

sentences.en: And this tried-and-true way, he's just bad at it.
sentences.zh: 而这种行之有效的方法，他却很不擅长。

sentences.en: There's something about – and maybe it's one of the – maybe it's from the beautiful things about electoral politics is that it can really humble people who are used to not being humble because suddenly they need the people who they don't care about to give them their approval.
sentences.zh: 这其中有些东西——也许这是选举政治的美妙之处之一，它可以真正让那些不习惯谦卑的人变得谦卑，因为突然间他们需要那些他们不在乎的人给予认可。

sentences.en: They need the approval of the people that previously they saw as beneath them.
sentences.zh: 他们需要那些以前被他们视为低人一等的人的认可。

sentences.en: And, I mean, that's – it goes back to the – in some ways to the original founding of the country where it was like, you know, this king's used to telling us what to do.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，这在某种程度上回到了国家的最初建立，当时就像是，你知道，国王习惯于告诉我们该做什么。

sentences.en: Well, what if we chose the king?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们选择国王会怎样？

sentences.en: And he had to pay attention to us once every four years.
sentences.zh: 他必须每四年关注我们一次。

sentences.en: You know, it's a real guardrail of democracy that Moses is coming up againSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是摩西所面临的民主的真正护栏。

sentences.en: Moses, to his credit, he does not hold a grudge against Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 值得称赞的是，摩西并没有对阿尔·史密斯怀恨在心。

sentences.en: This is before Moses opens the Central Park Zoo, which is basically his love present to Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 这发生在摩西开放中央公园动物园之前，这基本上是他给阿尔·史密斯的爱之礼物。

sentences.en: So that's the one relationship that he'll never let go of.
sentences.zh: 所以那是他永远不会放下的关系。

sentences.en: It's pretty interesting that this is happening simultaneously to that chapter that we read earlier about that ceremony and giving him the key and all that sort of stuff that meant so much to Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 很有趣的是，这与我们之前读到的关于那个仪式、给他钥匙以及所有那些对阿尔·史密斯意义重大的事情的章节同时发生。

sentences.en: It does, however, make me think that him missing that ceremony, there might be something a little bit more to that, you know, because he wasn't there for that.
sentences.zh: 然而，这确实让我觉得，他错过那个仪式可能还有点别的原因，你知道，因为他当时不在场。

sentences.en: And he says it's because he's sick.
sentences.zh: 他说是因为他病了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Guardrails of democracy.
sentences.zh: 民主的护栏。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: like so like Robert Moses just goes headfirst into a guardrail of democracy and he just he he ends up with the smallest percentage of the vote of any major party candidate in the history of New York State up until that point.
sentences.zh: 就像罗伯特·摩西一头撞上了民主的护栏，他最终获得了纽约州历史上任何主要政党候选人中最低的得票率。

sentences.en: Up until that point.
sentences.zh: 在那之前。

sentences.en: Since then, some enterprising candidates have beaten that record and gotten less.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，一些进取的候选人打破了那个记录，获得了更低的票数。

sentences.en: But Moses, he ends up with 35 percent of the vote, which in a two party competition is pretty abysmal.
sentences.zh: 但摩西最终只获得了35%的选票，在两党竞争中这相当惨淡。

sentences.en: And the GOP, they lose both houses of the legislature for the first time in 21 years.
sentences.zh: 共和党21年来首次失去了立法机构的两院控制权。

sentences.en: He even loses in the in the what are usually a solidly Republican upstate districts.
sentences.zh: 他甚至在通常是共和党铁票仓的北部地区也输了。

sentences.en: Those go for Lehman.
sentences.zh: 那些票投给了雷曼。

sentences.en: And Moses, of course, takes no responsibility.
sentences.zh: 当然，摩西不承担任何责任。

sentences.en: He's like, it was 1934.
sentences.zh: 他说，那是1934年。

sentences.en: The New Deal candidate was always going to win.
sentences.zh: 新政候选人注定会赢。

sentences.en: I couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 我无能为力。

sentences.en: But the political insiders are like, yeah, but election could have been closer.
sentences.zh: 但政治内部人士说，是啊，但选举本可以更接近一些。

sentences.en: And it's interesting that either Moses doesn't care or forgets or doesn't think about it that when you have an election year, the person at the head of the ticket,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，摩西要么不在乎，要么忘记了，要么没考虑到，当你在选举年时，领衔候选人的工作之一就是为名单上排名靠后的人争取支持。

sentences.en: part of their job is to draw support for the people lower down on the ticket.
sentences.zh: 所以即使他表现得更好，即使他输了，也许他的政党本可以保持对部分立法机构的控制，或者至少不会失去那么多席位。

sentences.en: So even if he had run better, even if he had lost, perhaps his party would have kept control of part of legislature or just wouldn't have lost so many seats.
sentences.zh: 但我也肯定摩西不在乎。

sentences.en: But Moses also, I'm sure, doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 他不在乎政党如何。

sentences.en: Like he doesn't care about how the rest of the parties.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他不在乎政党。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't care about the party.
sentences.zh: 并不是说从这一点开始，他就真正参与了共和党的政治。

sentences.en: It's not like from this point on, he's really involved in GOP politics.
sentences.zh: 当他输了，他就抛弃了他们，你知道。

sentences.en: Like when he loses, he he drops them, you know.
sentences.zh: 这是一个时刻，你知道，雷曼值得称赞的是，我认为在政治上摆脱摩西是合理的，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: And this is a moment where, you know, Lehman, to his credit, you know, like it would be, I think, politically reasonable to get rid of Moses at this moment because, you know,
sentences.zh: 他刚刚在竞争同一个职位，并称他为骗子，还做了所有这些令人讨厌的事情。

sentences.en: he just was, you know, in a competition for the same job and called him a liar and all these nasty things.
sentences.zh: 冒犯了该州的大多数人，只是让大多数人不喜欢他。

sentences.en: Offended most of the state, just made most of the state not like him.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，值得称赞的是，雷曼没有这样做。

sentences.en: But, you know, to his credit, Lehman doesn't do it.
sentences.zh: 他留用了他。

sentences.en: He keeps him on.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 他说这家伙工作很出色。

sentences.en: He says this guy's great at his job.
sentences.zh: 他正在做别人做不到的工作。

sentences.en: He's doing work nobody else can do.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为他叫我骗子并不意味着我应该解雇他。

sentences.en: Just because he called me a liar doesn't mean I should fire him.
sentences.zh: 这是那种有人做原则性事情，表面上做正确事情的时刻之一。

sentences.en: It is one of those moments where someone does the principled thing and does ostensibly the right thing.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，你会想，哦，天哪，你知道，这本该是那个时刻。

sentences.en: But in the long run, you're like, oh, man, you know, this would have been the moment.
sentences.zh: 我知道这本该是那个时刻。

sentences.en: I know this would have been the moment.
sentences.zh: 一线希望是，如果他解雇了摩西，

sentences.en: The silver lining is that if he had fired Moses,
sentences.zh: 那么罗伯特·卡罗就不可能写出我们现在如此享受的这本精彩的书，因为那个曾短暂成为最有权势的人的故事。

sentences.en: then there's no way Robert Carroll ever would have written this wonderful book that we're enjoying so much because the story of the man who was briefly the most powerful person.
sentences.zh: 作为公园专员在纽约，这不像那个做了多年的人的故事那样是一本好书。

sentences.en: In New York as Parks Commissioner is not as let's say not as much of a book as the guy who did it for for years and years.
sentences.zh: 卡罗在这里做了一些分析，他说，为什么摩西在这件事上做得这么糟糕？

sentences.en: And Carroll goes into he does a little bit of analysis here where he's saying, why did Moses do such a bad job with this?
sentences.zh: 就像这个通常很擅长利用媒体，很擅长展示自己并将自己定位在问题正确一边的人。

sentences.en: Like this guy who is usually so good at using the press, who is so good at presenting himself and at positioning himself on the right side of issues.
sentences.zh: 卡罗的理论是，部分原因是摩西很幸运，在此之前总是有热门议题。

sentences.en: And what Carroll says is his theory is that part of it is because Moses was kind of lucky to always have a popular issue before now.
sentences.zh: 他与公园建设挂钩。

sentences.en: He was tied to park building.
sentences.zh: 人们不必喜欢他这个人。

sentences.en: People didn't have to like him as a person.
sentences.zh: 他们只需要喜欢他支持公园建设这一事实。

sentences.en: They just had to like the fact that he was for parks.
sentences.zh: 但在政治竞选中，他不能说我是公园先生。

sentences.en: But in a political campaign, he can't say I'm the parks guy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他本可以。

sentences.en: I mean he could have.
sentences.zh: 如果他是一个更好的竞选者，他本可以说我是公园先生，但他的真实性格必须显露出来，而人们并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: If he was a better campaigner, he could have said I'm the parks guy, but his actual character had to come out and people did not like it.
sentences.zh: 卡罗说，为什么他不能像吸引他所需要的支持的权贵那样吸引选民，比如共和党人，或者正如我们稍后将看到的，报纸？

sentences.en: And Carroll says, why couldn't he charm the voters the way he charmed the powerful people whose support he needed, the people in the GOP party or as we'll see later in newspapers?
sentences.zh: 卡罗推测——这就是他变得有点心理分析的地方，我不确定我是否完全买账。

sentences.en: And Carroll theorizes that – this is where he gets a little psychoanalytical in a way that I'm not sure I fully buy into.
sentences.zh: 但他认为摩西太傲慢、太自以为是，以至于他真的无法假装关心别人的想法，而且他实际上从能够表达对别人的蔑视中获得了快感。

sentences.en: But he says that Moses is so arrogant and so entitled that he literally is incapable of pretending to care about what other people think and that he actually derives pleasure from being able to express the contempt that he holds other people in.
sentences.zh: 所以他需要展示他的优越感，他需要摧毁任何反对他的人。

sentences.en: And so he needs to display his superiority, and he needs to destroy anyone who opposes him.
sentences.zh: 这就是卡罗的观点——我想不出摩西为什么要对抗媒体，他本来很擅长操纵媒体，

sentences.en: And that's Carroll's like – I can't think of another reason why Moses would antagonize the press, who he was so good at manipulating,
sentences.zh: 但现在他觉得他需要展示他更好、更聪明，他不能仅仅击败他的敌人。

sentences.en: but now he felt like he needed to show he was better and smarter, and he can't just defeat his enemies.
sentences.zh: 他必须摧毁他们。

sentences.en: He has to destroy them.
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: And what do you think?
sentences.zh: 我不确定是那样，还是因为摩西真的很擅长讨好那些他觉得需要从中得到什么的人。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if it's that or if it's that just – Moses is just really good at fawning over people who he feels he needs something from.
sentences.zh: 尽管他知道他需要选民，但他把他们视为一个群体，他认为个别选民是无名小卒，

sentences.en: And as much as he knows he needs the voters, he thinks of them as a mass, and he thinks of individual voters as nobodies,
sentences.zh: 他觉得没有必要讨好他们，因为他们个人是无能为力的。

sentences.en: and he doesn't feel the need to fawn over them because individually they're powerless.
sentences.zh: 他觉得没有必要讨好他们，因为他们个人是无能为力的。

sentences.en: That's my theory.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的理论。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: I mean I think it could be both of those things.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得这两者都有可能。

sentences.en: I think that he –
sentences.zh: 我觉得他——

sentences.en: Got to pick one.
sentences.zh: 必须选一个。

sentences.en: Got to pick one, Roman.
sentences.zh: 必须选一个，罗曼。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I'll let you forge the middle path.
sentences.zh: 我让你来开辟中间道路。

sentences.en: That's fine, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那很好，没错。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's also just that, you know, Robert Moses is really great at creating the conditions where he is doing everything for the first time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得还有一点，你知道，罗伯特·摩西真的很擅长创造条件，让他所做的一切都成为前所未有的创举。

sentences.en: All of his whipsawing and his sort of lying and then, you know, stake driving and all his stuff,
sentences.zh: 他所有的那种左右摇摆、那种撒谎，还有，你知道，那种强行推进以及他那一套做法，

sentences.en: it just is about – he is the best because there's no one – there's no precedent for him.
sentences.zh: 关键就在于——他是最棒的，因为没有人——他没有先例可循。

sentences.en: You know, like, and this just is not an unprecedented job to be a politician in this way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像，以这种方式成为一名政客，这并不是一份没有先例的工作。

sentences.en: And he is finding that he cannot, like, bend his character to do any of these things.
sentences.zh: 而他发现自己无法，比如，为了做这些事而扭曲自己的性格。

sentences.en: Like, it just is anathema to his existence.
sentences.zh: 这对他来说简直是深恶痛绝的。

sentences.en: And he's never had to because he's always done things his own way.
sentences.zh: 而且他从来不需要这样做，因为他总是按自己的方式行事。

sentences.en: And this is just, like – I just think he's incapable of it.
sentences.zh: 这只是，就像——我只是觉得他做不到。

sentences.en: And when you're in the confidence of someone and they say something mean, you feel very warm to them sometimes because you're like, oh,
sentences.zh: 当你得到某人的信任，而他们说了些刻薄的话时，你有时会觉得和他们很亲近，因为你会想，噢，

sentences.en: they're being mean to that person and they like me.
sentences.zh: 他们对那个人很刻薄，但他们喜欢我。

sentences.en: You know, like –
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像——

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think he plays on that in a small room or with just a group of people, you know, a small group of people that he shares, you know, a kinship with.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他在一个小房间里，或者只和一群人在一起时，就会利用这一点，你知道，和他有某种亲缘关系的一小群人。

sentences.en: But the bigger and bigger that room is, then you're just, like, shouting at people and it is not fun at all, you know, to watch someone just be mean to someone in a large room.
sentences.zh: 但房间越大，你就越像是在对人咆哮，而且，你知道，看着一个人在大会场里对别人刻薄，一点也不好玩。

sentences.en: And I think that he – I think he just sort of traffics in a kind of gossip and chumminess and, you know, like – and being nice to you and mean to you in, like,
sentences.zh: 我觉得他——我觉得他只是在兜售某种八卦和亲昵，你知道，就像——对你很好，又对你很刻薄，以一种，

sentences.en: unpredictable ways so that his sort of abuses and control over you is strengthened by that.
sentences.zh: 不可预测的方式，这样他那种对你的虐待和控制就得到了加强。

sentences.en: And you just can't do that in a broad scale to people, like to a mass of people.
sentences.zh: 你不能在大范围内对人这样做，比如对大众。

sentences.en: I guess it goes to show, too, that, like, there's certain types of people whose personalities react to other personalities.
sentences.zh: 我想这也表明，确实有某些类型的人，他们的性格会对其他性格产生反应。

sentences.en: And Moses, for some reason in public and on a large scale, had the kind of personality that nobody reacted well to, that it just didn't mesh with anybody.
sentences.zh: 而摩西，出于某种原因，在公开场合和大范围内，他的性格没人能很好地应对，就是和谁都合不来。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: Like, except for when he could put up a ceremony, like, somewhat.
sentences.zh: 就像，除了他能举办某种仪式的时候，稍微好一点。

sentences.en: But that's it.
sentences.zh: 但仅此而已。

sentences.en: Like, he kind of knew the details of how to make people have a good time when he was opening something or doing something grand.
sentences.zh: 就像，他很清楚如何让人们在开幕式或举办盛大活动时玩得开心。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But when he spoke, it was, you know, pretty uninspiring.
sentences.zh: 但当他讲话时，你知道，相当乏味。

sentences.en: You know, like, it's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的很迷人。

sentences.en: That's not what his strength was.
sentences.zh: 那不是他的强项。

sentences.en: And so, at this point, you know, he's kind of at his lowest that we've seen him since, you know, his initial ascendancy.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这一点上，你知道，他处于我们自他最初崛起以来所见过的最低谷。

sentences.en: This is the lowest he's been since he was a 30-year-old guy who could not get a job in government.
sentences.zh: 这是他自30岁那年无法在政府找到工作以来的最低谷。

sentences.en: He is now – he has – I mean, he has two amazing jobs.
sentences.zh: 他现在——他有——我是说，他有两份了不起的工作。

sentences.en: But, I mean, he actually has, like, 11 amazing jobs.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，他实际上有11份了不起的工作。

sentences.en: But he is – but people don't like him.
sentences.zh: 但他——但人们不喜欢他。

sentences.en: The shine is off the star.
sentences.zh: 明星的光环褪去了。

sentences.en: The bloom is off the rose.
sentences.zh: 玫瑰的花期过了。

sentences.en: You know, his halo is hanging by a thread.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他的光环岌岌可危。

sentences.en: I don't know how many different messed-up metaphors.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有多少种乱七八糟的隐喻。

sentences.en: Unfortunately for us, unfortunately for him,
sentences.zh: 对我们来说不幸的是，对他来说不幸的是，

sentences.en: a strange savior is about to enter the scene as we roll into chapter 22 as Moses' oldest foe is about to become his inadvertent support beam.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入第22章时，一位奇怪的救星即将登场，因为摩西最古老的敌人即将成为他无意中的支撑梁。

sentences.en: I couldn't come up with the right metaphor for that either.
sentences.zh: 我也没能为那个找到合适的隐喻。

sentences.en: We'll do that one with chapter 22, order number 129, after this break.
sentences.zh: 我们会在休息后，在第22章，第129号令中讲那个。

sentences.en: This next chapter is chapter 22.
sentences.zh: 下一章是第22章。

sentences.en: It's called order number 129.
sentences.zh: 它叫第129号令。

sentences.en: And this is when Robert Moses is at his lowest, his old foe, Franklin Roosevelt, who's now the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗伯特·摩西处于最低谷的时候，他的老对手，富兰克林·罗斯福，现在是美国总统。

sentences.en: He decides that he's going to take his revenge on him.
sentences.zh: 他决定要对他进行报复。

sentences.en: And this is such a misfire.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一次严重的失误。

sentences.en: It's so colossal of a mistake.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的错误。

sentences.en: It's a Moses running for governor level of misfire from the president of the United States, and it has the exact opposite effect of what the president is hoping.
sentences.zh: 这是美国总统的一次失误，级别相当于摩西竞选州长，而且产生了与总统预期完全相反的效果。

sentences.en: Technically, this revenge happens – it starts before the gubernatorial campaign.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，这次报复发生在——它始于州长竞选之前。

sentences.en: In February of 1934, we have this scene where – Kara describes where LaGuardia is crying to Paul Wendell's New York City Corporation counsel.
sentences.zh: 1934年2月，我们有这样一个场景——卡罗描述了拉瓜迪亚向保罗·温德尔的纽约市公司法律顾问哭诉。

sentences.en: Again, don't know what the job is, but he's around a lot in this book.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，不知道那是什么工作，但他在书里经常出现。

sentences.en: He realizes that the guy he picked as his federal money guy, the city's interface between its needs and the federal government's largesse, is Robert Moses,
sentences.zh: 他意识到他选定的联邦资金负责人，即城市需求与联邦政府慷慨之间的接口，是罗伯特·摩西，

sentences.en: the one guy the president hates most in the world.
sentences.zh: 总统在世界上最讨厌的那个人。

sentences.en: And other than Hitler, I guess, but – and there's a quote that I love here, and I'm going to try it.
sentences.zh: 除了希特勒，我想，但是——这里有一句我喜欢的引语，我要试着说一下。

sentences.en: I want to do it in an accent, but I know I can't do justice, where Wendell says to Caro, I got in the car, and no sooner did I sit down than he cut loose.
sentences.zh: 我想用口音说，但我知道我无法还原，温德尔对卡罗说，我上了车，刚坐下他就爆发了。

sentences.en: Jesus Christ, of all the people in the city of New York, I had to pick the one man who Roosevelt won't stand for, and he won't give me any more money unless I get rid of him.
sentences.zh: 天哪，在纽约市的所有人中，我偏偏选了罗斯福无法容忍的那个人，如果我不除掉他，他就不会再给我钱了。

sentences.en: Jesus Christ, I had to pick the one that he hated.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我偏偏选了他最讨厌的那个人。

sentences.en: Jesus ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: He was shaking his fist in the air and shouting, Jesus ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 他挥舞着拳头大喊，天哪。

sentences.en: Jesus ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Seven million people in the city, and I had to pick the one Roosevelt can't stand.
sentences.zh: 城里有七百万人，我偏偏选了罗斯福无法忍受的那个人。

sentences.en: And I just – I love that.
sentences.zh: 我只是——我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: It's so amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: My favorite movie of all time is The Taking of Pelham 123, and LaGuardia sounds like the mayor in that movie at that moment where he's just like, oh,
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的电影是《地铁惊魂》，拉瓜迪亚在那一刻听起来就像电影里的市长，他就像，噢，

sentences.en: what did it like – just overcome with his troubles.
sentences.zh: 这就像——被他的麻烦事压垮了。

sentences.en: And so this is the case.
sentences.zh: 所以情况就是这样。

sentences.en: Interior Secretary Harold Ickes has made it clear to LaGuardia that until Moses is fired from the Tribal Authority Board, the Publix Works Administration,
sentences.zh: 内政部长哈罗德·伊克斯已经向拉瓜迪亚明确表示，除非摩西被部落管理局解雇，否则公共工程管理局，

sentences.en: which Harold Ickes oversees in the Interior Secretariat ship, in the Department of the Interior,
sentences.zh: 也就是哈罗德·伊克斯在内政部秘书处负责的那个部门，

sentences.en: it will give no money to New York City, no money until Moses is fired.
sentences.zh: 将不会给纽约市任何资金，直到摩西被解雇。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia is like, I can't legally fire Moses from Tribal.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚说，我在法律上无法解雇部落管理局的摩西。

sentences.en: I can't legally do it.
sentences.zh: 我在法律上做不到。

sentences.en: But maybe I can get him to resign by threatening to fire him as the parks commissioner, which I can do.
sentences.zh: 但也许我可以威胁要解雇他的公园专员职务来让他辞职，这个我能做到。

sentences.en: And Moses, of course, he knows there's only one tool that gets to what you want, which is a bigger resignation threat.
sentences.zh: 当然，摩西知道只有一种工具能达到你的目的，那就是更大的辞职威胁。

sentences.en: So he goes, yeah, I'll resign from Tribal.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，好吧，我会从部落管理局辞职。

sentences.en: I'll also resign from the park jobs, and then I'll tell everyone publicly that you made me resign because the federal government told you to.
sentences.zh: 我也会辞去公园的工作，然后我会公开告诉所有人，是你逼我辞职的，因为联邦政府让你这么做。

sentences.en: And Wendels tells LaGuardia, if that happens, everyone will see you as weak if publicly you're seen as bowing to federal pressure.
sentences.zh: 温德尔告诉拉瓜迪亚，如果那样，如果你公开表现出屈服于联邦压力，所有人都会认为你软弱。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia tries to stall, and Roosevelt's losing his patience.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚试图拖延，而罗斯福正在失去耐心。

sentences.en: And as soon as the governor's race is over, Roosevelt is like, nobody likes this guy anymore.
sentences.zh: 州长竞选一结束，罗斯福就说，没人再喜欢这家伙了。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 动手吧。

sentences.en: And they turn off the PWA money faucet until the day when Moses is cut loose.
sentences.zh: 他们关掉了公共工程管理局的资金水龙头，直到摩西被解雇的那一天。

sentences.en: And Caro, it's worth looking up on page 429, Caro goes through this ridiculously melodramatic description of the whole thing as a stage play and which parts everyone's playing.
sentences.zh: 卡罗，值得去查阅第429页，卡罗把整件事描述成一场荒谬的舞台剧，每个人都在扮演各自的角色。

sentences.en: And it is this metaphor that goes way too far, but it's so – I love it.
sentences.zh: 这个隐喻有点过头了，但是——我喜欢它。

sentences.en: It goes beautifully too far.
sentences.zh: 它美妙地过头了。

sentences.en: So it's too long to read here, but go open up your hymnals to page 429 and take a look at it.
sentences.zh: 所以这里读太长了，但去翻开你的赞美诗集第429页看看吧。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia is in a bind.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚陷入了困境。

sentences.en: He needs this money to improve the city.
sentences.zh: 他需要这笔钱来改善城市。

sentences.en: He has big plans for the city.
sentences.zh: 他对城市有宏伟的计划。

sentences.en: He wants to do the things that Moses is trying to get done, but he can't be seen as giving in to Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 他想做摩西试图完成的事情，但他不能表现出向罗斯福屈服。

sentences.en: And then on December 26, 1934, a date which will live on in bureaucracy, Icky's Issues PWA Administrative Order No.
sentences.zh: 然后在1934年12月26日，一个将在官僚史上永存的日子，伊克斯发布了公共工程管理局第129号行政令，

sentences.en: 129, the very order that gives this chapter its title, drafted in part by Roosevelt,
sentences.zh: 正是这个命令给了这一章标题，部分由罗斯福起草，

sentences.en: stating the PWA will give no money to an independent entity that has a project entirely in one city if the governing board of that entity has anyone on it who also holds public office in that city.
sentences.zh: 规定如果一个独立实体的管理委员会中有人在该市担任公职，那么公共工程管理局将不会向该实体提供资金，如果该实体的项目完全在一个城市内。

sentences.en: And it's so specifically worded.
sentences.zh: 措辞非常具体。

sentences.en: It's so clearly describing Moses' situation, but it happens to affect another guy too, Tenement House Commissioner Langdon W.
sentences.zh: 它非常清楚地描述了摩西的情况，但也碰巧影响了另一个人，廉租房专员兰登·W·波斯特。

sentences.en: PoSt.
sentences.zh: 波斯特。

sentences.en: And Icky's is like, confidentially, don't worry about him.
sentences.zh: 伊克斯说，私下里，别担心他。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: We don't care about him.
sentences.zh: 我们不在乎他。

sentences.en: And Post is on a – he's actually on a cruise at that moment, so he doesn't even know any of this is happening.
sentences.zh: 波斯特当时正在游轮上，所以他甚至不知道这一切正在发生。

sentences.en: They should have written in that, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们本应该写上，你知道，

sentences.en: like in addition to give no money to an independent entity that has a project entirely in one city if that governing board has an entity as anyone who holds public office in that city.
sentences.zh: 就像除了不给在一个城市内有项目的独立实体提供资金，如果该管理委员会中有任何在该市担任公职的人。

sentences.en: And your name rhymes with Paubert Poses, you know?
sentences.zh: 而且你的名字和“鲍伯特·摩西”押韵，你知道吗？

sentences.en: LaGuardia's like, my hands are tied.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚说，我束手无策。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: You and Charbert Shoses have to leave the government.
sentences.zh: 你和“查伯特·肖西”必须离开政府。

sentences.en: I apologize.
sentences.zh: 我道歉。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia does a foolish thing here, which is in order to show Moses, he has to give in.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚在这里做了一件愚蠢的事，为了向摩西展示，他不得不屈服。

sentences.en: He shows the order to Moses.
sentences.zh: 他把命令拿给摩西看。

sentences.en: And Moses is like, huh, interesting, interesting.
sentences.zh: 摩西说，嗯，有趣，有趣。

sentences.en: Press, can I leak something to you?
sentences.zh: 媒体，我可以向你们泄露点东西吗？

sentences.en: And he goes, I'm revealing this purely because the public deserves transparency.
sentences.zh: 他说，我揭露这一点纯粹是因为公众理应享有透明度。

sentences.en: And the press are unaware that Roosevelt and Moses have hated each other for years.
sentences.zh: 媒体并不知道罗斯福和摩西多年来一直互相憎恨。

sentences.en: This feud is common knowledge among the political types, but it's not public knowledge.
sentences.zh: 这种不和在政治圈内是常识，但不是公开的秘密。

sentences.en: And so the press portrays it as the president is trying to force a public servant out of his job purely because while he was running for governor, he criticized the New Deal.
sentences.zh: 所以媒体将其描绘成总统试图强迫一名公职人员离职，仅仅是因为他在竞选州长时批评了新政。

sentences.en: This is political partisan payback of the worst type.
sentences.zh: 这是最糟糕的政治党派报复。

sentences.en: And suddenly Ickes is being asked about whether Roosevelt knew about the order.
sentences.zh: 突然间，伊克斯被问及罗斯福是否知道这个命令。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia is on a train to D.C.
sentences.zh: 而拉瓜迪亚正在去华盛顿的火车上，

sentences.en: and doesn't know that Moses leaked it.
sentences.zh: 不知道摩西泄露了它。

sentences.en: And as soon as he gets off the train, he's mobbed by reporters.
sentences.zh: 他一下火车，就被记者围住了。

sentences.en: And I really love – there's something about how old world this all is where if you are traveling, you do not know what is happening outside of the container that you are in.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢——这一切有一种旧世界的味道，如果你在旅行，你不知道你所在的容器之外发生了什么。

sentences.en: So if you're on a cruise ship, you don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在游轮上，你不知道。

sentences.en: If you're on a train, you don't know.
sentences.zh: 如果你在火车上，你不知道。

sentences.en: Whereas now, the scene would be like his aide's BlackBerry suddenly buzzes – not BlackBerry, his cell phone.
sentences.zh: 而现在，场景会是他的助手黑莓手机突然震动——不是黑莓，是他的手机。

sentences.en: But his cell phone suddenly buzzes and he goes, sir, we'll have to take a look at this.
sentences.zh: 但他的手机突然震动，他说，先生，我们得看看这个。

sentences.en: And then by the time they are getting off the train, he's got a statement prepared.
sentences.zh: 等到他们下火车时，他已经准备好了声明。

sentences.en: Instead, he is just totally taken by surprise.
sentences.zh: 相反，他完全措手不及。

sentences.en: He has no idea what's been happening because he's on a train.
sentences.zh: 他根本不知道发生了什么，因为他在火车上。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: And like the image of a flustered LaGuardia is like an image I kind of love conjuring in my mind because you can totally imagine.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚慌乱的形象是我脑海中喜欢浮现的画面，因为你完全可以想象。

sentences.en: It's just his sweaty face, you know, just like –
sentences.zh: 就是他那张汗津津的脸，你知道，就像——

sentences.en: He already looks like he just rolled out of bed.
sentences.zh: 他看起来就像刚从床上爬起来一样。

sentences.en: So even more now, he's like –
sentences.zh: 所以现在更是这样，他就像——

sentences.en: Like I have to imagine this guy who runs his fingers through his hair a lot when he's like stressed out and thinking and makes it all poof out.
sentences.zh: 我得想象这个家伙，他在压力大和思考时经常用手指梳理头发，让头发蓬松起来。

sentences.en: And yeah, I love it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我喜欢。

sentences.en: And he's just like, what the fuck has this guy done to me now?
sentences.zh: 他就像，这个家伙现在又对我做了什么鬼事？

sentences.en: Oh, Jesus ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Jesus ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: You know, like you have to imagine every press report –
sentences.zh: 你知道，你得想象每一篇新闻报道——

sentences.en: Because back then they would kind of clean up a politician's answers to make them look better.
sentences.zh: 因为那时他们会润色政客的回答，让他们看起来更好。

sentences.en: That every press report, they're just blacking out the words Jesus Christ in the transcript, you know.
sentences.zh: 每一篇新闻报道，他们都在转录中删掉了“天哪”这个词，你知道。

sentences.en: But editorials are written about this.
sentences.zh: 但关于这件事的社论写出来了。

sentences.en: They're attacking LaGuardia.
sentences.zh: 他们在攻击拉瓜迪亚。

sentences.en: They're attacking Icky's.
sentences.zh: 他们在攻击伊克斯。

sentences.en: Suddenly, dozens of business and civic organizations are issuing resolutions in support of Moses.
sentences.zh: 突然间，几十个商业和民间组织纷纷发布决议，支持摩西。

sentences.en: He's a hero again.
sentences.zh: 他又成了英雄。

sentences.en: Suddenly, he's a hero.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他成了英雄。

sentences.en: And there's this long list of different organizations, different local civic and business groups that are going out of their way to issue public resolutions in support of Moses.
sentences.zh: 有一长串不同的组织，各种当地的民间和商业团体，都在不遗余力地发布公开决议来支持摩西。

sentences.en: And everyone's trying to stonewall.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在试图阻挠。

sentences.en: LaGuardia is like, this problem doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚的态度是，这个问题根本不存在。

sentences.en: But Moses keeps the fight in the press.
sentences.zh: 但摩西坚持在媒体上进行抗争。

sentences.en: Every week,
sentences.zh: 每周，

sentences.en: he's announcing how little money they have left on hand to complete building the Triborough Bridge because the government's not – the federal government's not giving them any.
sentences.zh: 他都会宣布他们手头剩下的钱有多么少，根本不够完成三区大桥的建设，因为政府——联邦政府根本没给他们拨款。

sentences.en: And Roosevelt finally admits to reporters that he was aware of Order 129.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福最终向记者承认，他知道第129号令的事。

sentences.en: And then 147 different civic organizations then meet,
sentences.zh: 然后147个不同的民间组织开了会，

sentences.en: and they basically make a show of reaccepting Moses as a member of the civic reform community because they want to support the principle of independent local government.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是做做样子，重新接纳摩西作为公民改革社区的一员，因为他们想支持独立地方政府的原则。

sentences.en: This principle of balance of powers and local control of things that is so fundamental to the founding blah, blah, blah, and et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 这种权力制衡和地方控制的原则，是建国之本，巴拉巴拉，等等等等。

sentences.en: And Moses is now the symbol of that.
sentences.zh: 而摩西现在就是这一原则的象征。

sentences.en: And by 1935, it's a national issue, and people are like, the New Deal funds are being used for political purposes.
sentences.zh: 到了1935年，这已经成了全国性的议题，人们都在说，新政资金被用于政治目的了。

sentences.en: This is not okay.
sentences.zh: 这可不行。

sentences.en: And Republicans want to investigate it.
sentences.zh: 共和党人想要调查此事。

sentences.en: LaGuardia finally comes with a solution.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚终于拿出了一个解决方案。

sentences.en: It's months later as after he has been going, oh, Jesus Christ, to anybody who will listen.
sentences.zh: 这已经是几个月后的事了，在此之前，他一直在对任何愿意听的人喊着“噢，天哪”。

sentences.en: He sends a letter to the government saying, I will abide by the order,
sentences.zh: 他给政府发了一封信，说我会遵守该命令，

sentences.en: but it would cause so much trouble to apply it retroactively because I cannot lose Langdon Post from the tenement housing position.
sentences.zh: 但如果追溯执行会造成太大的麻烦，因为我不能失去负责廉租房职位的兰登·波斯特。

sentences.en: I can't do it.
sentences.zh: 我做不到。

sentences.en: He's just too important.
sentences.zh: 他太重要了。

sentences.en: This guy who was on vacation when all this was going down, he's just – I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 这家伙在这一切发生时还在度假，他只是——我很抱歉。

sentences.en: It's too much to ask.
sentences.zh: 这要求太过分了。

sentences.en: Oh, and P.S., this would also apply to Robert Moses in addition.
sentences.zh: 噢，顺便提一下，这同样适用于罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: But Langdon Post is really why I'm doing this.
sentences.zh: 但兰登·波斯特才是我这么做的真正原因。

sentences.en: And Al Smith, who's been kind of biding his time, waiting for the right moment to step in, this is when he does step in.
sentences.zh: 而一直以来都在静观其变、等待时机介入的阿尔·史密斯，就在这时出手了。

sentences.en: He says, now is the time to put my finger on the scale.
sentences.zh: 他说，现在是时候让我施加影响了。

sentences.en: And he gives a speech talking about how necessary it is that Moses stay at the Triborough Authority so his big roads plan can go through.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一场演讲，谈到摩西留在三区大桥管理局是多么必要，这样他的大型道路规划才能得以实施。

sentences.en: And that's presented by Caro as the final kind of feather on the scale.
sentences.zh: 卡罗把这描述为天平上最后的一根羽毛。

sentences.en: That's what – the straw that breaks the camel's back.
sentences.zh: 这就是——压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: I'm trying to get more metaphors into this.
sentences.zh: 我正试着在谈话里多用点比喻。

sentences.en: And so Roosevelt, he has Ickes write a letter to LaGuardia accepting this non-retroactive reading.
sentences.zh: 于是罗斯福让伊克斯写信给拉瓜迪亚，接受这种非追溯性的解读。

sentences.en: But they predate the letter to one day before Smith's speech so that it won't look like it was because of the speech that they did it.
sentences.zh: 但他们把信的日期提前到了史密斯演讲的前一天，这样看起来就不像是受演讲影响才做的决定。

sentences.en: And the press immediately sees through it, and they're like, Moses beats Ickes.
sentences.zh: 媒体立刻看穿了这一点，他们说，摩西打败了伊克斯。

sentences.en: They did it.
sentences.zh: 他们做到了。

sentences.en: And Ickes, who at this point has just been doing what the president has been telling him to do.
sentences.zh: 而此时的伊克斯，一直以来都只是在执行总统的命令。

sentences.en: He doesn't have a personal stake in this.
sentences.zh: 他在这件事上没有个人利益。

sentences.en: He's very hurt by it, but he still kind of gives props to Moses for handling the fight in such a powerful way.
sentences.zh: 他为此感到非常受伤，但他还是对摩西以如此强有力的方式处理这场斗争表示了敬意。

sentences.en: And the most important thing of all is with this action, Moses now has his halo back.
sentences.zh: 最重要的一点是，通过这次行动，摩西现在又找回了他的光环。

sentences.en: Now he is no longer the mean guy who calls people a liar running to support the old guard.
sentences.zh: 他不再是那个为了支持旧势力而骂人是骗子的卑鄙小人了。

sentences.en: He is, again, the defender of the people that the bigger guy is trying to crush.
sentences.zh: 他再次成为了被大人物试图压迫的人民的捍卫者。

sentences.en: And this is the halo that stays on him pretty much for decades.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个几乎伴随了他几十年的光环。

sentences.en: Pretty much the rest of the time.
sentences.zh: 几乎是余下的所有时间。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Like, this is a real, like, if you come at the king, you best not miss kind of scenario.
sentences.zh: 这就像是那种“如果你要挑战国王，最好别失手”的剧本。

sentences.en: And they really missed, and it really resurrected him in every way possible.
sentences.zh: 他们确实失手了，这反而让他以各种可能的方式复活了。

sentences.en: It's like the bullet missed the king, bounced off the wall, hit a bottle of super medicine that then tipped into the king's mouth and made him stronger.
sentences.zh: 就像子弹没打中国王，反弹到墙上，击中了一瓶超级药水，药水倒进国王嘴里，让他变得更强了。

sentences.en: Like, that's how badly they missed, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，他们失手得就是这么离谱。

sentences.en: And so much so that they eventually share a stage, you know, when the opening of the Triborough Bridge happens.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们最终在三区大桥落成典礼上同台亮相了。

sentences.en: And this is one of my favorite things is, like, Moses can't accept that he just won this, like, completely.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一点是，摩西无法接受他竟然赢得如此彻底。

sentences.en: Like, this is, like, he won this so thoroughly, it's almost embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 他赢的程度简直让人尴尬。

sentences.en: It's embarrassing to Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 这对罗斯福来说很尴尬。

sentences.en: But the pettiness continues because when the Triborough Bridge opens, the ceremony happens.
sentences.zh: 但这种小家子气还在继续，因为当三区大桥开通时，仪式举行了。

sentences.en: And, you know, he's smart enough to know that he has to invite Roosevelt because otherwise, I mean, this is a big federal project.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他很聪明，知道必须邀请罗斯福，否则——毕竟这是一个大型联邦项目。

sentences.en: But he only allows him, because he puts together the ceremony, he only allows Roosevelt five minutes to speak.
sentences.zh: 但他只允许罗斯福发言五分钟，因为仪式是他一手操办的。

sentences.en: Like, the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 毕竟是美国总统啊。

sentences.en: And this is happening in 1936.
sentences.zh: 这发生在1936年。

sentences.en: So the president is also running for re-election that year.
sentences.zh: 所以总统那年还要竞选连任。

sentences.en: Like, this is a bit like, the president's going to want to talk for more than five minutes.
sentences.zh: 这有点像，总统肯定想讲超过五分钟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so LaGuardia tells him he's got to talk more than five minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以拉瓜迪亚告诉他，他得讲超过五分钟。

sentences.en: And Moses says, okay, he can talk for six minutes.
sentences.zh: 摩西说，好吧，他可以讲六分钟。

sentences.en: It's so, it's so ridiculously petty.
sentences.zh: 这真是太荒谬、太小气了。

sentences.en: And I was looking over this again.
sentences.zh: 我又把这些内容看了一遍。

sentences.en: I was thinking back to our talk with AOC last episode.
sentences.zh: 我想起了上一集我们和AOC的谈话。

sentences.en: Go back and listen to it if you didn't hear it.
sentences.zh: 如果你没听过，回去听听看。

sentences.en: Where she's talking about how, like, this happens.
sentences.zh: 她在谈论这种事情是如何发生的。

sentences.en: This is how decisions get made often is, I don't like that guy.
sentences.zh: 很多决策往往就是这样产生的：我不喜欢那个人。

sentences.en: I'm not going to do this.
sentences.zh: 我才不要做这个。

sentences.en: Or, ugh, I just cannot, I have to poke this guy.
sentences.zh: 或者，呃，我受不了，我非得找那家伙麻烦不可。

sentences.en: And so he goes, all right, I'll give him one more minute to talk.
sentences.zh: 于是他说，好吧，我让他多讲一分钟。

sentences.en: And also, Ickes is invited as a general spectator.
sentences.zh: 另外，伊克斯也作为普通观众被邀请了。

sentences.en: And he is really mad that he isn't going to get to speak.
sentences.zh: 他非常生气自己没能发言。

sentences.en: And finally he does.
sentences.zh: 最后他还是讲了。

sentences.en: And Roosevelt and Ickes, they give their speeches that do not mention Moses.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福和伊克斯发表了演讲，但都没有提到摩西。

sentences.en: And Moses in his speech does not mention the president.
sentences.zh: 而摩西在演讲中也没有提到总统。

sentences.en: But he indulges, and this is classic Moses.
sentences.zh: 但他还是放纵了一把，这很摩西。

sentences.en: I feel it's the perfect way to end this chapter and the duo of the candidate chapter in this one.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是结束这一章以及这一章中候选人二人组的完美方式。

sentences.en: Because it's Moses falling back in his bad habits again.
sentences.zh: 因为这又是摩西故态复萌了。

sentences.en: As far as his speech, he has this incredibly oblique insult towards Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 至于他的演讲，他对罗斯福进行了极其隐晦的侮辱。

sentences.en: This veiled insult that is based around knowing an anecdote from the life of Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 这种含蓄的侮辱是基于对塞缪尔·约翰逊生平轶事的了解。

sentences.en: And it flies completely into the radar because nobody knows what he's talking about.
sentences.zh: 它完全没引起注意，因为没人知道他在说什么。

sentences.en: And Carol has to take time to explain what this insult is and what it means.
sentences.zh: 卡罗不得不花时间解释这个侮辱是什么意思。

sentences.en: But it's like Moses cannot help being like, I know I won.
sentences.zh: 但摩西就是忍不住想表现出：我知道我赢了。

sentences.en: I'm going to try to be gracious in public, but secretly.
sentences.zh: 我要在公开场合表现得大度，但私下里，

sentences.en: I'm going to insult him in this way that nobody but me will understand.
sentences.zh: 我要用这种除了我没人能懂的方式侮辱他。

sentences.en: It's almost like the first letter of every sentence of my speech.
sentences.zh: 就像是我演讲中每一句话的第一个字母。

sentences.en: If you add it up, it says Roosevelt sucks or something like that.
sentences.zh: 如果你把它们加起来，写着“罗斯福烂透了”之类的。

sentences.en: Like no one will know but me.
sentences.zh: 就像没人会知道，只有我知道一样。

sentences.en: And it's just so incredible.
sentences.zh: 这真是太不可思议了。

sentences.en: They're such children.
sentences.zh: 他们简直像孩子一样。

sentences.en: They're such petty children.
sentences.zh: 他们是如此小气的孩子。

sentences.en: And they have the lives of millions in their hands.
sentences.zh: 而数百万人的生命却掌握在他们手中。

sentences.en: It's so – I mean I love it looking back on it, reading a book.
sentences.zh: 这真是——我是说，回过头来看，读着书，我挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: But I have to imagine – but knowing that this is still how the world operates, I'm like, oh, it's so frustrating.
sentences.zh: 但想到世界依然是这样运作的，我就觉得，噢，太令人沮丧了。

sentences.en: It is a little painful.
sentences.zh: 确实有点痛苦。

sentences.en: Although I'm always having this sort of pang of wanting to see the downfall of Robert Moses before it actually happens.
sentences.zh: 虽然我总是有一种想在罗伯特·摩西真正倒台之前看到他倒台的冲动。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: So like when you get these petty squabbles, I'm mainly on FDR's side in these things.
sentences.zh: 所以当出现这些琐碎的争吵时，我主要还是站在罗斯福这一边的。

sentences.en: Yeah, at this point.
sentences.zh: 是的，目前为止。

sentences.en: And it just is just – oh, it's just rough.
sentences.zh: 这真的——噢，这真的很难受。

sentences.en: It's just rough to witness it.
sentences.zh: 目睹这一切真的很难受。

sentences.en: It's the same thing.
sentences.zh: 都是一样的事。

sentences.en: I mean it's not as bad as this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还没到那种程度。

sentences.en: The worst version of this for me is I read a lot about Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，最糟糕的版本是我读了很多关于亚伯拉罕·林肯的书。

sentences.en: I read a lot of Abraham Lincoln books because I think he's the greatest person who ever lived.
sentences.zh: 我读了很多林肯的书，因为我认为他是史上最伟大的人。

sentences.en: We don't have to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我们不必谈论这个。

sentences.en: This is a Robert Moses podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于罗伯特·摩西的播客。

sentences.en: But every time I'm reading a biography of him and it's getting closer and closer to him going to Ford's theater, I'm always like, don't go.
sentences.zh: 但每次我读他的传记，读到他越来越接近去福特剧院时，我总是想，别去。

sentences.en: No, don't do it.
sentences.zh: 不，别去。

sentences.en: And then his bodyguard leaves to get a drink in the middle of the show and I'm like, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 然后他的保镖在演出中途离开去喝了一杯，我就想，你在干什么？

sentences.en: You know it's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: I mean it's what happens when you watch a movie over again too.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你重看一部电影时也是这样。

sentences.en: You know it's going to happen but you're hoping it doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道会发生什么，但你还是希望它不要发生。

sentences.en: But that's part of the thrill of history I guess is knowing that it could have gone differently but it's too late now.
sentences.zh: 但我想这就是历史的魅力所在，知道事情本可以有不同的走向，但现在太晚了。

sentences.en: It's not going to go differently ever again.
sentences.zh: 它再也不会有不同的走向了。

sentences.en: But because of these petty machinations of FDR, Moses is sort of back on top and doing what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 但由于罗斯福这些琐碎的阴谋，摩西算是东山再起，继续做他的事了。

sentences.en: He is back in the saddle which is the title of chapter 23 in the saddle.
sentences.zh: 他重回马鞍，这也是第23章的标题，“重回马鞍”。

sentences.en: And it starts with this description of LaGuardia being just hilariously omnipresent in New York City.
sentences.zh: 开头描述了拉瓜迪亚在纽约市那种滑稽的无处不在感。

sentences.en: You're just everywhere that something is happening, LaGuardia is there just having fun, showing off, trying to make everyone love him.
sentences.zh: 无论哪里发生什么事，你都能看到拉瓜迪亚，他在那儿玩得很开心，炫耀着，试图让每个人都爱他。

sentences.en: It's hilarious.
sentences.zh: 这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: Caro makes it sound like there are 17 LaGuardias running around the city at any given point.
sentences.zh: 卡罗把它写得好像城市里随时都有17个拉瓜迪亚在跑来跑去。

sentences.en: It's like he's over there.
sentences.zh: 就像他在那边一样。

sentences.en: He's personally inspecting the treatment of people in public housing.
sentences.zh: 他亲自视察公共住房中人们的待遇。

sentences.en: There he is over there.
sentences.zh: 他又在那边了。

sentences.en: He's at the Bronx Terminal Market.
sentences.zh: 他在布朗克斯终端市场。

sentences.en: There's been stories of artichoke racketeering.
sentences.zh: 有关于朝鲜蓟敲诈勒索的传闻。

sentences.en: So he's personally banning artichokes from the Bronx Terminal Market.
sentences.zh: 所以他亲自下令禁止在布朗克斯终端市场销售朝鲜蓟。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 噢哦。

sentences.en: Firefighters are trapped under a collapsed wall.
sentences.zh: 消防员被困在倒塌的墙下。

sentences.en: He's going to go whisper encouragement to them while they're being saved.
sentences.zh: 他要去在他们获救时低声鼓励他们。

sentences.en: Like he's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他简直无处不在。

sentences.en: And at the same time, he's slashing nonessential jobs and city budget.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他还在削减非必要的工作岗位和城市预算。

sentences.en: He's pushing back on local corruption.
sentences.zh: 他在抵制地方腐败。

sentences.en: He's bullying the city into submission.
sentences.zh: 他在强迫城市屈服。

sentences.en: But he's also bullying his staff.
sentences.zh: 但他也在欺负他的员工。

sentences.en: He loves to yell at his staff.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢对员工大吼大叫。

sentences.en: He loves to fire his staff.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢解雇员工。

sentences.en: This is not entirely all positive.
sentences.zh: 这并不全是积极的。

sentences.en: But yeah, he's just – it just presents him as – I imagine him zooming around like a cartoon character, just puffs of smoke appearing where he used to be.
sentences.zh: 但确实，他只是——书里把他呈现为——我想象他像个卡通人物一样四处飞奔，在他待过的地方只留下几缕烟雾。

sentences.en: As he like runs off.
sentences.zh: 当他跑开的时候。

sentences.en: And the person who can always stand up to him is Moses.
sentences.zh: 而唯一能一直顶撞他的人就是摩西。

sentences.en: And they fight.
sentences.zh: 他们争吵。

sentences.en: They shout.
sentences.zh: 他们大喊大叫。

sentences.en: Moses is deliberately rude to him.
sentences.zh: 摩西故意对他无礼。

sentences.en: He calls him by Italian slurs both behind his back and in front of his back.
sentences.zh: 他在背后和当面都用意大利语辱骂他。

sentences.en: He's always threatening to resign to the point where – I love this so much.
sentences.zh: 他总是威胁要辞职，以至于——我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: This makes me love LaGuardia – is he has a pad printed up with forms on it that say,
sentences.zh: 这让我爱上了拉瓜迪亚——他印了一叠表格，上面写着，

sentences.en: I, Robert Moses, do hereby resign as blank, effective blank.
sentences.zh: 我，罗伯特·摩西，在此辞去空白处的职务，即日起生效。

sentences.en: And the next time Moses resigns, he hands him the pad.
sentences.zh: 而下一次摩西辞职时，他直接把辞职信甩给对方。

sentences.en: And Moses gets really mad about it.
sentences.zh: 摩西对此感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And it totally wins.
sentences.zh: 而且这招完全奏效。

sentences.en: Like he blunts that as a thing.
sentences.zh: 就像他把这当作一种手段。

sentences.en: And Robert Moses doesn't do it to him anymore.
sentences.zh: 从此罗伯特·摩西再也不敢对他那样做了。

sentences.en: They have figured out this way of like complimentary abuse that somehow fosters this kind of mutual respect that just kind of works for them.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了一种相互攻击却又相辅相成的方式，这种方式在某种程度上培养了一种对他们双方都行之有效的相互尊重。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: But it just – it does.
sentences.zh: 但事实就是如此，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it means they're constantly butting heads against each other even though in the grand scheme of things, they agree on the major goals.
sentences.zh: 没错，但这意味着他们总是针锋相对，尽管从大局来看，他们在主要目标上是一致的。

sentences.en: But they're always butting heads.
sentences.zh: 但他们总是互不相让。

sentences.en: And there are a couple fights that Kara goes into.
sentences.zh: 卡罗书中提到了几次他们之间的冲突。

sentences.en: My favorite of them that I find very sad is in 1936, Moses, he wants the land that's currently being held by the terminal for a ferry that goes between Astoria and Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一个故事，也是我觉得非常可悲的一个，发生在1936年。摩西想要征用当时由轮渡码头控制的土地，那条轮渡往返于阿斯托里亚和曼哈顿之间。

sentences.en: And you're like, oh, I'd like to go take that ferry.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，哦，我想去坐那趟轮渡。

sentences.en: You can't.
sentences.zh: 但你坐不成了。

sentences.en: It's not there anymore.
sentences.zh: 它已经不存在了。

sentences.en: Don't even try.
sentences.zh: 别白费力气了。

sentences.en: I'll tell you why it's not there.
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你它为什么不在了。

sentences.en: LaGuardia is like, you should wait.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚说，你应该等等。

sentences.en: The commuters are not ready to lose it.
sentences.zh: 通勤者们还没准备好失去它。

sentences.en: It's a five-cent ferry trip which is more pleasant and cheaper than riding on what's going to be a 50-cent toll road.
sentences.zh: 那是一趟五分钱的轮渡，比乘坐即将建成的50美分收费公路更舒适、更便宜。

sentences.en: And Caro, he paints it as the kind of like endearing, antiquated piece of old New York, this old,
sentences.zh: 卡罗把它描绘成一种令人怀念的、过时的老纽约风情，这种老旧的、

sentences.en: this rusty old ferry that modern New York is doing its best to just throw away as fast as possible.
sentences.zh: 这种锈迹斑斑的老轮渡，现代纽约正竭尽全力想尽快将其抛弃。

sentences.en: And Moses is in his patient.
sentences.zh: 而摩西却很有耐心。

sentences.en: So literally as soon as the ferry leaves the dock one day,
sentences.zh: 所以有一天，轮渡刚一离开码头，

sentences.en: he just sends his workers in and they start smashing up the dock and smashing up the ferry terminal building and even tearing up the road leading to the ferry terminal building.
sentences.zh: 他立刻派工人进去，开始拆毁码头、砸烂轮渡候船大楼，甚至拆除了通往候船大楼的道路。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia has to send the police to arrest the parks workers who are doing this.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚不得不派警察去逮捕那些正在执行任务的公园管理局工人。

sentences.en: And then a week later, Moses, he just gets the land and he tears down the ferry house completely.
sentences.zh: 一周后，摩西直接拿到了土地，把候船室彻底拆平了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's crazy.
sentences.zh: 没错，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I mean like he calls the police on his own parks guy and it's just sort of like it's like they're playing a game of chess and there's all these people, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他竟然报警抓自己公园管理局的人，这就像他们在下一盘棋，而所有这些人，你知道的，

sentences.en: caught in the middle of it where, you know,
sentences.zh: 都被夹在中间，你知道，

sentences.en: a policeman has to like arrest a worker who's just being told like don't stop for anybody because this jerk Robert Moses tells him not stop for anybody.
sentences.zh: 警察不得不去逮捕一个工人，而那个工人只是被告知“不要停下，不管是谁都别管”，因为那个混蛋罗伯特·摩西命令他不许停下。

sentences.en: And the cops come and the cops come and it's just a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 警察来了又来，这简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: And then they have to like there's like a boat out like that has nowhere to go because it has to find another place to dock because he tore the dock up.
sentences.zh: 然后他们不得不……有一艘船无处可去，因为它必须找到另一个停靠点，因为他把码头拆了。

sentences.en: He just doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 他根本不在乎。

sentences.en: There's people on that boat.
sentences.zh: 船上还有人呢。

sentences.en: They can't live on it.
sentences.zh: 他们没法住在船上。

sentences.en: It's crazy how much he doesn't think about individuals.
sentences.zh: 他完全不考虑个人的感受，这真是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And it's just sort of stunning.
sentences.zh: 这简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: I'm sort of like this is like real villainy.
sentences.zh: 我感觉这简直是真正的邪恶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, he knows that his goals – and this will become clear more and more in this section of the book as we're talking,
sentences.zh: 好吧，他知道他的目标——随着我们谈话的深入，在书的这一部分会越来越清晰，

sentences.en: this overall episode – that his goals he believes are the best and only useful goals.
sentences.zh: 也就是这一整集的内容——他认为自己的目标是最好且唯一有价值的目标。

sentences.en: And so anything that has to be done to get those goals as quickly and as effectively as possible, he'll do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了尽快、最有效地实现这些目标，无论需要做什么，他都会去做。

sentences.en: You know, there's – in 1937, so the next year, LaGuardia's got to call the police out on him again because LaGuardia's like we've got to move 2,000 of the laborers,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在1937年，也就是第二年，拉瓜迪亚不得不再次报警对付他，因为拉瓜迪亚说我们必须调走2000名劳工，

sentences.en: the federal workers who are working for you.
sentences.zh: 那些为你工作的联邦工人。

sentences.en: We've got to reassign them from your projects to other projects.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把他们从你的项目中调到其他项目中去。

sentences.en: And he goes, okay, we'll reassign the playground supervisors, and he fires 2,000 playground supervisors,
sentences.zh: 结果他说，好吧，那就调走游乐场管理员吧，于是他解雇了2000名游乐场管理员，

sentences.en: and he locks shut over 140 playgrounds and removes the playground equipment so they can't be reopened.
sentences.zh: 并锁上了140多个游乐场，拆除了游乐设施，这样它们就无法重新开放了。

sentences.en: And moms with kids start protesting because they went to their playground, and they found that the police have chained it shut, and there's no equipment.
sentences.zh: 带着孩子的母亲们开始抗议，因为她们去游乐场时发现警察已经锁上了大门，里面什么设施都没有了。

sentences.en: And he's got to call out the police again to try to get him to stop closing these playgrounds.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚不得不再次出动警察，试图让他停止关闭这些游乐场。

sentences.en: And every time this happens, Moses is able to spin it so that they blame the city or they blame LaGuardia rather than Moses.
sentences.zh: 而每次发生这种情况，摩西都能扭转舆论，让人们去责怪市政府或拉瓜迪亚，而不是摩西。

sentences.en: And Caro starts to theorize that Moses got away with this partly because LaGuardia respected people who would stand up to him and fight him and partly because they both wanted the same thing ultimately.
