sentences.zh: 卡罗开始推测，摩西之所以能逍遥法外，部分原因是拉瓜迪亚尊重那些敢于站出来反抗他的人，部分原因是他们最终想要的东西是一样的。

sentences.en: LaGuardia wants New York to be a beautiful city.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚希望纽约成为一座美丽的城市。

sentences.en: He wants it to be a new, functioning, gleaming city, and he loves engineering.
sentences.zh: 他希望它成为一座崭新的、功能齐全、熠熠生辉的城市，而且他热爱工程学。

sentences.en: He's hugely in awe of large-scale construction.
sentences.zh: 他非常敬畏大型建筑工程。

sentences.en: He's like a child.
sentences.zh: 他就像个孩子。

sentences.en: He likes to wear a construction hat or a hard hat and go to a construction site and go, wow, look at those big machines.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢戴上建筑工人的安全帽，去施工现场说，哇，看那些大机器。

sentences.en: Wow, look at that.
sentences.zh: 哇，看那个。

sentences.en: And at one point, LaGuardia calls Moses the greatest engineer in the world, and Moses even is not technically an engineer.
sentences.zh: 有一次，拉瓜迪亚称摩西为世界上最伟大的工程师，尽管摩西在技术上根本不是工程师。

sentences.en: He doesn't have an engineering degree.
sentences.zh: 他没有工程学位。

sentences.en: He doesn't know how to draw up plans, but he has the staff that can draw up plans, and he's the only person who has it.
sentences.zh: 他不知道怎么画图纸，但他拥有能画图纸的员工，而且他是唯一拥有这种资源的人。

sentences.en: So the third part of it, I don't remember how many – I haven't counted.
sentences.zh: 所以这第三点，我不记得有多少点了——我还没数过。

sentences.en: The final leg in the stool of however many legs is that they need this federal money to do it,
sentences.zh: 无论有多少根支柱，最后的一根支柱就是他们需要联邦资金来完成这些项目，

sentences.en: and Moses is the only guy who can get that federal money because he can create the plans.
sentences.zh: 而摩西是唯一能拿到联邦资金的人，因为他能制定出计划。

sentences.en: He has the people who can create the plans to get it.
sentences.zh: 他拥有能制定出获取资金计划的人才。

sentences.en: Yeah, he has shovel-ready projects that allow them to pass through the PWA system, and he can keep getting money and money and money.
sentences.zh: 没错，他有随时可以开工的项目，这使它们能够通过公共工程管理局（PWA）的系统，他可以源源不断地获得资金。

sentences.en: He's just like always ready, always on the ball.
sentences.zh: 他总是准备就绪，总是反应敏捷。

sentences.en: He also, like when it comes to these types of arguments and the rough tactics which they use against each other, Moses sort of lacks compunction.
sentences.zh: 而且，当涉及到这类争论以及他们相互使用的粗暴手段时，摩西似乎缺乏负罪感。

sentences.en: Like I think they fight over these things, and LaGuardia wants a lot of the same things Moses wants.
sentences.zh: 我想他们会为这些事情争吵，拉瓜迪亚想要的很多东西和摩西想要的一样。

sentences.en: But the reason why Moses wins in each of these moments is because he does not care about these people, and LaGuardia actually does.
sentences.zh: 但摩西在每一次冲突中都能获胜，是因为他根本不在乎那些人，而拉瓜迪亚确实在乎。

sentences.en: And it's just infuriating to watch.
sentences.zh: 看着这一切真是让人愤怒。

sentences.en: I mean it just makes me so mad to read about it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，读到这些真的让我非常生气。

sentences.en: It's a little bit like the story of Solomon and the two mothers and the baby.
sentences.zh: 这有点像所罗门王和两个母亲争夺婴儿的故事。

sentences.en: If Solomon had said, we're going to have to cut this baby in half, and the one mother said, okay, go ahead, do it.
sentences.zh: 如果所罗门说，我们得把这个孩子劈成两半，其中一个母亲说，好吧，动手吧。

sentences.en: And Solomon said, I had my guts.
sentences.zh: 然后所罗门说，我真是受够了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you take the baby.
sentences.zh: 没错，孩子给你吧。

sentences.en: You stood up, and you wouldn't compromise.
sentences.zh: 你站了出来，而且你不肯妥协。

sentences.en: You take this baby.
sentences.zh: 孩子给你。

sentences.en: Like it feels unjuSt.
sentences.zh: 这感觉太不公平了。

sentences.en: It feels like things go the wrong way when Moses just bullies his way into getting stuff done.
sentences.zh: 当摩西只是靠霸凌手段强行把事情办成时，感觉事情总是走向了错误的方向。

sentences.en: But that happens in politics still that there's a certain respect for the ability to not care in that you're unstoppable.
sentences.zh: 但这在政治中依然会发生，人们对那种“不在乎”的能力有一种敬畏，因为这意味着你势不可挡。

sentences.en: You won't let anyone stand in your way.
sentences.zh: 你不会让任何人挡你的路。

sentences.en: And it's the person who cares too much who is more easily held hostage because if things go bad, they'll be upset.
sentences.zh: 而那个太在乎的人反而更容易被挟持，因为如果事情变糟了，他们会感到难过。

sentences.en: But the other side, if things go bad, they don't care.
sentences.zh: 但另一方，如果事情变糟了，他们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter to them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说无所谓。

sentences.en: They don't care at all.
sentences.zh: 他们一点也不在乎。

sentences.en: And I think the other part that keeps Moses sort of buttressed in these fights is he has such a tight relationship with the press.
sentences.zh: 我认为摩西在这些争斗中能够屹立不倒的另一个原因，是他与媒体有着极其紧密的关系。

sentences.en: So like none of this would leak out.
sentences.zh: 所以这些事情都不会泄露出去。

sentences.en: Like him not caring, him being the person that moved the park workers and fired them so that the parks would be shut down.
sentences.zh: 比如他不在乎，比如他就是那个调动公园工人并解雇他们导致公园关闭的人。

sentences.en: You know, none of that leaks out because he just has cultivated this relationship with the press that is almost – there's just no light between them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些都不会泄露出去，因为他已经培养了与媒体的关系，几乎到了密不透风的地步。

sentences.en: And he's very good at wooing the press.
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长讨好媒体。

sentences.en: He like takes publishers and editors and reporters.
sentences.zh: 他会招待出版商、编辑和记者。

sentences.en: At this point, there's 13 daily newspapers in New York City, which is astonishing to me.
sentences.zh: 当时纽约市有13家日报，这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: It's just incredible.
sentences.zh: 这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: And he takes the publishers and the editors and reporters on banquets.
sentences.zh: 他会请出版商、编辑和记者参加宴会。

sentences.en: He'll take them on yacht trips.
sentences.zh: 他会带他们去坐游艇旅行。

sentences.en: He'll throw parties for them at Jones Beach.
sentences.zh: 他会在琼斯海滩为他们举办派对。

sentences.en: And there's a chapter much later in the book where it kind of gives you a firsthand look at the luxury lifestyle that lavishes in the RM chapter.
sentences.zh: 书的后面有一章，让你亲眼目睹了他在那一章里挥霍的奢华生活方式。

sentences.en: Well, I'm so looking forward to that one.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我非常期待那一章。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But he's also personal friends with some of the most powerful newspaper owners in the city.
sentences.zh: 但他也是城里一些最有权势的报业老板的私人朋友。

sentences.en: He's friends with Ogden Mills-Reed of the Herald Tribune.
sentences.zh: 他是《先驱论坛报》奥格登·米尔斯·里德的朋友。

sentences.en: You may remember Ogden Mills-Reed as the guy that Moses was going to con money out of when he was a Yale student.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得奥格登·米尔斯·里德，就是摩西在耶鲁大学读书时打算骗他钱的那个人。

sentences.en: Reed never found out about that, so he's still his friend.
sentences.zh: 里德从来没发现那件事，所以他还是他的朋友。

sentences.en: But most importantly, he's friends with the Salzburgers, the owners of the New York Times at the time as is now.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，他是萨尔茨伯格家族的朋友，也就是当时（现在也是）《纽约时报》的所有者。

sentences.en: It's the most influential paper in the country, and two-thirds of the Times stock is owned by Ithagene Ox Salzburger, such an amazing name.
sentences.zh: 这是全国最有影响力的报纸，《纽约时报》三分之二的股份由伊塔金·奥克斯·萨尔茨伯格拥有，这名字太棒了。
zh_words: 伊塔金·奥克斯·萨尔茨伯格

sentences.en: And she loves public parks.
sentences.zh: 她热爱公共公园。

sentences.en: She loves parks, and she worships Moses too as the guy who can make parks.
sentences.zh: 她热爱公园，也崇拜摩西，认为他是那个能建造公园的人。

sentences.en: And she doesn't always agree with him.
sentences.zh: 她并不总是同意他的观点。

sentences.en: She's the one that Carol quotes as saying that engineers are straight-line crazy, which becomes the name of the David Hare play about Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 卡罗引用过她的话，说工程师都是“直线狂人”，这后来成了大卫·黑尔关于罗伯特·摩西的戏剧的名字。

sentences.en: So she wants parks that are grass.
sentences.zh: 所以她想要的是草地公园。

sentences.en: She doesn't want concrete facilities, and she thinks Moses is doing the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 她不想要混凝土设施，她认为摩西的做法是错误的。

sentences.en: But even if he's doing the wrong way, he's still building parks.
sentences.zh: 但即使他的做法不对，他毕竟还是在建公园。

sentences.en: A concrete park is better than no park.
sentences.zh: 有混凝土公园总比没有公园强。

sentences.en: No park, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没有公园，没错。

sentences.en: And so that's what she cares about.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是她所关心的。

sentences.en: And there's a part where she disagrees with Moses, and he sends her an insulting letter.
sentences.zh: 有一次她和摩西意见不合，摩西给她写了一封侮辱性的信。

sentences.en: And the New York Times prints her apology, her public apology for disagreeing with him.
sentences.zh: 结果《纽约时报》刊登了她的道歉声明，为她与摩西意见不合而公开道歉。

sentences.en: And the reporters at the Times, they're never told by her, you have to support Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 《时报》的记者们从未被她要求“你们必须支持罗伯特·摩西”。

sentences.en: But they know how to keep the boss happy.
sentences.zh: 但他们知道如何让老板高兴。

sentences.en: Like when you work for someone, you know how to keep them happy.
sentences.zh: 就像当你为某人工作时，你知道如何让他们满意。

sentences.en: You know what they want, and you know what things they're going to like.
sentences.zh: 你知道他们想要什么，也知道他们会喜欢什么。

sentences.en: And so when Moses says something, the Times but also the other papers, but especially the Times, takes it as truth.
sentences.zh: 所以当摩西发表言论时，《时报》以及其他报纸，尤其是《时报》，都会将其视为真理。

sentences.en: He's the guy who's telling the truth, and his side is the one that deserves reporting.
sentences.zh: 他是那个说真话的人，他的立场才是值得报道的。

sentences.en: So LaGuardia can't fire him.
sentences.zh: 所以拉瓜迪亚没法解雇他。

sentences.en: The most powerful newspaper at a time when newspapers were so much more powerful than they are now.
sentences.zh: 在那个报纸比现在强大得多的时代，这是最有权势的报纸。

sentences.en: It's the way most people still got their information about the world around them.
sentences.zh: 那是大多数人获取周围世界信息的主要途径。

sentences.en: It'll give him hell if he fires Moses.
sentences.zh: 如果拉瓜迪亚解雇摩西，报纸会让他日子不好过。

sentences.en: And so at this point, a certain point, LaGuardia is like not even bringing up complaints to Moses.
sentences.zh: 所以到了某个阶段，拉瓜迪亚甚至不再向摩西提出抱怨了。

sentences.en: And he learns that he's got to argue with Moses in private, but then let Moses have his way and then pretend in public that there was no disagreement between the two of them.
sentences.zh: 他学会了必须私下里和摩西争论，但随后让摩西如愿以偿，然后在公开场合假装他们之间没有任何分歧。

sentences.en: Because Moses is just untouchable because of this relationship to the press.
sentences.zh: 因为摩西凭借这种与媒体的关系，简直是不可触碰的。

sentences.en: And he's also untouchable because he holds this sort of like role getting money from the federal government.
sentences.zh: 而且他不可触碰的另一个原因是，他担任着从联邦政府获取资金的角色。

sentences.en: He holds this role in the city.
sentences.zh: 他在市政府担任这个角色。

sentences.en: And he also has this role in the state government.
sentences.zh: 同时他在州政府也担任这个角色。

sentences.en: And this is the reason why there was a law that made that illegal.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么曾经有一项法律规定这种做法是非法的。

sentences.en: Because it is a very easy way to make someone more powerful than the mayor.
sentences.zh: 因为这太容易让人变得比市长更有权势了。

sentences.en: Yes, which is exactly what happens because Moses has access to the federal money.
sentences.zh: 是的，这正是发生的事情，因为摩西有权获取联邦资金。

sentences.en: He's not using city money to build his projects usually.
sentences.zh: 他通常不使用市政资金来建造他的项目。

sentences.en: So he doesn't need the city's approval.
sentences.zh: 所以他不需要市政府的批准。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter what the voters of the city necessarily think because he's not listening to them.
sentences.zh: 而且城市选民的想法并不重要，因为他根本不听他们的。

sentences.en: And if the mayor says, hey, you shouldn't do that.
sentences.zh: 如果市长说，嘿，你不应该那样做。

sentences.en: The people in the city aren't going to like it.
sentences.zh: 城里的人不会喜欢的。

sentences.en: He can say to the people in the state government, make some trouble for LaGuardia.
sentences.zh: 他可以对州政府的人说，给拉瓜迪亚制造点麻烦。

sentences.en: I don't want things to go easy for him while he's making it difficult for me.
sentences.zh: 当他给我制造困难时，我也不想让他过得轻松。

sentences.en: Or he can approve his own projects when it needs state approval.
sentences.zh: 或者当项目需要州政府批准时，他可以自己批准自己的项目。

sentences.en: And it's as if my children had outside money coming in and also then had a relationship with my parents where I'd be like, it's time to go to bed.
sentences.zh: 这就好比我的孩子们有外来的钱，而且和我父母关系很好，当我说“该睡觉了，你们现在必须去睡觉”时，

sentences.en: You've got to go to bed right now.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，哦，有意思。

sentences.en: And they're like, oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我为什么不给爷爷打个电话，让他来生你的气呢？

sentences.en: Well, why don't I call up grandpa and have him get mad at you?
sentences.zh: 那不如我给爷爷打个电话，让他来骂你一顿？

sentences.en: Why don't I have grandpa yell at you over the phone?
sentences.zh: 要不我让爷爷在电话里冲你吼两句？

sentences.en: And I'm like, well, then you're not going to eat your allowance.
sentences.zh: 我就说，那你就别想拿零花钱了。

sentences.en: And they're like, that's cool because the federal government is giving me a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 他们就会说，没关系，联邦政府给了我十亿呢。

sentences.en: So I don't need this allowance money.
sentences.zh: 所以我根本不需要这点零花钱。

sentences.en: I think I'm going to stay up until midnight tonight.
sentences.zh: 我想今晚熬到午夜再睡。

sentences.en: But you have school tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 可你明天还要上学呢。

sentences.en: Do I?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Do I have to call grandpa again?
sentences.zh: 难道非得让我再给爷爷打个电话？

sentences.en: Like that's the situation.
sentences.zh: 情况就是这样。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, ostensibly the guy who works for the mayor is more powerful than the mayor and is running things.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，表面上那个为市长工作的人比市长权力更大，而且是他说了算。

sentences.en: And so Carroll makes the point, and he goes into a lot of detail about it, but we can kind of like skim,
sentences.zh: 卡罗指出了这一点，并对此进行了详细阐述，不过我们可以略读一下，

sentences.en: is that more money is being spent in the city than ever before to rebuild the city.
sentences.zh: 那就是为了重建这座城市，投入的资金比以往任何时候都要多。

sentences.en: But it's not the city's money.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是市政府的钱。

sentences.en: All because he's constructed this power organization that is beholden to no one, no one elected figure who is supposed to have oversight over him.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是因为他建立了一个权力组织，谁也不用负责，没有任何民选官员能对他进行监督。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: And this actually just gets worse because pretty soon he's going to get all that toll money too to do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而且情况只会更糟，因为很快他就能拿到所有的过路费，用来做同样的事。

sentences.en: But right now he is just balancing all these different forces that he has his tentacles in and he can just lean on one, you know, like get money from another, circumvent another.
sentences.zh: 但现在，他只是在平衡各种势力，他的触角伸向了各个角落，他可以向一方施压，你知道，比如从另一方弄钱，或者绕过第三方。

sentences.en: And he just is this amazing operator, you know, just taking advantage of the gaps between these different organizations and how they cannot work together.
sentences.zh: 他真是一个了不起的操盘手，你知道，他充分利用了这些不同组织之间的缝隙，以及他们无法协同工作的事实。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the things that he saw as impossible to do before, like trading political favors to get support, he's now totally fine with doing.
sentences.zh: 以前他认为不可能做到的事，比如通过政治交易来换取支持，现在他做起来完全没有心理负担。

sentences.en: And whereas before he used to be the no – he'd tell people, go to hell if you want patronage.
sentences.zh: 以前他会拒绝——如果有人想求他办事，他会让人滚蛋。

sentences.en: Now he's like, does your kid need a summer job as a lifeguard?
sentences.zh: 现在他会说，你孩子需要一份救生员的暑期工作吗？

sentences.en: Well, give me your vote.
sentences.zh: 那就把选票投给我。

sentences.en: He's got that job.
sentences.zh: 那份工作他拿到了。

sentences.en: He's very happy to do that.
sentences.zh: 他非常乐意这么做。

sentences.en: And at this point, Moses, as we mentioned before, he has more in common with the Republicans in the state legislature than LaGuardia who is ostensibly the Republican mayor.
sentences.zh: 此时，正如我们之前提到的，摩西与州议会的共和党人比与拉瓜迪亚（表面上的共和党市长）更有共同语言。

sentences.en: LaGuardia is the original rhino.
sentences.zh: 拉瓜迪亚是典型的“假共和党人”。

sentences.en: He's basically a New Deal liberal who just happens to be a Republican.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是个新政自由派，只是恰好挂着共和党的名头。

sentences.en: And he just has so much power.
sentences.zh: 而且他拥有太大的权力了。

sentences.en: And the ultimate point of this that Caro is trying to make throughout the book is that in theory,
sentences.zh: 卡罗在整本书中试图表达的核心观点是，从理论上讲，

sentences.en: the purpose of a democracy is so that the people have ultimate control and ultimate say over how they are governed and how their municipalities exist,
sentences.zh: 民主的目的在于让人民拥有最终的控制权和话语权，决定他们如何被治理，市政如何运作，

sentences.en: what's built and what's not built and things like that.
sentences.zh: 什么该建，什么不该建，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Moses has hacked the system in a way that takes him completely out of that accountability control.
sentences.zh: 而摩西破解了这个系统，使他完全脱离了这种问责控制。

sentences.en: And is that the way that a city government or a state government or a federal government should be operating?
sentences.zh: 这难道是市、州或联邦政府应有的运作方式吗？

sentences.en: No, sir.
sentences.zh: 不，先生。

sentences.en: No, sir.
sentences.zh: 不，先生。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: And yet, that's the way it is.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实就是如此。

sentences.en: The cracks are there.
sentences.zh: 裂痕已经出现了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，没错，没错。

sentences.en: This is really it.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键所在。

sentences.en: His knowledge of all these different systems, it just allows him to exploit and, you know, wheedle his way through and strong arm in some places,
sentences.zh: 他对所有这些系统的了解，让他能够进行剥削，你知道，通过钻营和在某些地方强行施压，

sentences.en: acquiesce in others when it's appropriate.
sentences.zh: 在适当的时候又选择默许。

sentences.en: He just is thinking around these people in ways that is just like the system wasn't built to stop Moses.
sentences.zh: 他的思维方式完全绕过了这些人，就好像这个系统根本不是为了阻止摩西而设计的。

sentences.en: He just has this ability to work around it.
sentences.zh: 他就是有这种绕过系统的能力。

sentences.en: And he really does it because of, you know, the halo effect of the parks and then the halo effect of like the integrity of local governance, I guess, you know.
sentences.zh: 他之所以能做到，是因为公园带来的光环效应，以及地方治理廉洁带来的光环效应，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things that's so ironic about it is it's like we've got to support Moses because supporting Moses means supporting the independence of the New York City government.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，人们觉得我们必须支持摩西，因为支持摩西就意味着支持纽约市政府的独立性。

sentences.en: And then it's like if there's one guy who is doing an end run around the New York City government, it is Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 但如果说有一个人正在绕过纽约市政府行事，那个人就是罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: It is – he is such a – so many times I feel like throughout the book, in the public's eye,
sentences.zh: 他真是——在整本书中，我多次感觉到，在公众眼中，

sentences.en: he's the champion of the exact thing that he is not doing or the exact danger that he has.
sentences.zh: 他所捍卫的正是他自己正在破坏的东西，或者说他正是他所宣称的危险本身。

sentences.en: And it's just astounding.
sentences.zh: 这简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: He's like – it's like they put a card counter in charge of the casino and he's like, yeah, yeah,
sentences.zh: 这就好比——他们让一个算牌高手去管理赌场，而他说，没错，没错，

sentences.en: I'm just making sure nobody's counting cards around here while he's just keeping track of everything.
sentences.zh: 我只是在确保这里没有人算牌，而他自己却在暗中掌控一切。

sentences.en: And it's astonishing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: And he's going to make greater and greater use of that as we go into the next chapter.
sentences.zh: 随着我们进入下一章，他会越来越多地利用这一点。

sentences.en: Yes, the next chapter is driving.
sentences.zh: 是的，下一章是“驾驶”。

sentences.en: We'll get to that after this quick.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: So we're up to chapter 24.
sentences.zh: 现在我们读到第24章。

sentences.en: It's called driving.
sentences.zh: 这一章叫“驾驶”。

sentences.en: It's another chapter called driving.
sentences.zh: 又是一章叫“驾驶”。

sentences.en: So one of the things that I'm always impressed by about this book is the structure of it.
sentences.zh: 这本书最让我印象深刻的一点就是它的结构。

sentences.en: It's a long book and it's structured in a way that is not straightforward chronology, which can be confusing sometimes, but is often thematically illuminating.
sentences.zh: 这是一本很厚的书，它的结构并非简单的线性编年史，有时可能会让人困惑，但往往在主题上具有启发性。

sentences.en: And Caro is returning to themes and finding new layers to them or new meanings to the same words.
sentences.zh: 卡罗不断回归主题，并为它们挖掘出新的层面，或赋予同样的词汇以新的含义。

sentences.en: And it's a book that exists on a literary level in addition to existing on a historical nonfiction level.
sentences.zh: 这本书不仅是一部历史非虚构作品，在文学层面上也同样出色。

sentences.en: And so this is one of the driving chapters.
sentences.zh: 所以这是关于“驾驶”的章节之一。

sentences.en: Changing is a chapter title he likes to use.
sentences.zh: “改变”是他喜欢用的章节标题。

sentences.en: Driving is a chapter title he likes to use.
sentences.zh: “驾驶”也是他喜欢用的章节标题。

sentences.en: For some reason, the curator of Cauliflower is just a one-time title chapter.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，“花椰菜的策展人”只用过一次。

sentences.en: I would have used that one twice for sure.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会用两次。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The last line of the book should have been, truly, the curator had now been cauliflowered.
sentences.zh: 书的最后一句本该是：真的，策展人现在被花椰菜化了。

sentences.en: The Cauliflower is curating him.
sentences.zh: 花椰菜正在策展他。

sentences.en: It's a really drive-it-home, but missed opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这本该是一个强有力的结尾，可惜错失了机会。

sentences.en: It's a big book.
sentences.zh: 这是一本大部头。

sentences.en: But this is – you'd think Moses is on top of the world, right?
sentences.zh: 但你可能会觉得摩西现在处于人生巅峰，对吧？

sentences.en: But no, he's still got a rush.
sentences.zh: 不，他依然很匆忙。

sentences.en: He's always got a rush because the position he's put himself in is that if he's dependent on one thing at the moment – before, as you're saying,
sentences.zh: 他总是很匆忙，因为他所处的境地是，如果他目前依赖某样东西——正如你之前所说，

sentences.en: the triborosal bridges up really bringing in a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 三区大桥确实带来了大量收入。

sentences.en: He's dependent on that federal money, and the federal government is not ultra-reliable because whenever the economy looks like it's getting a little better,
sentences.zh: 他依赖联邦资金，而联邦政府并不十分可靠，因为每当经济看起来好转一点时，

sentences.en: the conservatives in Congress want to cut that federal money that's being poured out.
sentences.zh: 国会的保守派就想削减那些投入的联邦资金。

sentences.en: Every time the economy gets better, things get worse for Moses.
sentences.zh: 每次经济好转，摩西的处境就变糟。

sentences.en: He's – in a very real sense, his success has an inverse relationship to the economic health of the entire United States of America.
sentences.zh: 从某种现实意义上讲，他的成功与整个美国的经济健康状况成反比。

sentences.en: So he's got to work faSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须抓紧时间。

sentences.en: He can't let anyone get in his way.
sentences.zh: 他不能让任何人挡他的路。

sentences.en: And he's – because he's written his own laws that give him power, he's not beholden to some laws.
sentences.zh: 因为他自己编写了赋予他权力的法律，所以他不受某些法律的约束。

sentences.en: In other ones, he ignores them.
sentences.zh: 在其他情况下，他直接无视法律。

sentences.en: He's very big on submitting plans to be examined on the day that the construction starts or when things are almost finished.
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长在施工当天或工程快结束时才提交计划供审查。

sentences.en: He starts employing what he calls his bloodhounds who are digging up compromising personal information on reluctant officials that he can use to pressure them.
sentences.zh: 他开始雇佣他所谓的“猎犬”，去挖掘那些不配合的官员的个人丑闻，以此来要挟他们。

sentences.en: It's just out-and-out blackmail.
sentences.zh: 这完全就是赤裸裸的勒索。

sentences.en: And if a civil servant resists him and there's no blackmail material, he can use the press to smear them to make them seem like a hack who's getting in the way.
sentences.zh: 如果某个公务员抵制他，又没有把柄可抓，他就利用媒体抹黑他们，让他们看起来像个只会碍手碍脚的庸才。

sentences.en: And that didn't work against Governor Lehman because Governor Lehman is famous.
sentences.zh: 这招对莱曼州长没用，因为莱曼州长很有名。

sentences.en: Everybody knows who he is.
sentences.zh: 大家都认识他。

sentences.en: But if you're the deputy comptroller and the papers start talking about what a bad dude you are, what a troublemaker you are, there's no one knows anything about you.
sentences.zh: 但如果你只是个副审计长，报纸开始说你是个坏蛋、是个麻烦制造者，没人了解你，

sentences.en: You're going to have to – you resign because of that pressure.
sentences.zh: 你就只能因为压力而辞职。

sentences.en: And the first level of this is just like, oh, these are just namby-pamby bureaucrats who can't get anything done.
sentences.zh: 第一层面的看法是，哦，这些只是些软弱无能的官僚，什么事都干不成。

sentences.en: And I get things done.
sentences.zh: 而我能干成事。

sentences.en: And if we had to wait for this board of estimate to do something, we'll never get anything done.
sentences.zh: 如果我们非得等估算委员会来做决定，那什么事也别想干成。

sentences.en: And that gets him pretty far.
sentences.zh: 这招让他走得很远。

sentences.en: But then when that doesn't work, it gets pretty ugly.
sentences.zh: 但当这招不管用时，事情就变得很丑陋了。

sentences.en: And he's a very, very early kind of McCarthyist when it comes to labeling people as communists.
sentences.zh: 在给别人扣上“共产主义者”的帽子方面，他是一个非常、非常早期的麦卡锡主义者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Carol writes, he says, if Robert Moses was a pioneer in the fields of parks and highways, he was also a pioneer in McCarthyism 20 years before McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 卡罗写道，如果说罗伯特·摩西是公园和公路领域的先驱，那他也是麦卡锡主义的先驱，比麦卡锡早了20年。

sentences.en: This is the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪30年代。

sentences.en: And he's always already saying, this guy doesn't agree with me.
sentences.zh: 他总是已经在说，这家伙不同意我的观点。

sentences.en: He's probably a red.
sentences.zh: 他大概是个赤色分子。

sentences.en: This guy's probably a radical.
sentences.zh: 这家伙大概是个激进分子。

sentences.en: This guy's a socialiSt.
sentences.zh: 这家伙是个社会主义者。

sentences.en: And he already doesn't like the idea of a classless society.
sentences.zh: 而且他本来就不喜欢无阶级社会的概念。

sentences.en: So it's not like he's – it's like he is using his own beliefs as a weapon in a mercenary way.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像他——他就像是在以一种雇佣兵的方式，将自己的信仰当作武器。

sentences.en: And Carol tells the story of LaGuardia's law secretary, Paul J.
sentences.zh: 卡罗讲述了拉瓜迪亚的法律秘书保罗·J·克恩的故事，

sentences.en: Kern, who was kind of building the kind of relationship with LaGuardia that Moses had with Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 他与拉瓜迪亚建立的关系，就像摩西与阿尔·史密斯的关系一样。

sentences.en: And Kern likes Moses, but when he tries to keep Moses from circumventing civil service hiring regulations, the kind of laws that Moses was the champion of in his younger days,
sentences.zh: 克恩很欣赏摩西，但当他试图阻止摩西绕过公务员招聘法规时——也就是摩西年轻时曾极力倡导的那些法律，

sentences.en: Moses is like, nope.
sentences.zh: 摩西的态度是：不行。

sentences.en: And he's like, LaGuardia, Kern is saying bad things about you.
sentences.zh: 他会对拉瓜迪亚说，克恩在说你的坏话。

sentences.en: This is really terrible.
sentences.zh: 这真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Like he's just lying to him about him.
sentences.zh: 他就是在对他撒谎。

sentences.en: And then Kern says, I'm going to start a system where workers are rewarded for reporting violations in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 然后克恩说，我要建立一个系统，奖励那些举报工作场所违规行为的员工。

sentences.en: And Moses goes to the press and says, a Soviet-style secret police.
sentences.zh: 摩西就跑去媒体说，这是“苏联式的秘密警察”。

sentences.en: Well, well, I guess Kern, the communist, is causing this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，我想一定是克恩这个共产主义者在搞鬼。

sentences.en: And LaGuardia, as a New Deal Republican, is so afraid of being accused of being a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 而拉瓜迪亚作为一名新政共和党人，非常害怕被指责为共产主义者。

sentences.en: He just fires Kern.
sentences.zh: 他直接解雇了克恩。

sentences.en: And Carol notes that until Moses stopped as parks commissioner in 1960, no civil service commissioner ever interfered with his hiring practices again.
sentences.zh: 卡罗指出，直到1960年摩西卸任公园专员，再也没有公务员专员敢干涉他的招聘行为。

sentences.en: It was just clear.
sentences.zh: 这很清楚。

sentences.en: He's so good at bullying people.
sentences.zh: 他太擅长欺负人了。

sentences.en: And the only way – maybe if you're powerful enough, you can push back on him.
sentences.zh: 唯一的办法——也许如果你足够强大，你可以反击他。

sentences.en: If you stand up to him, maybe he'll back down a little bit, respect your strength.
sentences.zh: 如果你坚持立场，也许他会退缩一点，尊重你的实力。

sentences.en: But otherwise, he'll just run all over you.
sentences.zh: 但否则，他会把你踩在脚下。

sentences.en: He's supposed to have a – there's a weekly luncheon of all the commissioners on the mayor's administration.
sentences.zh: 他本该参加——市长行政部门每周都有一次所有专员的午餐会。

sentences.en: And Moses hates going to it.
sentences.zh: 但摩西讨厌参加。

sentences.en: He sees it's a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 他觉得那是浪费时间。

sentences.en: So he always sends a potted plant in his place to sit at the lunches.
sentences.zh: 所以他总是派一盆盆栽代替自己去参加午餐会。

sentences.en: And the commissioner is so mad at him, but they're afraid of doing anything about it.
sentences.zh: 专员们对他非常生气，但他们不敢对此采取任何行动。

sentences.en: And Moses would – he'd say to the other commissioners, you should designate one of your people as like an official liaison to my department.
sentences.zh: 摩西会告诉其他专员，你们应该指派一个人作为与我部门的官方联络人。

sentences.en: And then he would cultivate that worker and basically make them his mole in the other commission.
sentences.zh: 然后他会培养那个员工，基本上让他们成为他在其他委员会里的内应。

sentences.en: So he's just so good at, as you were saying before, outthinking people.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你之前所说，他非常擅长在智力上压倒别人。

sentences.en: He's good at bullying them.
sentences.zh: 他擅长欺凌他们。

sentences.en: And he's just – he's got all those techniques that we've come to know and love so well.
sentences.zh: 他就是——他掌握了所有我们已经非常熟悉和喜爱的技巧。

sentences.en: Stake driving, when you start a project before you have permission.
sentences.zh: “立桩法”，即在获得许可之前就开始项目。

sentences.en: By the time they're answering questions about it, it's too late.
sentences.zh: 等他们开始质询时，一切都太晚了。

sentences.en: It's already started.
sentences.zh: 项目已经开始了。

sentences.en: Whip sawing.
sentences.zh: “双向施压法”。

sentences.en: You go to the city and you go, oh, the federal government said I would get this money, so why don't you give me a little bit?
sentences.zh: 你去找市政府说，哦，联邦政府说会给我这笔钱，所以你们为什么不给我一点呢？

sentences.en: And then he goes to the federal government and says, oh, the city is going to give me this money, so why don't you give me the rest of it?
sentences.zh: 然后他去找联邦政府说，哦，市政府要给我这笔钱，所以你们为什么不把剩下的补齐呢？

sentences.en: He doesn't have the money, but he's telling both sides that he has it.
sentences.zh: 他其实并没有钱，但他告诉双方他都有。

sentences.en: Wedge driving.
sentences.zh: “楔入法”。

sentences.en: You go, can I have a little bit of money?
sentences.zh: 你问，我能要一点钱吗？

sentences.en: Okay, that's all it's going to take.
sentences.zh: 好，只需要这么多。

sentences.en: And then a year later, I'm going to need more money.
sentences.zh: 然后一年后，我还需要更多钱。

sentences.en: You have to give it to me now.
sentences.zh: 你现在必须给我。

sentences.en: And deception.
sentences.zh: 还有欺骗。

sentences.en: He just lies about things.
sentences.zh: 他只是在撒谎。

sentences.en: If he's told don't do something, he starts doing it.
sentences.zh: 如果有人告诉他别做什么，他偏要去做。

sentences.en: He wants to build a marine park in Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 他想在布鲁克林建一个海洋公园。

sentences.en: He goes, I need $6 million.
sentences.zh: 他会说，我需要600万美元。

sentences.en: That's the whole coSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是全部成本。

sentences.en: And then when that's spent, he goes, I need another $6 million.
sentences.zh: 等这笔钱花完了，他又会说，我还需要600万美元。

sentences.en: You're going to let that last $6 million go to waste?
sentences.zh: 难道你要让那600万美元白白浪费掉吗？

sentences.en: Because you didn't check that what I was telling you was true?
sentences.zh: 就因为你没去核实我告诉你的话是否属实？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: If you want to tell the people of the city that you got tricked by Moses again, it's such trickster rabbit type stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果你想告诉市民们你又被摩西骗了，这简直是骗子惯用的把戏。

sentences.en: The favorite one is when he wants to build a stadium on Randall's Island and he goes to the board of the city, the board of investment.
sentences.zh: 最典型的例子是他想在兰德尔岛建体育场，于是他去找市里的董事会，也就是投资委员会。

sentences.en: He goes, the WPA is going to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 他说，工程进度管理局（WPA）会出钱。

sentences.en: I don't need any money from the city.
sentences.zh: 我不需要市里出一分钱。

sentences.en: Well, I need $250,000, but that's all the money that the entire Triborough project is going to cost the city.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我需要25万美元，但这已经是整个三区大桥项目需要市里承担的全部费用了。

sentences.en: And then he comes back and he goes, I need $8 million.
sentences.zh: 然后他回来又说，我需要800万美元。

sentences.en: And he goes, I didn't mean the land for the approach roads to the bridge.
sentences.zh: 他说，我指的不是通往大桥引道的土地。

sentences.en: You were foolish when I said the whole project.
sentences.zh: 当我提到整个项目时，是你们太愚蠢了。

sentences.en: You thought I meant everything in the project.
sentences.zh: 你们以为我指的是项目里的所有东西。

sentences.en: And if they push back on him, he is abusive.
sentences.zh: 如果有人反驳他，他就会进行辱骂。

sentences.en: He is verbally abusive in the way he was to crowds.
sentences.zh: 他言语上的辱骂方式和他对待人群时如出一辙。

sentences.en: And the crowds wouldn't take it.
sentences.zh: 而大众是不会忍受这种辱骂的。

sentences.en: But these individuals will in these smaller rooms, even though ostensibly they have more power than he does, but really he has more power than they do.
sentences.zh: 但在这些小房间里，这些人却会忍气吞声，尽管表面上他们的权力比他大，但实际上他的权力比他们更大。

sentences.en: He's the power broker.
sentences.zh: 他才是真正的权力掮客。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is just like becomes his source of power is that he does not care about people.
sentences.zh: 这成了他权力的来源，因为他根本不在乎人。

sentences.en: He will destroy them.
sentences.zh: 他会摧毁他们。

sentences.en: He will destroy, you know, like these sort of somewhat nameless bureaucrats inside these organizations, these somewhat more named commissioners.
sentences.zh: 他会摧毁那些组织里无名的小官僚，以及那些稍微有点名气的专员。

sentences.en: And but but he really does not care about the humans inside of a city at all.
sentences.zh: 但他确实一点也不关心城市里的普通人。

sentences.en: There's an enormous strength in being able to rewrite the rules to your liking, but also in having the freedom to ignore the rules.
sentences.zh: 能够按照自己的意愿重写规则，以及拥有无视规则的自由，这本身就是一种巨大的力量。

sentences.en: Like every now and then there it feels like someone comes along and people like this guy is playing chess on a whole nother level.
sentences.zh: 就像偶尔会有人出现，让人们觉得这家伙是在另一个层面上玩国际象棋。

sentences.en: Like he's out thinking everybody and their secret is just that they're being bad, just refusing to play by the rules of the game.
sentences.zh: 他似乎比所有人都想得远，而他们的秘诀仅仅是他们够坏，拒绝遵守游戏规则。

sentences.en: You can win a monopoly if you're allowed to rob the other players and, you know, and like just throw free hotels onto your properties.
sentences.zh: 如果你被允许抢劫其他玩家，并且可以随意在你的地盘上加盖免费酒店，那你当然能在《大富翁》里赢。

sentences.en: Like that's, you know, if you don't play by the rules, it's a lot easier to win the game.
sentences.zh: 这就是说，如果你不按规则出牌，赢游戏就容易多了。

sentences.en: And that's what he does.
sentences.zh: 而他就是这么做的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he's also built up his sort of like portfolio of accomplishments in these places like Long Island where there are fewer people to get angry, you know, like, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且他还在长岛这些地方积累了一系列成就，因为那里没多少人会生气，你知道的，你知道，

sentences.en: these places like mostly that that land was empty land.
sentences.zh: 这些地方大部分土地都是空地。

sentences.en: It was owned by someone.
sentences.zh: 它们是有主人的。

sentences.en: Maybe there's the occasional farmer that, you know, he destroys without any regard.
sentences.zh: 也许偶尔会有个农民，他会毫不留情地将其摧毁。

sentences.en: Just the occasional small farmer, the occasional wealthy baron he has to accommodate slightly, you know.
sentences.zh: 只是偶尔有个小农场主，或者偶尔有个他必须稍微迁就一下的富豪，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah, but but now he's, you know, he's building all this stuff in densely populated New York City where, you know,
sentences.zh: 是啊，但现在他是在人口稠密的纽约市大兴土木，你知道，

sentences.en: these things have a big effect on what what's going to happen in these people's lives.
sentences.zh: 这些事情对这些人的生活会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And it's just causing a bit of complication.
sentences.zh: 这确实造成了一些麻烦。

sentences.en: And he's like he's like a startup or something like he needs to go at that same rate of increase.
sentences.zh: 他就像一家初创公司，他需要保持同样的增长速度。

sentences.en: He he's just sort of like required to go at like maybe just some kind of personal ambition,
sentences.zh: 他只是被迫要继续前进，也许仅仅是出于某种个人野心，

sentences.en: like where he notices the rules are changing and the easy land where he can grow has now been exploited to to the extent that that it can be.
sentences.zh: 他注意到规则正在改变，而他可以轻松扩张的土地已经被开发到了极限。

sentences.en: And he and he has to keep now he has to work in like in these neighborhoods that are more complicated and where you cannot just lay down Jones Beach because nothing is there.
sentences.zh: 他现在必须在更复杂的社区工作，不能再像在琼斯海滩那样随心所欲地铺路，因为那里本来什么都没有。

sentences.en: It's like now there's lots of stuff there.
sentences.zh: 现在那里已经有很多东西了。

sentences.en: Yeah, the secret to his success was was finding unused land and taking advantage of it.
sentences.zh: 没错，他成功的秘诀就是寻找未使用的土地并加以利用。

sentences.en: And Carol makes a big talks a lot about this here that you can't do that in New York City.
sentences.zh: 卡罗在这里谈了很多，说你在纽约市是做不到这一点的。

sentences.en: You can't.
sentences.zh: 你做不到。

sentences.en: It's a it's a it's a city.
sentences.zh: 这毕竟是一座城市。

sentences.en: And he compares building on Long Island to painting on a blank canvas.
sentences.zh: 他把在长岛建设比作在空白画布上作画。

sentences.en: And he compares building in New York City to painting in a mural that already exists.
sentences.zh: 而他把在纽约市建设比作在现有的壁画上作画。

sentences.en: And he has this very beautiful section about kind of describing the mural and that these I'll read you just a little bit of that.
sentences.zh: 他有一段非常优美的文字描述了这幅壁画，我给你读一小段。

sentences.en: It goes because a mural whose brush strokes were tiny and intricate and often when one looked closely quite wonderful lending to the vast urban panorama subtle shadings and delicate tints and an endless variety so that if it was crowded and confused and ugly,
sentences.zh: 它写道，因为这幅壁画的笔触细微而复杂，当你仔细观察时，往往会发现它非常美妙，为广阔的城市全景增添了微妙的阴影、精致的色彩和无穷的变化，所以即使它显得拥挤、混乱且丑陋，

sentences.en: it was also full of life and very human.
sentences.zh: 它也充满了生命力，非常人性化。

sentences.en: So much so, in fact, that while the painting as a whole might lack beauty, order, balance, perspective, a unifying principle and an overall effect commensurate with its size.
sentences.zh: 事实上，尽管这幅画整体上可能缺乏美感、秩序、平衡、透视、统一原则以及与其规模相称的整体效果，

sentences.en: It nonetheless possessed many charming little touches and an overall vitality, a brio that made it unique and should not be loSt.
sentences.zh: 但它依然拥有许多迷人的小细节和一种整体的活力，一种使其独一无二且不应丢失的生机。

sentences.en: I think that's so beautiful, the idea of New York as this really messy piece of work.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太美了，把纽约看作一件非常杂乱的作品的构思。

sentences.en: And the closer you get to it, the more you see the beautiful details in it and the things you don't want to lose.
sentences.zh: 你离它越近，就越能看到其中美丽的细节，以及那些你不想失去的东西。

sentences.en: But all Moses can see is the full canvas.
sentences.zh: 但摩西眼里看到的只有整块画布。

sentences.en: And he's like, well, let's put a road here.
sentences.zh: 他会说，好吧，在这里修条路吧。

sentences.en: Sport just puts a huge thing of paint over people's homes, lives, neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 他只是在人们的家园、生活和社区上涂抹了一大块颜料。

sentences.en: And comparing it to a startup is such a good parallel because often a startup will – their whole point is they're doing a new thing that hasn't been done before.
sentences.zh: 把它比作初创公司是一个很好的类比，因为初创公司的全部意义往往在于他们在做一件前所未有的新事。

sentences.en: And maybe they have to move fast or maybe they have to kind of overreach because nobody's done this thing before.
sentences.zh: 也许他们必须快速行动，或者因为没人做过这件事，他们不得不有些越界。

sentences.en: And it feels like so many of those companies, when they get big, they are like, well,
sentences.zh: 感觉很多这样的公司，当它们做大之后，它们就会觉得，好吧，

sentences.en: the only way to grow now is to take over something that already exists or to take its customer base and then monetize that.
sentences.zh: 现在唯一的增长方式就是接管现有的东西，或者获取其客户群，然后将其货币化。

sentences.en: And they stop being their customers and start being their product for larger companies.
sentences.zh: 他们不再是客户，而是成了大公司眼中的产品。

sentences.en: And it feels like Moses is doing pretty much that.
sentences.zh: 感觉摩西做的也差不多是这样。

sentences.en: He's like, the thing that I did here, I have to do it bigger.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，我在这里做过的事，我必须做得更大。

sentences.en: And I did it in theory.
sentences.zh: 而且我理论上做到了。

sentences.en: I built these parks for people to come and enjoy.
sentences.zh: 我建造了这些公园供人们前来享受。

sentences.en: Now I have a place that's full of people,
sentences.zh: 现在我有一个挤满人的地方，

sentences.en: and I'm going to build roads for the people who live outside of this community for their convenience to a great extent and not for the people who are in it.
sentences.zh: 我要为社区外的人修建道路，在很大程度上是为了他们的方便，而不是为了社区里的人。

sentences.en: The people who ostensibly are my customers, they are now my – if not a product, exactly an obstacle.
sentences.zh: 那些表面上是我的客户的人，现在成了我的——如果不是产品，那也绝对是障碍。

sentences.en: Well, you had a really great parallel, and I really messed it up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你之前那个类比真的很棒，结果被我搞砸了。

sentences.en: I really got – made it – I really found out how to overcomplicate that, much like a beautiful mural that maybe in the aggregate is messy.
sentences.zh: 我真的——把它弄得——我发现自己把它过度复杂化了，就像一幅美丽的壁画，整体上可能很杂乱。

sentences.en: But there's lots of little points that are still beautiful.
sentences.zh: 但仍有许多小地方依然很美。

sentences.en: And Carol talks about how in Long Island, you can open up land to public development by running a road there.
sentences.zh: 卡罗谈到在长岛，你可以通过修路来开发土地供公众使用。

sentences.en: But in a city, if you open up land that hasn't been fully developed before the city is prepared to provide the services that a city provides to a neighborhood,
sentences.zh: 但在城市里，如果你在城市准备好提供社区服务之前就开发了尚未完全开发的土地，

sentences.en: then it's going to lead to a mess.
sentences.zh: 那只会导致一团糟。

sentences.en: And Carol bounces a little bit.
sentences.zh: 卡罗对此做了一些反思。

sentences.en: He says that Moses' drive, his drive to get things done, the very driving that is the title of this chapter,
sentences.zh: 他说摩西的干劲，他把事情做成的动力，正是本章标题所指的“干劲”，

sentences.en: and his ability to cut through red tape and to force things are not necessarily bad, and they're not necessarily unneeded, that a city needs to build big things.
sentences.zh: 以及他打破官僚作风和强行推进事物的能力，并不一定就是坏事，也不一定是不需要的，因为城市确实需要建设宏大的工程。

sentences.en: It needs to get them done.
sentences.zh: 它需要把事情做成。

sentences.en: It needs to have someone whose ability to get them done is, if not unquestioned at least, is very – a high level.
sentences.zh: 它需要一个办事能力极强的人，即使不是无可置疑，至少也是高水平的。

sentences.en: It needs someone who's able to make these things, but it needs to include humanity into those decisions.
sentences.zh: 它需要一个能建成这些东西的人，但这些决策必须包含人性。

sentences.en: It needs to include an understanding of the smaller groups of people, and Moses either cannot think on that smaller granular scale or just doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 它需要包含对小群体人们的理解，而摩西要么无法在那种细微的层面上思考，要么就是根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Like the scale of a single neighborhood is – means nothing to a guy who is now used to building only enormous things.
sentences.zh: 对于一个习惯了只建造庞然大物的人来说，单个社区的规模对他而言毫无意义。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: He can go to that neighborhood and say, what do you need?
sentences.zh: 他本可以去那个社区问问，你们需要什么？

sentences.en: What's the best thing about this?
sentences.zh: 这里最好的地方是什么？

sentences.en: But he doesn't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 但他不想那样做。

sentences.en: Like he doesn't care, and he's also so focused on the idea of active recreation because he is an active guy.
sentences.zh: 他不在乎，而且他太专注于积极娱乐的概念，因为他自己就是一个活跃的人。

sentences.en: He likes to swim.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢游泳。

sentences.en: He likes to do things.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢做事。

sentences.en: That the idea of peaceful conservation, a place for someone to sit or a place for someone to be in the shade of a tree, someone who's not just driving a car or something,
sentences.zh: 所以对于安静的保护，比如给人们一个坐的地方，或者给人们一个在树荫下休息的地方，给那些不是在开车的人一个空间，

sentences.en: that's uninteresting to him.
sentences.zh: 他对此毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: He's not interested in preserving things.
sentences.zh: 他没兴趣保护任何东西。

sentences.en: He's interested in building things.
sentences.zh: 他只对建造东西感兴趣。

sentences.en: There's a certain level at Moses' character where he can't point to a forest that he's preserved and be like, look at that.
sentences.zh: 摩西的性格中有一个层面，他无法指着一片他保护的森林说，看那个。

sentences.en: Isn't that an achievement?
sentences.zh: 那不是一项成就吗？

sentences.en: Because it's not.
sentences.zh: 因为那不是他做的。

sentences.en: To him, he's like, I didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，他会想，那又不是我做的。

sentences.en: I guess God built that.
sentences.zh: 我想那是上帝造的。

sentences.en: I want to build something.
sentences.zh: 我想造点什么。

sentences.en: I'm going to put a stadium there.
sentences.zh: 我要在那里建个体育场。

sentences.en: I'm going to put a bandshell.
sentences.zh: 我要建个露天舞台。

sentences.en: I'm going to put something I can put my name on.
sentences.zh: 我要建个能刻上我名字的东西。

sentences.en: He's really interested in building big things.
sentences.zh: 他真的只对建造宏大的东西感兴趣。

sentences.en: And when you have this mural of intricate brushstrokes, like little things matter.
sentences.zh: 当你面对这幅有着复杂笔触的壁画时，小细节是很重要的。

sentences.en: Like each of those brushstrokes matter.
sentences.zh: 每一个笔触都很重要。

sentences.en: And like a tiny park that's only two acres matters a lot to the people right near there.
sentences.zh: 比如一个只有两英亩的小公园，对附近的人来说意义重大。

sentences.en: And it just does not matter to Moses.
sentences.zh: 但这对摩西来说根本不重要。

sentences.en: Like when Caro talks about a kind of planning genius that he witnessed where he holds his hand out and gets a rolled up map and he rolls it out and he starts drawing on it.
sentences.zh: 当卡罗谈到他所见证的那种规划天才时，他伸出手，拿出一张卷起来的地图，摊开，然后开始在上面画画。

sentences.en: He sees big things really, really well.
sentences.zh: 他确实非常擅长处理宏大的事物。

sentences.en: But he's very, very blind to small things.
sentences.zh: 但他对细微的事物却非常非常盲目。

sentences.en: And I think it's because there's something wrong with his soul.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是因为他的灵魂出了点问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm going to be a little bit nicer to him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我会对他稍微客气一点。

sentences.en: I'm going to play devil's advocate again.
sentences.zh: 我又要扮演魔鬼代言人了。

sentences.en: I'm going to say that it's a sort of like – I think it's called what?
sentences.zh: 我想说这是一种——我想这叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Hedonic adaptation or something where the standard that was new and exciting before becomes normal to you now.
sentences.zh: 享乐适应症之类的，就是以前觉得新鲜刺激的标准，现在对你来说变得习以为常了。

sentences.en: And I think as he's been working on these larger and larger scale things, he has – he just doesn't connect with that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我觉得随着他处理越来越大规模的项目，他已经——他只是不再与那些细微的东西产生共鸣了。

sentences.en: That's normal to him.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这很正常。

sentences.en: It's normal to him to build a road that displaces thousands of people or to tear up buildings and not care about the people who are there because he's just gotten so used to it.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，修建一条导致成千上万流离失所的道路，或者拆毁建筑而不关心那里的人，这都很正常，因为他已经习惯了。

sentences.en: And there are all these choices that need to be made when it comes to a project and especially a public work.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到一个项目，尤其是公共工程时，需要做出各种选择。

sentences.en: Who is it serving?
sentences.zh: 它服务于谁？

sentences.en: How is it serving them?
sentences.zh: 它是如何服务他们的？

sentences.en: What needs need to be met?
sentences.zh: 需要满足什么需求？

sentences.en: What needs can't be met?
sentences.zh: 哪些需求无法满足？

sentences.en: If the nature of driving is different, if it's not about leisure anymore, if it's about going from point A to point B,
sentences.zh: 如果驾驶的本质变了，如果不再是为了休闲，而是为了从A点到B点，

sentences.en: why should the best scenery be preserved for people in cars instead of people on foot?
sentences.zh: 为什么最好的风景要留给开车的人，而不是步行的人？

sentences.en: And what kind of park does a neighborhood need rather than what kind of park does Robert Moses feel like building?
sentences.zh: 社区需要什么样的公园，而不是罗伯特·摩西想建什么样的公园？

sentences.en: And all that stuff needs to be discussed, but Moses is not interested in discussing things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都需要讨论，但摩西对讨论这些没兴趣。

sentences.en: And where he used to like kind of spar with his staff a little bit and let them challenge him slightly when it came to ideas, and he would push them to do their beSt.
sentences.zh: 他过去还会和下属争论一番，让他们在创意上挑战自己，他会鞭策他们做到最好。

sentences.en: Now he just doesn't care about other people's opinions, and he's surrounded himself by yes-men who whatever RM says, that's what it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 现在他根本不在乎别人的意见，他身边全是唯唯诺诺的人，无论RM说什么，就得按那个办。

sentences.en: And Caro, he continues this, I think in a very nice and very subtle way, he continues this metaphor of or analogy, I don't know, I'm not an English professor,
sentences.zh: 卡罗，他继续这样写，我觉得用一种非常优美且微妙的方式，他继续使用这个隐喻或类比，我不知道，我不是英语教授，

sentences.en: this whatever it is of Moses as an artist by saying how Moses has cut himself off from new information and new ideas.
sentences.zh: 无论这是什么，他通过说摩西如何切断了与新信息和新思想的联系，来描述摩西作为艺术家的形象。

sentences.en: His understanding of himself as the master builder stands between him and the world,
sentences.zh: 他作为“建筑大师”的自我认知，横亘在他与世界之间，

sentences.en: and he could overcome this obstacle maybe if he was giving the work he was doing the kind of deep sustained thought that he used to.
sentences.zh: 如果他能像过去那样，对他所做的工作进行深入、持续的思考，他或许能克服这个障碍。

sentences.en: When he was spending hours tromping through Long Island, tromping around the city, thinking of ideas, looking at real life,
sentences.zh: 当他花几个小时在长岛跋涉，在城市里奔走，构思创意，观察现实生活时，

sentences.en: and thinking about how to fix it instead of just looking at maps.
sentences.zh: 他思考的是如何解决问题，而不是仅仅盯着地图看。

sentences.en: And he can't do that anymore.
sentences.zh: 但他现在做不到了。

sentences.en: He doesn't have the time.
sentences.zh: 他没时间了。

sentences.en: He's taken on so much work.
sentences.zh: 他承担了太多的工作。

sentences.en: He's overloaded.
sentences.zh: 他超负荷了。

sentences.en: He's doing all the New York City parks.
sentences.zh: 他负责所有的纽约市公园。

sentences.en: He's doing the Long Island parks.
sentences.zh: 他还要负责长岛的公园。

sentences.en: He's building the state parkways.
sentences.zh: 他正在修建州立公园大道。

sentences.en: He's building his dam work in Niagara.
sentences.zh: 他正在尼亚加拉进行大坝工程。

sentences.en: He's added so much work that – Caro mentions this, but he doesn't go into detail that he nearly has a nervous breakdown by the end of 1934 that he's so overworked.
sentences.zh: 他增加了如此多的工作量——卡罗提到了这一点，但没有详述——以至于到1934年底，他因过度劳累几乎精神崩溃。

sentences.en: And he cannot give his attention to each of these projects, and so they're starting to become banal.
sentences.zh: 他无法顾及每一个项目，所以这些项目开始变得平庸。

sentences.en: Instead of making individual decisions, he has a standardized form that just gets reused.
sentences.zh: 他不再做出个性化的决策，而是采用了一套可以反复使用的标准化模板。

sentences.en: And that like a great artist who loses connection with the reality, with the real world and only knows art,
sentences.zh: 就像一位伟大的艺术家失去了与现实、与真实世界的联系，只懂得艺术一样，

sentences.en: his work starts to become a repetition or a comment on itself rather than something that really relates to the lives and needs and emotions of people.
sentences.zh: 他的作品开始变成一种重复，或者说是对自己的一种注脚，而不是真正与人们的生活、需求和情感相关联的东西。

sentences.en: And it's something that happens to anyone who's in a sort of creative field.
sentences.zh: 这是任何从事创意领域工作的人都会遇到的问题。

sentences.en: And Moses is very much working in a creative way.
sentences.zh: 而摩西在很大程度上是以一种创造性的方式在工作。

sentences.en: It happens to anyone who only knows their own bubble and doesn't really ever get out of it and see the outside world.
sentences.zh: 这会发生在任何只了解自己圈子，从未走出去看看外部世界的人身上。

sentences.en: And you see a lot in the way that like movie makers at a certain point start making movies that feel more like they're about other movies than they – or standup comedians will start doing jokes about ordinary life.
sentences.zh: 你会发现很多电影制作人在某个阶段开始制作那些看起来更像是关于电影本身的电影，或者脱口秀演员开始讲关于普通生活的笑话。

sentences.en: And then if they get famous enough, all their routines become about being a famous person and what it's like to be famous.
sentences.zh: 如果他们变得足够出名，他们所有的段子就都变成了关于如何成为名人以及当名人是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Or he's pointed out to me once that if you read Stephen King's books in order,
sentences.zh: 或者他曾向我指出，如果你按顺序阅读斯蒂芬·金的书，

sentences.en: the characters go from being kind of like blue-collar ordinary people to being like writers and then college professors.
sentences.zh: 角色会从蓝领普通人变成作家，然后是大学教授。

sentences.en: Like it's – which at one point – to a certain point makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上是有道理的。

sentences.en: You lose touch with that part of your history, and so you're no longer inspired by it.
sentences.zh: 你失去了与那段历史的联系，所以你不再从中获得灵感。

sentences.en: But it means that – I'm not saying this about Stephen King.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着——我不是在说斯蒂芬·金。

sentences.en: He still comes out with great work.
sentences.zh: 他依然能创作出伟大的作品。

sentences.en: But that Robert Moses' work is less and less connected to reality and more and more just connected to his pre-conceived notions about what a park is.
sentences.zh: 但罗伯特·摩西的作品与现实的联系越来越少，而与他关于公园应该是什么样子的先入之见联系得越来越多。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Like it hasn't evolved much at all.
sentences.zh: 就像它几乎没有什么进化一样。

sentences.en: Like he had some good ideas in the beginning, and he had the canvas to make it.
sentences.zh: 他起初有一些好点子，也有实现这些点子的蓝图。

sentences.en: He had the ingenuity to make it all happen.
sentences.zh: 他有实现这一切的独创性。

sentences.en: And now that's not available, but his ideas have not modified or changed at all.
sentences.zh: 现在这些条件不再具备，但他的想法却一点也没有修正或改变。

sentences.en: Like the city has changed a lot, but he hasn't changed.
sentences.zh: 城市已经发生了很大的变化，但他没有变。

sentences.en: And therefore, it's just like he's not interested in solving these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就像他根本没兴趣解决这些问题一样。

sentences.en: He's not interested in the details.
sentences.zh: 他不关心细节。

sentences.en: He's not interested in providing gaiety to people who arrive at these parks like he did when Jones Beach was being designed.
sentences.zh: 他不像设计琼斯海滩时那样，有兴趣为来到这些公园的人们提供快乐。

sentences.en: It just is like he has the most power he's ever had to get things done.
sentences.zh: 这就像他拥有了有史以来最大的权力来完成事情。

sentences.en: And his disconnect with the job he's doing is so much greater that it makes like more of this just messy, thoughtless, you know, even cruel decisions are being made.
sentences.zh: 但他与所做工作的脱节程度之大，导致更多混乱、草率，甚至可以说是残酷的决策被做出。

sentences.en: Yeah, and we'll see – in later chapters, we'll see how he's really destroying people's lives through his construction of work.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们会在后面的章节中看到，他是如何通过他的工程建设真正摧毁人们的生活的。

sentences.en: But there are even little things that Caro mentions here.
sentences.zh: 但卡罗在这里提到的甚至是一些小事。

sentences.en: He mentions how he uses the same design for parks in the city that he would use for parks in Long Island where people are going to drive to the parks rather than – small parks and playgrounds.
sentences.zh: 他提到摩西在城市里使用的公园设计，竟然和他在长岛使用的完全一样，而长岛的人们是开车去公园的——那些小公园和游乐场。

sentences.en: So he has steps where in the city, if you're a parent with a baby – Caro says mothers because this book was written 50 years ago, but I would say parents.
sentences.zh: 所以他设计了台阶，在城市里，如果你是一个带着婴儿的家长——卡罗说是母亲，因为这本书是50年前写的，但我会说是家长。

sentences.en: Now, if you're pushing your baby in a baby carriage or a stroller, you've got to deal with all these steps because in a Long Island park,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你推着婴儿车，你就得应付这些台阶，因为在长岛的公园里，

sentences.en: you drive your kid there in a car and you just take them out and carry them around where they walk.
sentences.zh: 你是开车带孩子去那里，把他们抱出来，然后让他们自己走。

sentences.en: But in the city, you need to be pushing a carriage.
sentences.zh: 但在城市里，你需要推着婴儿车。

sentences.en: And it means that these – it's just a small instance of these parks are not being designed for the people who are actually using them because Moses is just repeating the same things he's been doing over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这意味着——这只是一个小例子，说明这些公园的设计并没有考虑到真正使用它们的人，因为摩西只是在重复他一直以来所做的事情。

sentences.en: Much like you hear it a lot with chefs, I guess, when they open a restaurant and they're like, oh, it's just the same slate of dishes they've been doing for years.
sentences.zh: 就像你经常听到厨师那样，我想，当他们开一家餐馆时，他们提供的还是多年来一成不变的菜品。

sentences.en: Where's the new ideas?
sentences.zh: 创新的想法在哪里？

sentences.en: And part of that is also you can do more whimsical stuff outside of a city than you can in a city.
sentences.zh: 部分原因也是因为在城市之外，你可以做更多异想天开的事情，而在城市里则不行。

sentences.en: And Caro talks about how the early Central Park playgrounds when Moses was redoing Central Park were much more whimsical,
sentences.zh: 卡罗谈到摩西重修中央公园时，早期的中央公园游乐场要异想天开得多，

sentences.en: but it meant you had all these kind of hidden spaces for animals or perverts to do what they wanted to do with the space, which was not great, which was not what needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着你会有各种隐藏的空间，让动物或变态者利用这些空间做他们想做的事，这并不好，也不是当时所需要的。

sentences.en: And Caro's style throughout this section is a little repetitive but I think in a way that's purposeful where he is giving you slight variations on kind of similar ideas about Moses' limitations here,
sentences.zh: 卡罗在这一部分的文风有点重复，但我认为这是有目的的，他通过对摩西局限性的类似观点给出细微的变化，

sentences.en: almost as if he is also laying down brush stroke after brush stroke, layers of paint to kind of build up this argument in your mind until by the end of the chapter,
sentences.zh: 几乎就像他也在一笔一笔地涂抹，一层一层地刷漆，在你的脑海中构建这个论点，直到章节结束时，

sentences.en: you fully understand what he's talking about rather than just stating it and then moving on.
sentences.zh: 你完全理解他在说什么，而不是仅仅陈述一遍就继续往下写。

sentences.en: He's really hammering it home and the thing that he starts to hammer home here, which we'll talk about in even more depth next episode,
sentences.zh: 他真的在反复强调这一点，而他在这里开始强调的事情，我们将在下一集更深入地讨论，

sentences.en: is that Moses is not just uninterested in individual neighborhoods and how individuals react.
sentences.zh: 那就是摩西不仅对个别社区和个人的反应不感兴趣。

sentences.en: He's particularly personally uninterested in a certain type of person and that person is, for lack of a better word, poor and that type of person is, for lack of a better word,
sentences.zh: 他特别对某种特定的人不感兴趣，用一个词来形容，就是穷人，而这类人，用一个词来形容，

sentences.en: black or Puerto Rican.
sentences.zh: 就是黑人或波多黎各人。

sentences.en: He's making the point that there are all these opportunities to build these small parks in slum areas and areas where people don't have money or in areas where there is a majority non-white population.
sentences.zh: 他指出，在贫民窟地区、人们没有钱的地区或非白人人口占多数的地区，有这么多建造小公园的机会。

sentences.en: And the black population of the city has grown very quickly.
sentences.zh: 而城市的黑人人口增长非常迅速。

sentences.en: In 1900, it's 60,000 people.
In 1940, right after the period we're talking about now, it's 458,000 people.
sentences.zh: 1940年，就在我们现在讨论的时期之后，有45.8万人。

sentences.en: And that part of the city's population, those residents, are shut out of much of the mainstream of economic and recreational life.
sentences.zh: 而城市人口的那一部分，那些居民，被排除在大部分主流经济和娱乐生活之外。

sentences.en: They do not have the things that the rest of the city is taking for granted now that Moses is sprinkling parks and playgrounds all over the place.
sentences.zh: 他们没有城市其他地方现在认为理所当然的东西，而摩西正在到处撒播公园和游乐场。

sentences.en: And these are people who feel unwelcome in the parts of the city that now have parks and playgrounds.
sentences.zh: 这些人感到在城市里那些现在拥有公园和游乐场的地方并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: They need places to play.
sentences.zh: 他们需要玩耍的地方。

sentences.en: And we're going to talk about this more in the next chapter because Carol brings it up in more detail.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下一章讨论这个问题，因为卡罗提到了更多细节。

sentences.en: But Moses is not interested in providing those services to them, in providing their children with places to play.
sentences.zh: 但摩西对为他们提供这些服务，为他们的孩子提供玩耍的地方不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And this means that the kids in those areas are forced to play in the streets, play in places that are not safe for them, that are dirty or dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这些地区的孩子被迫在街上玩耍，在对他们不安全、肮脏或危险的地方玩耍。

sentences.en: But it sends the message to that large part of the city's population that the city does not care about them.
sentences.zh: 但这向城市中那大部分人口传达了一个信息：这座城市并不关心他们。

sentences.en: And the reformers who are now kind of turning on Moses slightly, a little bit at a time,
sentences.zh: 而那些现在开始稍微有点反对摩西的改革者们，

sentences.en: they see that Moses has effectively barred poor black New Yorkers from his parks through their lack of public transportation going to them.
sentences.zh: 他们看到摩西通过缺乏公共交通，有效地将贫穷的黑人纽约人挡在了他的公园之外。

sentences.en: And now he won't even provide little parks in their neighborhoods for them.
sentences.zh: 现在他甚至不愿在他们的社区里为他们提供小公园。

sentences.en: He's just not interested in doing it.
sentences.zh: 他就是没兴趣做这件事。

sentences.en: And Moses pushbacks a little bit, and he says, well, they can always go to Randall's Island or Riverside Park.
sentences.zh: 摩西稍微反驳了一下，他说，好吧，他们总是可以去兰德尔岛或河滨公园。

sentences.en: And he also says, eh, the smallest a park should be is three acres.
sentences.zh: 他还说，呃，公园最小应该有三英亩。

sentences.en: It's not really financial sense to make a park that's smaller than three acres.
sentences.zh: 建造小于三英亩的公园在经济上并不划算。

sentences.en: And the reformers are like, eh, but you could make one that's smaller than three acres.
sentences.zh: 而改革者们说，呃，但你可以建一个小于三英亩的。

sentences.en: It would be nice.
sentences.zh: 那会很不错。

sentences.en: You could do it.
sentences.zh: 你可以做到的。

sentences.en: It's possible.
sentences.zh: 这是可能的。

sentences.en: And also that because Moses doesn't want bus service to Randall's Island, where he has these facilities he says that black New Yorkers can go to,
sentences.zh: 而且因为摩西不想提供去兰德尔岛的公交服务，而他声称黑人纽约人可以去那里使用他拥有的这些设施，

sentences.en: it means that to get there from Harlem or the South Bronx, where much of New York's black population is centered,
sentences.zh: 这意味着从哈莱姆区或南布朗克斯区——纽约大部分黑人人口集中的地方——去那里，

sentences.en: you have to walk anywhere from three quarters of a mile to two miles.
sentences.zh: 你必须步行四分之三英里到两英里不等。

sentences.en: And it's – that's an insane idea to say that, yeah, they've got park facilities.
sentences.zh: 这——说他们有公园设施简直是疯了。

sentences.en: They just have to walk two miles to get to them in one of the most crowded cities in the United States of America because it's not like it's a pleasant walk for all that time.
sentences.zh: 他们得走两英里才能到达，这还是在美国最拥挤的城市之一，因为那段路程并不总是令人愉快的步行。

sentences.en: I mean, to be honest, I like walking through cities.
sentences.zh: 我是说，老实说，我喜欢在城市里散步。

sentences.en: So it would be – I mean, in some ways it's a pleasant walk.
sentences.zh: 所以这——我是说，在某些方面这是一种愉快的散步。

sentences.en: But they're not walking through the best areas probably.
sentences.zh: 但他们可能不是走在最好的区域。

sentences.en: You don't do it daily after school.
sentences.zh: 你不会每天放学后都这么做。

sentences.en: You don't walk two miles to get to a park.
sentences.zh: 你不会为了去公园走两英里路。

sentences.en: Or on a weekend when you've been working all week and your children want to go play.
sentences.zh: 或者在周末，当你工作了一整周，孩子们想去玩的时候。

sentences.en: It's hard to get up to – and you have to bring – I mean, if you've gone – you've gone plays with children, Roman.
sentences.zh: 很难动身——而且你必须带上——我是说，如果你去过——你和孩子们一起玩过，罗曼。

sentences.en: You've got to bring food with you.
sentences.zh: 你得带上食物。

sentences.en: You've got to bring stuff for them to do.
sentences.zh: 你得带上让他们玩的东西。

sentences.en: It's like the storming of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 这就像诺曼底登陆一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it sucks.
sentences.zh: 是的，糟透了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's the worSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Bringing children anywhere.
sentences.zh: 带孩子去任何地方。

sentences.en: And the press will – they'll print the letters to the editor from these reformers about this stuff.
sentences.zh: 媒体会——他们会刊登这些改革者关于此事的致编辑信。

sentences.en: But they'll also print Moses' rebuttals and they won't put their editorial support, the idea of slumparks, of Nita.
sentences.zh: 但他们也会刊登摩西的反驳，而且他们不会给予编辑支持，不支持贫民窟公园的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you're getting at this point now where Moses had the support of a lot of reformers because he was preserving all this woodland around the city.
sentences.zh: 是的，你现在谈到了这一点，摩西曾得到许多改革者的支持，因为他保护了城市周围所有的林地。

sentences.en: And they were like, he's doing it.
sentences.zh: 他们当时觉得，他做得对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And now they're watching as he is cutting down that woodland.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们眼睁睁看着他砍伐那些林地。

sentences.en: Like he's chopping it down to replace it with ball fields and things like that.
sentences.zh: 就像他把它们砍掉，换成球场之类的东西。

sentences.en: And they're only starting to realize again.
sentences.zh: 他们才刚刚开始意识到。

sentences.en: It's like that – and this happens throughout the book and it is very frustrating.
sentences.zh: 这就像——这种情况在整本书中都在发生，非常令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And I don't know if it's – how it happened in real life or it's the way Caro organized it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是——在现实生活中是怎么发生的，还是卡罗组织叙述的方式。

sentences.en: But the reformers are always like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 但改革者们总是说，等一下。

sentences.en: He did this thing.
sentences.zh: 他做了这件事。

sentences.en: Maybe it's not so great.
sentences.zh: 也许没那么好。

sentences.en: So like he tore down the casino.
sentences.zh: 比如他拆除了赌场。

sentences.en: That wasn't so great.
sentences.zh: 那不太好。

sentences.en: Now he's cutting down these forests.
sentences.zh: 现在他正在砍伐这些森林。

sentences.en: Wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: That's not so great.
sentences.zh: 那不太好。

sentences.en: Later we'll see him attack a genuinely historically important building.
sentences.zh: 后来我们会看到他攻击一座具有真正历史重要性的建筑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And for no real reason and they're like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无正当理由，他们说，等一下。

sentences.en: That's not so great.
sentences.zh: 那不太好。

sentences.en: And Caro says here that no one was putting the pieces together,
sentences.zh: 卡罗在这里说，没有人把这些碎片拼凑起来，

sentences.en: that this is an overall overarching ideology for Moses because they're kind of – they're still enthralled to his image.
sentences.zh: 认为这对摩西来说是一种整体的、包罗万象的意识形态，因为他们——他们仍然被他的形象所迷惑。

sentences.en: But also they're only really paying attention to their local parks.
sentences.zh: 但他们也只关注自己当地的公园。

sentences.en: They don't see that the same thing is happening all over.
sentences.zh: 他们没有看到同样的事情正在到处发生。

sentences.en: And they probably have the same blind spots that he has.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能也有和他一样的盲点。

sentences.en: I mean they're probably not really aware of people that are different from them and they see the good parts of him and they don't have to experience the bad parts of him because he's not running a road through their house.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们可能并没有真正意识到与他们不同的人，他们看到了他好的一面，而且不必经历他坏的一面，因为他没有在他们的房子上修路。

sentences.en: He's not putting up parks in their neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 他没有在他们的社区里强行建设公园。

sentences.en: They just probably just don't really connect with the suffering that he's causing even at this point.
sentences.zh: 他们可能只是没有真正感受到他所造成的痛苦，即使是在这个时候。

sentences.en: But they will.
sentences.zh: 但他们会感受到的。

sentences.en: Not yet.
sentences.zh: 还没到时候。

sentences.en: But look, he put roads through the other neighborhoods and I said nothing because it wasn't my neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 但是看，他在其他社区修路时，我什么也没说，因为那不是我的社区。

sentences.en: And then he put a – he tore down a park in this other neighborhood and I didn't say anything.
sentences.zh: 然后他在另一个社区拆掉了一个公园，我也没有说什么。

sentences.en: I really should have had the details for this thing before I said it.
sentences.zh: 我在说这些话之前真的应该把细节搞清楚。

sentences.en: Anyway, eventually he came for me.
sentences.zh: 总之，最终他找上了我。

sentences.en: That's the end.
sentences.zh: 这就是结局。

sentences.en: Eventually he came for my neighborhood, which does happen, which starts to happen.
sentences.zh: 最终他找上了我的社区，这确实发生了，也开始发生了。

sentences.en: And as we'll see, that's when the turning point doesn't come until years later when he does start doing things in middle class neighborhoods that have kind of a louder,
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，转折点直到多年后才出现，当他开始在中产阶级社区做事情时，那些社区有更响亮、

sentences.en: more powerful voice.
sentences.zh: 更有力的声音。

sentences.en: But they also – this is also one of their flaws is they have the classic flaw of all liberals.
sentences.zh: 但他们也——这也是他们的缺陷之一，他们有所有自由派的典型缺陷。

sentences.en: All liberals have this flaw.
sentences.zh: 所有自由派都有这个缺陷。

sentences.en: I have it.
sentences.zh: 我有。

sentences.en: Roman, I don't know you super well, but I'm sure you have it too.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，我不太了解你，但我敢肯定你也有。

sentences.en: I probably do.
sentences.zh: 我可能确实有。

sentences.en: This belief that if I just sat down and discussed this with him and just explained to him why this was not going to work, he would say, oh, yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 这种信念是：如果我能坐下来和他讨论这件事，并向他解释为什么这样做行不通，他就会说，哦，是的，你是对的。

sentences.en: I will – I was wrong to do that.
sentences.zh: 我会——我那样做是错的。

sentences.en: We will do it the other way.
sentences.zh: 我们会换种方式做。

sentences.en: Let's come to a compromise.
sentences.zh: 让我们达成妥协吧。

sentences.en: Whenever anyone's like, we need a national conversation on this, as if a conversation has ever made anything better.
sentences.zh: 每当有人说，我们需要就此进行全国对话时，就好像对话曾经让事情变得更好一样。

sentences.en: It only – it almost never does.
sentences.zh: 它几乎从来没有。

sentences.en: But they're like, if we can just discuss this with him, if we can just get in there and talk to him about it, we're sure we could show him the truth.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，如果我们能和他讨论这件事，如果我们能进去和他谈谈，我们肯定能让他看到真相。

sentences.en: And that's how Caro leads into the end of the chapter, which is chilling, he says.
sentences.zh: 这就是卡罗引出本章结尾的方式，非常令人不寒而栗，他说，

sentences.en: But Moses no longer had to discuss.
sentences.zh: 但摩西不再需要讨论了。

sentences.en: He had long had great dreams for the city, and now he had learned how to make dreams come true.
sentences.zh: 他很久以前就对这座城市怀有伟大的梦想，而现在他已经学会了如何让梦想成真。

sentences.en: He had learned the technique of stake driving and of whipsawing.
sentences.zh: 他学会了立桩和左右开弓的技巧。

sentences.en: He had learned how to mislead and conceal and deceive, how to lie to men and bully them, how to ruin their reputations.
sentences.zh: 他学会了如何误导、隐瞒和欺骗，如何对人撒谎和欺凌，如何毁掉他们的名声。

sentences.en: And he used all these methods to bring the dream to reality.
sentences.zh: 他利用所有这些方法将梦想变成了现实。

sentences.en: Then there's a little space, indent, indent, indent.
sentences.zh: 然后留出一点空间，缩进，缩进，再缩进。

sentences.en: Or was it all for the dream?
sentences.zh: 还是说这一切都是为了那个梦想？

sentences.en: And that's how he ends that chapter.
sentences.zh: 他那一章就是这样结尾的。

sentences.en: That's how chapter 24, driving, ends and is where this section ends.
sentences.zh: 第24章“驾驶”就是这样结束的，这一部分也就到此为止了。

sentences.en: Was it for the dream or are there darker desires?
sentences.zh: 是为了梦想，还是有更阴暗的欲望？

sentences.en: Well, the next part, part five, is entitled The Love of Power.
sentences.zh: 好吧，下一部分，第五部分，标题是《权力的爱》。

sentences.en: So that's a little spoiler.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一个小剧透。

sentences.en: I think that tells you what it's about.
sentences.zh: 我想这已经告诉你它讲的是什么了。

sentences.en: We'll cover The Love of Power on the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下一集讨论《权力的爱》。

sentences.en: That's only two chapters.
sentences.zh: 那只有两章。

sentences.en: It's pages 499 to 606, chapters 25 and 26.
sentences.zh: 是第499到606页，第25章和第26章。

sentences.en: You may be wondering how only two chapters can be a longer section of the book than the one we covered in this episode.
sentences.zh: 你可能在想，为什么仅仅两章的内容，却比我们这一集涵盖的部分还要长。

sentences.en: One of them is a very long chapter.
sentences.zh: 其中一章非常长。

sentences.en: It's only two chapters, but it feels like a Robert Moses type thing to be like, it's only two chapters.
sentences.zh: 虽然只有两章，但感觉就像罗伯特·摩西那种风格，会说“这不过才两章而已”。

sentences.en: By the way, one of those chapters is 75 pages long.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，其中一章有75页长。

sentences.en: I didn't tell you that.
sentences.zh: 我之前没告诉你。

sentences.en: But they're very good chapters.
sentences.zh: 但它们是非常精彩的章节。

sentences.en: I'm very excited about the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我对下一集感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Coming up, our conversation with investigative journalist Brandi Zadrozny.
sentences.zh: 接下来，是我们与调查记者布兰迪·扎德罗兹尼的对话。

sentences.en: Our Power Broker Book Club guest for this week is Brandi Zadrozny.
sentences.zh: 我们本周的《权力掮客》读书会嘉宾是布兰迪·扎德罗兹尼。

sentences.en: I am a reporter for NBC News.
sentences.zh: 我是NBC新闻的记者。

sentences.en: I cover misinformation, disinformation, extremism, the internet, platforms, politics, people.
sentences.zh: 我报道错误信息、虚假信息、极端主义、互联网、平台、政治和人物。

sentences.en: It sort of runs the gambit.
sentences.zh: 范围相当广泛。

sentences.en: Brandi mostly works on longer investigative pieces where her research background as a reference librarian comes in handy.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪主要从事长篇调查报道，她作为参考馆员的研究背景在这里派上了用场。

sentences.en: One of her recent stories is about how a far-right sheriff's group is urging local law enforcement agencies to investigate baseless claims of voter fraud.
sentences.zh: 她最近的一篇报道是关于一个极右翼治安官组织如何敦促当地执法机构调查毫无根据的选民欺诈指控。

sentences.en: She also hosted this great podcast called Tiffany Dover is Dead about a nurse in Tennessee who passed out on live television after receiving the COVID vaccine in December of 2020 and then became the center of an anti-vax conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 她还主持了一个很棒的播客叫《蒂芙尼·多佛死了》，讲述了田纳西州一名护士在2020年12月接种新冠疫苗后在电视直播中晕倒，随后成为反疫苗阴谋论中心的故事。

sentences.en: It's really compelling stuff and infuriating and compelling at the same time.
sentences.zh: 内容非常引人入胜，既让人愤怒又让人欲罢不能。

sentences.en: Somehow, Brandi also found time to read The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，布兰迪竟然还抽出时间读了《权力掮客》。

sentences.en: What struck me about this book from the beginning was I knew who Robert Caro was.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，这本书就让我印象深刻，因为我知道罗伯特·卡罗是谁。

sentences.en: I had never read his books.
sentences.zh: 但我以前从未读过他的书。

sentences.en: But, like, I had known a little bit about his story.
sentences.zh: 不过，我对他的一些事迹略有耳闻。

sentences.en: And so the very first thing is just it's kind of he's realizing a dream for so many of us.
sentences.zh: 所以第一点就是，他实现了我们许多人的梦想。

sentences.en: You know, like, the idea of turning every page is a real luxury.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种能翻阅每一页的感觉真是一种奢侈。

sentences.en: And so, you know, he – I think he started this series because he was a reporter on Long Island, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他——我想他开始写这个系列是因为他当时是长岛的一名记者，对吧？

sentences.en: He was doing a story on some piece of infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在报道某个基础设施项目。

sentences.en: And then he thought, wow, that's really strange.
sentences.zh: 然后他想，哇，这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: You know, how did this guy amass all this power?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这家伙是怎么积累起这么多权力的？

sentences.en: And we have a million questions like that when doing any story, right?
sentences.zh: 我们在做任何报道时都会有无数类似的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: But you never really get the time to keep going.
sentences.zh: 但你永远没有时间去深究。

sentences.en: You're sort of on to the next story or on to the next beat of that story.
sentences.zh: 你总是忙着下一篇报道，或者忙着报道故事的下一个阶段。

sentences.en: And no one has the time to turn every page.
sentences.zh: 没有人有时间去翻阅每一页。

sentences.en: So the fact that he said, I'm going to and did the thing for however many years it took him to do that, it's just – it's so aspirational.
sentences.zh: 所以他竟然说“我要去翻阅”，并且真的花了那么多年去完成这件事，这简直——太令人向往了。

sentences.en: And then when you get in it from the very beginning, you're like, he's going to do this thing.
sentences.zh: 当你从一开始就沉浸其中，你会觉得，他真的要把它做成。

sentences.en: Like, there is nothing left.
sentences.zh: 就像，没有任何遗漏。

sentences.en: And it's just great.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: You're saying you would love to come to your editor and say, I have this story.
sentences.zh: 你是说你很想去找你的编辑说，我有一个故事。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 它太棒了。

sentences.en: And they say, how long is it going to take me to work on the story?
sentences.zh: 然后他们问，我需要花多长时间来做这个报道？

sentences.en: And you say, seven years.
sentences.zh: 你说，七年。

sentences.en: And for them to say, yes, go for it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说，好的，去做吧。

sentences.en: And then you go and talk to your spouse.
sentences.zh: 然后你回去和你的配偶商量。

sentences.en: And you say, okay, we're going to sell the house.
sentences.zh: 你说，好吧，我们要卖掉房子。

sentences.en: And we're going to get real poor for a time period.
sentences.zh: 我们要过上一段很穷的日子。

sentences.en: For a long time.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间。

sentences.en: And then it's going to pay off because a bunch of nerds are going to talk about it 50 years later.
sentences.zh: 然后这会得到回报，因为50年后会有一群书呆子讨论它。

sentences.en: Well, my conversation with my editor is always like, how many words do you think this is going to be, Brandy?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我和编辑的对话总是像这样：“你觉得这篇报道会有多少字，布兰迪？”

sentences.en: And I'm like, 10,000.
sentences.zh: 我说，一万字。

sentences.en: She's like, try five.
sentences.zh: 她说，试着写五千字。

sentences.en: And then, you know, you get into a place where you're like, ha-ha, I snuck six.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，你最后写完时会说，哈哈，我偷偷写了六千字。

sentences.en: And that's like a big win.
sentences.zh: 那就算是一场大胜利了。

sentences.en: I can't even imagine, you know, being able to do that.
sentences.zh: 我简直无法想象，你知道，能够做到那种程度。

sentences.en: And also, like, the details that I think are so interesting about these stories are often cut by my editor.
sentences.zh: 而且，我觉得这些故事中非常有趣的细节往往会被我的编辑删掉。

sentences.en: Who's like, eh, superfluous, boring.
sentences.zh: 她会说，呃，多余的，无聊。

sentences.en: And it's like, but that's what the fun thing is.
sentences.zh: 而我觉得，但这才是最有趣的地方啊。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And interesting doesn't always make it into the final cut.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的东西并不总能进入最终版本。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of what Robert Caro is doing, and I don't know if he just intuited this or this is the writer he is.
sentences.zh: 我是说，罗伯特·卡罗所做的大部分工作，我不知道他是凭直觉还是他天生就是这种作家。

sentences.en: He is about building a gestalt through lots of information so that you, like, it sort of fills in your foundation.
sentences.zh: 他通过大量信息构建出一个整体，让你感觉，它填补了你的认知基础。

sentences.en: And then when he's making his really bold case, which is like changing the mind of a bunch of people who think this other,
sentences.zh: 然后当他提出他那非常大胆的论点时，比如改变那些几十年来一直认为某人是圣人的人的看法，

sentences.en: this man is a saint for decades of his professional existence.
sentences.zh: 这在他的职业生涯中持续了数十年。

sentences.en: Well, narratives are really strong and people don't read.
sentences.zh: 嗯，叙事的力量非常强大，而且人们不怎么读书。

sentences.en: I mean, I say that, you know, with a heavy sigh because I will write some, you know, revelatory piece on someone that really pulls the mask off who they are.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我带着沉重的叹息说出这一点，因为我会写一些关于某人的揭露性文章，真正撕下他们的伪装。

sentences.en: And then the next day they're, you know, sitting in front of a House Judiciary Committee.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天他们就坐在众议院司法委员会面前了。

sentences.en: And I'm like, don't you know who this is?
sentences.zh: 我心想，你们不知道他是谁吗？

sentences.en: I told you.
sentences.zh: 我告诉过你们了。

sentences.en: So I can only imagine someone with sort of the heft and, you know, reputation that Moses had just that not getting through until this thing happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我只能想象，像摩西那样拥有如此分量和声誉的人，在事情发生之前是不会被揭穿的。

sentences.en: So when you investigate things, I mean, I suppose like a lot of, since you cover stuff sort of in the modern era of misinformation and lots of online things,
sentences.zh: 那么当你调查事情时，我是说，我想像你这样报道现代错误信息和大量网络内容的人，

sentences.en: your archive is the world of the Internet and then talking to people and stuff like this.
sentences.zh: 你的档案就是互联网世界，还有与人交谈等等。

sentences.en: How did it strike you when you, you know, picture, you know, Robert Caro in, you know, these basements on Randall's Island and things like this?
sentences.zh: 当你想象罗伯特·卡罗在兰德尔岛的地下室里做这些事时，你有什么感想？
zh_words: 罗伯特·卡罗在兰德尔岛

sentences.en: Does this, does this like make you feel like envious?
sentences.zh: 这会让你感到嫉妒吗？

sentences.en: Do you like, or does it make you just admire it?
sentences.zh: 还是说，这只会让你钦佩？

sentences.en: Like, what is your take on it?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看的？

sentences.en: So I was actually thinking about this last night as I was like trying to remind myself of what happened in the chapters that y'all are going to discuss.
sentences.zh: 昨晚我还在想这个问题，当时我正试图回想你们要讨论的章节里发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I just started looking through the New York Times time machine because they have all their archives up.
sentences.zh: 我开始翻阅《纽约时报》的时间机器，因为他们把所有档案都上传了。

sentences.en: And so I was looking at like, you know, in the 30s, like what were the letters to the editor and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我当时在看，你知道，30年代的读者来信之类的东西。

sentences.en: And I was just thinking, I was literally thinking, oh, he must have been like in a library for this or like he must have been in the stacks.
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想，我真的在想，哦，他当时一定是在图书馆里做这些，或者一定是在书库里。

sentences.en: That's so interesting.
