sentences.zh: 那太有趣了。

sentences.en: And I also thought, because I did a pretty clean sweep in a couple hours before bed.
sentences.zh: 而且我还想，因为我在睡前几个小时里做了一次相当彻底的搜寻。

sentences.en: And that's really great that we have the opportunity to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们有机会这样做真是太好了。

sentences.en: But so much is lost because we think everything is online.
sentences.zh: 但很多东西都丢失了，因为我们以为一切都在网上。

sentences.en: Like, there are a lot of things that if you just walk down to the courthouse, I was doing a story on Trump in 2016, and walked down to the New York courthouse,
sentences.zh: 比如，有很多东西如果你直接走到法院去——我在2016年做关于特朗普的报道时，走到纽约法院，

sentences.en: the New York City courthouse, and got a large portion of his divorce records, which we weren't supposed to get.
sentences.zh: 纽约市法院，拿到了他很大一部分离婚记录，而我们本不该拿到这些的。

sentences.en: But because it was a real person, you know, and there were real papers, we got a bunch of things.
sentences.zh: 但因为那是真实的人，有真实的文件，我们确实得到了一堆东西。

sentences.en: And I remember for that story, specifically, a friend at a different outlet wanted to go down to the courthouse, but they wouldn't let her leave her desk.
sentences.zh: 我记得那篇报道时，另一家媒体的一位朋友想去法院，但他们不让她离开办公桌。

sentences.en: And it was like, oh, you can still get so much by using those sort of old school reporting techniques and going to the place and trying to get the things.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，哦，通过使用那些老派的报道技巧，亲自去现场尝试获取资料，你仍然可以得到很多东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's really true.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为确实如此。

sentences.en: That's so much fun to think about.
sentences.zh: 想到这一点真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: And that's what I love.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我所热爱的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, just the excitement of that hunt is, like, so enjoyable, especially when it takes place in a physical location when you're opening up files and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，那种搜寻的兴奋感是如此令人享受，尤其是当它发生在实体场所，当你打开档案柜之类的东西时。

sentences.en: Like, I just love archive research so much.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢档案研究了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The scariest part of a story is not having one.
sentences.zh: 报道最可怕的部分就是没有故事可写。

sentences.en: And once you have a story that you're like, this is a story that I'm working on, and you can just dig and dig and dig and dig and dig and dig.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了故事，你会觉得，这就是我正在做的报道，然后你就可以不断地挖掘、挖掘、挖掘。

sentences.en: Like, that's all the fun stuff, that needing a story and then actually writing the story.
sentences.zh: 这才是所有有趣的部分，需要一个故事，然后真正写出这个故事。

sentences.en: That's what terrifies me.
sentences.zh: 那才是我最害怕的。

sentences.en: The rest is the best part.
sentences.zh: 剩下的部分才是最好的。

sentences.en: That's what Kara told us.
sentences.zh: 这就是卡罗告诉我们的。

sentences.en: Kara told us basically that if he could get away with just doing all the research and not writing the book, he'd be very happy if he could just do the research all the time.
sentences.zh: 卡罗基本上告诉我们，如果他能只做研究而不写书，他会非常高兴，如果他能一直做研究的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, I had an editor who refused to let me talk to him about my work when I'd be like, oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 是的，我以前有一位编辑，当我兴奋地说“天哪”时，他拒绝让我谈论我的工作。

sentences.en: And he's like, nope, because once you say it, once you communicate it, then you won't get it out.
sentences.zh: 他说，不行，因为一旦你说出来，一旦你交流了，你就写不出来了。

sentences.en: You won't write the thing.
sentences.zh: 你就不会写那篇东西了。

sentences.en: And they were right.
sentences.zh: 他们是对的。

sentences.en: So, you know, this episode, we talk about a lot how Moses has great success using the press to get what he wants.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这一集我们谈了很多摩西如何利用媒体成功达到目的。

sentences.en: And the one thing, the mainly thing that he does is, you know, he just puts out kind of press releases or he has lots of, you know, familiarity with a lot of press people.
sentences.zh: 他主要做的一件事就是，你知道，他只是发布新闻稿，或者他与许多媒体人士非常熟悉。

sentences.en: And his story becomes the story.
sentences.zh: 他的故事就成了新闻报道的主题。

sentences.en: I'm just curious about this.
sentences.zh: 我对此很好奇。

sentences.en: Like when you're you talk or you report on sort of like how a mainstream media outlet, you know, like reports a thing, how a citizen journalist, in quotes, reports a thing.
sentences.zh: 比如当你谈论或报道主流媒体如何报道一件事，或者所谓的“公民记者”如何报道一件事时，

sentences.en: You know, what does it strike you about like that time period and how information is spread and how the press is used in these ways?
sentences.zh: 那个时代的信息传播方式以及媒体被利用的方式，给你留下了什么印象？

sentences.en: I think it still works that way for the most part.
sentences.zh: 我认为在很大程度上它仍然是那样运作的。

sentences.en: I mean, when you when you go to a website or when you open the paper, you're mostly reading commodity news.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你访问一个网站或打开报纸时，你读到的主要是商品化新闻。

sentences.en: You're mostly reading the kind of news that like you get anywhere because a thing has happened.
sentences.zh: 你读到的主要是那种你在任何地方都能看到的新闻，因为事情已经发生了。

sentences.en: You know, there is a unveiling.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一个揭幕仪式。

sentences.en: There is a crime.
sentences.zh: 有一桩犯罪。

sentences.en: There is, you know, so like and the police have told the police beat reporter about that crime.
sentences.zh: 有，你知道，警察已经把那桩犯罪告诉了警务记者。

sentences.en: Like you get into this rhythm as a reporter where you're like, this is my beat.
sentences.zh: 作为记者，你会进入一种节奏，你会觉得，这就是我的报道领域。

sentences.en: This is these are the sources for my beat.
sentences.zh: 这就是我报道领域的线人。

sentences.en: And here is how I report that out day to day.
sentences.zh: 这就是我每天报道这些事情的方式。

sentences.en: And especially if you're in a paper, if you're broadcasting where you have to have something every single day, like you have to fill that space.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你在报社，或者在广播电台，你必须每天都有东西要播，你必须填补那个空间。

sentences.en: Then you rely on these people that, you know, are good for factual stories that people like and your editors like.
sentences.zh: 那么你就会依赖那些你知道的、能提供人们喜欢且编辑也喜欢的真实故事的人。

sentences.en: And so, like, I don't think that that has changed much.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不认为这一点改变了很多。

sentences.en: There are still bazillions of publicists who make their living on, like, getting a story to a reporter who takes that press release and writes it up and makes it a story.
sentences.zh: 仍然有无数公关人员靠着把故事提供给记者为生，记者拿着新闻稿写出来，把它变成一篇报道。

sentences.en: So, that's not very different at all.
sentences.zh: 所以，这根本没什么不同。

sentences.en: What's funny about this book and what is leading, I think, to your question is that, like, it feels very today, all of it.
sentences.zh: 这本书有趣的地方，以及我认为引出你问题的地方在于，这一切感觉都非常现代。

sentences.en: The way that he manipulates the press with these events, with, you know, leaking to them, with, you know, befriending them and bringing them to nice events.
sentences.zh: 他通过这些活动操纵媒体的方式，通过向他们泄密，通过与他们交朋友并带他们参加高级活动。

sentences.en: Like, that with the way the New York Times operates, like, all of this feels very of the moment.
sentences.zh: 就像《纽约时报》的运作方式一样，这一切都感觉非常符合当下。

sentences.en: And it's like, he used it to such great effect.
sentences.zh: 而且他利用这些手段取得了巨大的成效。

sentences.en: I mean, like, you know, Moses in this moment has just spectacularly lost running for governor.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，摩西在这一刻刚刚惨败了州长竞选。

sentences.en: Like, just is completely on his ass.
sentences.zh: 就像，完全跌入谷底。

sentences.en: And FDR concocts this Order 129 to do this sort of final blow and take him out.
sentences.zh: 然后罗斯福炮制了第129号行政令，给了他最后一击，想把他干掉。

sentences.en: And Moses leaks that to the press.
sentences.zh: 而摩西把这个泄露给了媒体。

sentences.en: And it totally revives his career, which sets up the entire rest of the book.
sentences.zh: 这彻底复活了他的职业生涯，也为整本书的其余部分奠定了基础。

sentences.en: I mean, it really is, like, his resurrection that makes him stronger than ever.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这确实是他的复活，让他变得比以往任何时候都更强大。

sentences.en: And, you know, and that comes about because the press, you know, just take Moses' side of this at face value.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是因为媒体只是照单全收了摩西的说法。

sentences.en: Moses seems to discover that, like, yeah, that newspapers need material.
sentences.zh: 摩西似乎发现，报纸需要素材。

sentences.en: They need things to print.
sentences.zh: 他们需要东西来印刷。

sentences.en: And so if he can provide that in the form of press releases or leaked documents or we're opening a park, we're opening a pool, then they're not going to say,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他能以新闻稿、泄露文件，或者“我们要开个公园”、“我们要开个游泳池”的形式提供这些，那么他们就不会说，

sentences.en: let's double check this before we actually put it in the newspaper, you know.
sentences.zh: “在我们把它放进报纸之前，让我们先核实一下”，你知道。

sentences.en: Well, A, we love a leak.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我们喜欢泄密。

sentences.en: Like, that is, like, we love a leak.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们真的喜欢泄密。

sentences.en: We love a whistleblower.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢吹哨人。

sentences.en: Like, and that's just human nature, right?
sentences.zh: 这就像是人性使然，对吧？

sentences.en: Because that makes a good story.
sentences.zh: 因为那样才是一个好故事。

sentences.en: Like, ooh, this is secret.
sentences.zh: 比如，噢，这是秘密。

sentences.en: This is secret information that I'm giving you, like, that nobody knows about.
sentences.zh: 这是我告诉你的秘密信息，就是那种没人知道的信息。

sentences.en: Like, that is what we live for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们赖以生存的东西。

sentences.en: And so, like, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，这说得通。

sentences.en: I think the other part of it is sort of human nature, and I try to think about this all the time,
sentences.zh: 我认为另一部分原因算是人性，我一直试图思考这个问题，

sentences.en: about my just human biases and narrative and the way that when sources approach me, because my sources are not all good guys.
sentences.zh: 思考我作为人类的偏见、叙事方式，以及当消息源接近我时的情况，因为我的消息源并不全是好人。

sentences.en: Like, I have sources who are literal white supremacists, right, who are, like, not people that I'd want to have tea with,
sentences.zh: 比如，我有一些消息源是彻头彻尾的白人至上主义者，真的，他们不是那种我想一起喝茶的人，

sentences.en: but who have given me information that is true and helps me explain this world that we live in right now.
sentences.zh: 但他们提供给我的信息是真实的，有助于我解释我们现在所处的世界。

sentences.en: But when the point of that is that, like, when someone comes to you with a narrative, it might be, like, when my child comes to me, right, and says, my other child hit me.
sentences.zh: 但重点在于，当有人带着某种叙事来找你时，可能就像我孩子来找我，说，我的另一个孩子打了我。

sentences.en: Then now I'm investigating my child hit me.
sentences.zh: 然后我就开始调查我孩子打我的事。

sentences.en: And that's, like, the narrative that has been started, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是已经开始的叙事，对吧？

sentences.en: So, like, Roosevelt hit me.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗斯福打了我。

sentences.en: Okay, that is what I understand the facts to be.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是我所理解的事实。

sentences.en: And so I might go, as they did, to Roosevelt's team and say, why did you do this, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我可能会像他们那样，去罗斯福的团队问，你们为什么要这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: But then they're on the defensive, and I've already set up that narrative.
sentences.zh: 但那时他们处于防御状态，而我已经设定好了那种叙事。

sentences.en: That is the narrative that I've established.
sentences.zh: 那就是我已经确立的叙事。

sentences.en: And that is very, very powerful.
sentences.zh: 那是非常、非常有力量的。

sentences.en: It's hard to come back from that, which is why, you know, again, like, he's so good on offense and less so on defense.
sentences.zh: 很难从中扭转局面，这就是为什么，你知道，再说一次，他在进攻时很强，但在防守时就没那么强了。

sentences.en: So I've been checking out your work, and I love your podcast, Tiffany Dover is Dead.
sentences.zh: 我一直在关注你的作品，我很喜欢你的播客《蒂芙尼·多佛死了》。

sentences.en: But a lot of the time, it makes me really angry because I have this just complete disdain for conspiracy theorists.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，它让我非常生气，因为我完全鄙视阴谋论者。

sentences.en: And then I started thinking about this book, The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始思考这本书，《权力掮客》。

sentences.en: And if you take, like, a 30,000-foot view of this, you squint really hard, it kind of has the vague shape of a conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 如果你从三万英尺的高空俯瞰，眯起眼睛仔细看，它隐约有一种阴谋论的轮廓。

sentences.en: Like, instead of, you know, infrastructure being done by committee and through goodwill and trying to make the world a better place, you know, this is 1,300 pages of Robert Caro,
sentences.zh: 比如，基础设施建设本应由委员会通过善意来完成，旨在让世界变得更美好，但你看到的却是罗伯特·卡罗写的1300页内容，

sentences.en: you know, convincing you that there's this man behind it all, Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他让你相信这一切背后有一个人，罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: And this man has, you know, evil intent, and he did bad things.
sentences.zh: 而这个人有邪恶的意图，他做了坏事。

sentences.en: And this feels like a conspiracy theory, and it kind of blew my mind.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像一个阴谋论，让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: So I've been thinking about what makes the difference between, like, an investigative piece that reveals something that, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在思考，揭露某些事情的调查报道与阴谋论之间的区别是什么，你知道，比如，

sentences.en: sinister intent by a small group of people versus, you know, conspiracy theories that are completely, you know,
sentences.zh: 一小群人的险恶用心，与那些完全，你知道，

sentences.en: out the airlock and completely crazy and just trying to reconcile that and how you reconcile that in your work.
sentences.zh: 脱离现实、完全疯狂的阴谋论之间的区别，我只是在试图调和这些，以及你在工作中如何调和这些。

sentences.en: Well, no, I've been thinking about that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，我一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: Like, the deep state is real, and it is Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 比如，深层政府是真实存在的，那就是罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: Like, he is the man who, by his great machinations and money and power, is literally, like, choosing who, what children get sunlight and what children don't, right?
sentences.zh: 他就是那个通过巨大的权谋、金钱和权力，真正在选择哪些孩子能晒到太阳，哪些孩子不能的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, who gets access to the water and who doesn't?
sentences.zh: 比如，谁能获得水源，谁不能？

sentences.en: Like, it's very, it's stuff that rings very true in conspiracy land.
sentences.zh: 这在阴谋论领域听起来非常真实。

sentences.en: And conspiracy theories are great because conspiracies are real and conspiracies happen, especially at the local government.
sentences.zh: 阴谋论很棒，因为阴谋是真实存在的，阴谋确实会发生，尤其是在地方政府层面。

sentences.en: But what's interesting about this is that the truth is that real conspiracies operate like this in sort of banal ways, in paper pushing, in behind-the-scenes meetings, in,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，真相在于，真正的阴谋以这种平庸的方式运作，在文书工作中，在幕后会议中，在，

sentences.en: you know, through the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，通过《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: And it's like, it takes however many pages, several hundred, over a thousand, something, I listen to audiobook, 60s-plus hours of pages to explain, in fact,
sentences.zh: 这需要几百页，甚至超过一千页，我听的是有声书，花了60多个小时来解释，事实上，

sentences.en: how this conspiracy worked because it's boring, you know?
sentences.zh: 这个阴谋是如何运作的，因为它很无聊，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's not like one secret meeting at a CDC in Georgia which determined that everybody's going to get autism.
sentences.zh: 它不像是在佐治亚州疾控中心的一次秘密会议，决定了每个人都会患上自闭症。

sentences.en: Well, and also that the N's are banal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且那些阴谋也很平庸。

sentences.en: The N's are, I don't want poor people to be able to take the bus to these communities on Long Island.
sentences.zh: 那些阴谋是，我不希望穷人能坐公交车去长岛的这些社区。

sentences.en: And so I'm going to do everything I can to block that, as opposed to the fun conspiracies where helicopters are going to round us up and send us, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我将尽我所能阻止这一点，而不是那种有趣的阴谋，比如直升机要把我们围捕起来，把我们，你知道，

sentences.en: and make us slaves to trans-dimensional reptiles and things like that.
sentences.zh: 让我们成为跨维度爬行动物的奴隶之类的东西。

sentences.en: Those are the fun conspiracies.
sentences.zh: 那些才是好玩的阴谋。

sentences.en: And it feels like the real conspiracies are harder maybe to get people to see because they're not as exciting, you know?
sentences.zh: 感觉真正的阴谋可能更难让人看出来，因为它们没那么刺激，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, ones that are rooted in things like institutional racism and, like, you know, rich people not liking poor people and not thinking they are deserving of the same things.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些植根于制度性种族主义，以及，你知道，富人不喜欢穷人，认为他们不配拥有同样的东西之类的事情。

sentences.en: And, like, it's stuff like that that's like, that's the real thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种东西，那才是真实存在的。

sentences.en: You want something to be mad about?
sentences.zh: 你想找点什么来生气吗？

sentences.en: Go be mad about that, not your fake Guantanamo Bay stuff.
sentences.zh: 去为那些事情生气吧，而不是你那些虚假的关塔那摩湾之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it does strike me that these conspiracies of Robert Moses and the Moses Men are all that hidden.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实让我觉得罗伯特·摩西和摩西党人的这些阴谋并没有那么隐蔽。

sentences.en: And they don't, they're not really about a conspiracy of action and deed.
sentences.zh: 它们并不是关于行动和行为的阴谋。

sentences.en: They're kind of a conspiracy of shared values.
sentences.zh: 它们更像是一种共享价值观的阴谋。

sentences.en: You know, like, they all agree on a thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们都在某件事上达成了一致。

sentences.en: They, you know, like, tacitly or explicitly, you know, like, express those things and create the world that they see fit.
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道，默许或明确地表达这些东西，并创造出他们认为合适的世界。

sentences.en: But it's not like they're, like, secretly doing a whole lot, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 但并不是说他们在秘密地做很多事情，你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Because, like, when Robert Caro goes and talks to him and talks about the bridges and when you investigate it today and you go, like,
sentences.zh: 因为，当罗伯特·卡罗去采访他，谈论桥梁时，当你今天去调查，你会说，

sentences.en: how did you know that Robert Moses really did make the bridges shorter?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道罗伯特·摩西真的把桥建得更矮了？

sentences.en: And he was like, his assistant told me.
sentences.zh: 他说，他的助手告诉我的。

sentences.en: That's what he said.
sentences.zh: 他就是这么说的。

sentences.en: You know, like, like, it just is like, you know, it's just like.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像是，这只是，你知道，就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, how easy would it have been for a reporter to go into some of the communities that, you know, were being razed to build these new expressways or to, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，记者进入那些被拆除以修建新高速公路的社区，或者去，你知道，

sentences.en: clear these slums and go talk to those people?
sentences.zh: 清理这些贫民窟，去和那些人谈谈，这有多容易？

sentences.en: Like, that was a story in plain sight.
sentences.zh: 那是一个显而易见的故事。

sentences.en: That was, you know, thousands and thousands of people being displaced, communities being destroyed over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 那是成千上万的人流离失所，社区一次又一次地被摧毁。

sentences.en: So, like, why weren't those stories bigger than the man Robert Moses?
sentences.zh: 所以，为什么这些故事没有罗伯特·摩西这个人的故事大？

sentences.en: Why didn't those stories get more play?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些故事没有得到更多的报道？

sentences.en: It's because, I would venture to say, those people were not cared about in the same way.
sentences.zh: 这是因为，我敢说，人们并没有以同样的方式关心那些人。

sentences.en: They were not valorized.
sentences.zh: 他们没有被赋予价值。

sentences.en: They weren't important in the same way that Robert Moses was.
sentences.zh: 他们不像罗伯特·摩西那样重要。

sentences.en: And the reporters were more like Robert Moses than they were like the people that were.
sentences.zh: 而且记者们更像罗伯特·摩西，而不是那些被拆迁的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, they were all the same people.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们都是同一类人。

sentences.en: They hung out at lunch.
sentences.zh: 他们一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: I mean, the owner of the New York Times loved him so very, very much.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，《纽约时报》的老板非常、非常爱他。

sentences.en: Like, I've been trying to think a lot about corollaries.
sentences.zh: 我一直在努力思考很多类比。

sentences.en: Like, who – and just selfishly and maybe because I'm living aspirationally through Robert Harris' work.
sentences.zh: 比如，谁——仅仅是自私地，也许是因为我正通过罗伯特·哈里斯的作品进行抱负性的生活。

sentences.en: But I'm like, who is the Robert Moses of our time?
sentences.zh: 但我会想，谁是我们这个时代的罗伯特·摩西？

sentences.en: Who is the person who is doing the things that we should be looking at right now that we're all missing?
sentences.zh: 谁是那个正在做我们现在应该关注，但我们都忽略了的事情的人？

sentences.en: I haven't thought about it, but listeners can please contact me.
sentences.zh: 我还没想过，但听众可以联系我。

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of one of those things where if we knew about it,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点像是那种如果我们知道的话，

sentences.en: it wouldn't necessarily be the same thing because he was so good at presenting a different version of himself than was actually taking action.
sentences.zh: 它不一定是一回事，因为他非常擅长展示一个与他实际行动不同的自己。

sentences.en: And you need some kind of amazing whistleblower leaker that can meet you in a parking garage somewhere, I guess, and give you the information.
sentences.zh: 而且你需要某种了不起的举报人或泄密者，可以在某个停车场和你见面，我想，然后把信息给你。

sentences.en: Although something I like so much about the book is that Robert Caro is consistently not dramatizing his own investigation or his own research.
sentences.zh: 尽管我非常喜欢这本书的一点是，罗伯特·卡罗始终没有戏剧化他自己的调查或研究。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of like – and then I did something that was really exciting.
sentences.zh: 没有太多像——然后我做了一件非常令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: At most, he'll say, as he does in this episode, well, when I talked to this guy in his house, he told me this.
sentences.zh: 最多，他会说，就像他在这一集里所做的那样，嗯，当我在他家里和这个人交谈时，他告诉了我这个。

sentences.en: Or I went to this guy's office, and this is what he said.
sentences.zh: 或者我去了这个人的办公室，这就是他说的。

sentences.en: There's a – there's not a – he's not creating the suspense around himself during the story.
sentences.zh: 没有——他没有在故事中围绕自己制造悬念。

sentences.en: No, I wasn't even aware, and maybe because I missed it, but while I was listening, I wasn't even aware that he had spoken – actually spoken with Moses,
sentences.zh: 不，我甚至不知道，也许是因为我错过了，但当我在听的时候，我甚至不知道他曾经和摩西谈过——真正谈过，

sentences.en: that he had gotten like the Moses interview.
sentences.zh: 他得到了摩西的采访。

sentences.en: And at the end, I was sort of like, wait, what?
sentences.zh: 最后，我有点像，等等，什么？

sentences.en: This – oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 这——哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Which is a bold and the best choice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大胆且最好的选择。

sentences.en: It's a very old school choice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常老派的选择。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like – it's like – it's not the current sort of fashion for sure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像——这肯定不是目前的流行趋势。

sentences.en: Like, if I would – if I were to do this story, it would be all about how amazing it was that I did this story.
sentences.zh: 如果我要做这个故事，那肯定全是关于我做这个故事有多了不起。

sentences.en: Like, I did this for seven years.
sentences.zh: 比如，我做了七年。

sentences.en: You know, like, that would be the opening line.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那将是开场白。

sentences.en: Can you believe what I did?
sentences.zh: 你能相信我做了什么吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, I appreciated it as I appreciate something old that I read.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我欣赏它，就像我欣赏我读过的旧东西一样。

sentences.en: I see it, but at the same time, you see those little – he does it in his own way.
sentences.zh: 我看到了，但同时，你看到了那些小细节——他以自己的方式做到了。

sentences.en: Oh, he does, for sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，他确实做到了，肯定的。

sentences.en: There's a quiet bragging that goes on here where he's talking about, like, forming of Long Island and, like, even at the beginning where he's like, and then, like, okay,
sentences.zh: 这里有一种安静的吹嘘，他谈论长岛的形成，甚至在开头，他说，然后，好吧，

sentences.en: you know all the roads.
sentences.zh: 你知道所有的路。

sentences.en: Like, I – like, you've done it.
sentences.zh: 就像我——就像你已经做到了。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So, it's different, and I sort of like the narrator.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很不同，我有点喜欢这个叙述者。

sentences.en: I like knowing a little bit about the narrator who's leading me through something.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢了解一点引导我完成某事的叙述者。

sentences.en: I appreciate the modernization of that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我稍微欣赏一下这种现代化。

sentences.en: But I do think – I think what it felt like to me – and I think this is true regardless of, like, the little flair that he would insert about himself as the author.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为——我认为对我来说感觉是这样的——我认为无论他作为作者插入关于自己的小花絮如何，这都是事实。

sentences.en: It shows to me – it's another sort of brick in the house that shows me that he cares about story, about the factual tale of this person more than anything.
sentences.zh: 这向我展示了——这是房子里的另一块砖，向我展示了他关心故事，关心这个人的事实真相，胜过一切。

sentences.en: I think he also – what I also love about Caro is – and I think this is the next thing I want to talk to him about when I talk to him was this – what made him so empathic in regards to the people that – you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为他也——我同样喜欢卡罗的一点是——我认为这是我下次和他谈话时想和他讨论的事情——是什么让他对这些人如此有同理心——你知道，

sentences.en: he really feels the destruction of Moses.
sentences.zh: 他真的感受到了摩西的破坏。

sentences.en: Like, he's going into it with that in mind.
sentences.zh: 他带着这种想法去深入研究。

sentences.en: And I find that very fascinating, and I wonder, you know, when you think about your work, you know, what tunes you into wanting to tell the story of, you know,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常迷人，我想知道，当你思考你的工作时，是什么让你想要讲述这个故事，你知道，

sentences.en: who the victim is in a certain story and where your sensitivities lie and where you – who you are fighting for or fighting to tell the story of.
sentences.zh: 谁是某个故事中的受害者，你的敏感点在哪里，你为谁而战，或者努力为谁讲述故事。

sentences.en: I think Robert Caro has a real, like, old-school liberal, like, you know, just, like, he wants to take care of these people.
sentences.zh: 我认为罗伯特·卡罗有一种真正的、老派的自由主义，就像，你知道，他只是想照顾这些人。

sentences.en: Like, he wants to make sure that their story is told.
sentences.zh: 他想确保他们的故事被讲述出来。

sentences.en: There's just something noble and interesting about that that I like.
sentences.zh: 这其中有一些高尚而有趣的东西，我很喜欢。

sentences.en: But he doesn't really go out and say it, but I can just feel it.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有真正说出来，但我能感觉到。

sentences.en: This is going to seem disjointed, but I swear I have a point.
sentences.zh: 这看起来会很脱节，但我发誓我有重点。

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请说。

sentences.en: So I will often say that I fall in love with every person that I interview, and I will go to an interview.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常说，我爱上了我采访的每一个人，我会去参加采访。

sentences.en: And even, you know, I'm using little quotations, bad guys, conspiracy theorists, you know, just not always the nicest people.
sentences.zh: 即使，你知道，我用了小引号，坏人，阴谋论者，你知道，并不总是最友善的人。

sentences.en: But every time I talk to someone, I feel like I'm nodding along with them, like, oh, that makes sense why you would be doing this thing.
sentences.zh: 但每次我和某人交谈时，我都觉得我在点头表示赞同，哦，你做这件事是有道理的。

sentences.en: Most people, I think, are sincere in their wants, you know, and in their beliefs, like Moses probably was, where he thought he was doing what was ultimately best for the city.
sentences.zh: 我认为大多数人的愿望和信仰是真诚的，就像摩西可能那样，他认为他所做的是最终对城市最好的事情。

sentences.en: And so, like, I think people are typically sincere, and I believe them each time we talk.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为人们通常是真诚的，每次我们交谈时我都相信他们。

sentences.en: And then, you know, I believe sort of everyone, and then I will go home, and I will say I've talked to everyone I need to.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，我有点相信每个人，然后我会回家，我会说我已经和所有需要交谈的人谈过了。

sentences.en: I have all the documents I need to, and now I'm going to write this story.
sentences.zh: 我有我需要的所有文件，现在我要写这个故事了。

sentences.en: And then, you know, after the story is written and is published, although none of the facts in it surprise anyone, the people that I speak to will, you know, call me back and say,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，在故事写完并发表后，虽然其中的事实没有让任何人感到惊讶，但我交谈过的人会，你知道，回电给我说，

sentences.en: I'm, you know, not so happy with the way that this came out.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道，对结果不太满意。

sentences.en: I felt like you really understood where I was coming from and my point of view.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你真的理解我的立场和我的观点。

sentences.en: But then, you know, you were so kind to this, you were too kind to this other group or, you know, and so I will joke that at the end of a story, if everybody's a little mad at me,
sentences.zh: 但后来，你知道，你对这个群体太好了，你对另一个群体太好了，或者，你知道，所以我开玩笑说，在故事结束时，如果每个人都对我有点生气，

sentences.en: then I've probably done a good job.
sentences.zh: 那么我可能做得很好。

sentences.en: But I do feel there is, you know, a certain group or a certain type of source that you do feel like I am the only way this person is going to get this story out.
sentences.zh: 但我确实觉得有一个特定的群体或特定类型的消息源，你会觉得我是这个人能把这个故事传出去的唯一途径。

sentences.en: Nobody seems to care about, you know, about this group of people, about, you know, autistic kids, you know, and their mothers who are being fed misinformation or, like,
sentences.zh: 似乎没人关心，你知道，这个群体的人，你知道，自闭症儿童，你知道，以及被喂食错误信息的母亲们，或者，

sentences.en: or being scammed in this way.
sentences.zh: 或者以这种方式被欺骗。

sentences.en: And so I, you feel an affinity for people whose voices aren't being heard.
sentences.zh: 所以你对那些声音没有被听到的人产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: And there's so much power in the press.
sentences.zh: 媒体的力量太大了。

sentences.en: Like, we have so much power to elevate certain voices.
sentences.zh: 我们有太大的力量去提升某些声音。

sentences.en: And those are always a choice.
sentences.zh: 而这些总是一个选择。

sentences.en: It's always a choice who we choose to elevate and how we tell this narrative.
sentences.zh: 我们选择提升谁以及我们如何讲述这个叙事，总是一个选择。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of responsibility that comes with that.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是巨大的责任。

sentences.en: And I got that very much, that feeling from Caro as well.
sentences.zh: 我也从卡罗那里得到了那种感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I also kind of have that issue when I interview people, I'm bored.
sentences.zh: 我在采访别人时也有类似的问题，我很无聊。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know if I, I don't talk to quite the extremists you do, but like, you know, like, so it's, I don't know what that situation is like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不知道我是否——我没有和像你那样极端的极端分子交谈，但就像，你知道，所以，我不知道那种情况是什么样的。

sentences.en: You talk to a lot of people with extreme views about architecture.
sentences.zh: 你采访过很多对建筑有极端观点的人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, but I'm always like, yeah, okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，我总是会想，嗯，好吧。

sentences.en: And then I have to go back and assess it.
sentences.zh: 然后我得回去重新评估一下。

sentences.en: Like, when you take all that stuff in and then you recalibrate to form this narrative, you know, how do you adjust that?
sentences.zh: 比如，当你吸收了所有这些信息，然后重新调整以形成这种叙事时，你知道，你是如何进行调整的？

sentences.en: Like, how do you pull yourself back from the emotional sort of, like, seduction of their passion and turn the dials to make it into what you're presenting as the truth?
sentences.zh: 比如，你是如何让自己从那种情感上的、某种被他们的热情所吸引的状态中抽离出来，并转动刻度盘，把它变成你所呈现的真相的？

sentences.en: I mean, it's probably some sort of, like, emotional disability or something, but like, I feel, I don't know if it's a good thing, but like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能是一种情感上的障碍之类的，但我感觉，我不知道这是否是件好事，但，

sentences.en: I remember what's in front of my face or like, I emotionally connect with what's in front of my face right at that moment.
sentences.zh: 我记得我眼前的东西，或者说，我与当下眼前的东西产生了情感上的连接。

sentences.en: And then when I leave, even like walking to my car, I'm like, wait a minute, that guy was full of moony.
sentences.zh: 然后当我离开时，甚至在走到车边的时候，我会想，等一下，那家伙满嘴胡言。

sentences.en: I'm like, that's not true.
sentences.zh: 我在想，那不是真的。

sentences.en: Or like, I don't believe that.
sentences.zh: 或者说，我不相信那个。

sentences.en: Why was I nodding along?
sentences.zh: 我当时为什么要点头附和？

sentences.en: Sometimes I'll actually have like a post-it if I'm doing like a phone interview that says, stop nodding along or like, stop smiling.
sentences.zh: 有时如果我在做电话采访，我甚至会贴一张便利贴，上面写着：别再点头了，或者别再笑了。

sentences.en: Because I do, you want to connect.
sentences.zh: 因为我确实会，你想建立连接。

sentences.en: So much of this is about connection.
sentences.zh: 这其中很大一部分是关于连接的。

sentences.en: But ultimately the responsibility when you get home is to say, what is real?
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，当你回家时，责任在于问自己：什么是真实的？

sentences.en: What is the truth?
sentences.zh: 什么是真相？

sentences.en: And how can I accurately reflect that in a piece of writing or a video or whatever it is that we're doing?
sentences.zh: 我该如何在文章、视频或我们正在做的任何事情中准确地反映这一点？

sentences.en: I wonder if you see that in the book also,
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否也在书中看到了这一点，

sentences.en: I feel like I see it a little bit where you can tell when sometimes when Carol is talking about Moses or kind of implying the times that he saw Moses,
sentences.zh: 我觉得我看到了一点，你可以看出有时当卡罗（Caro）谈论摩西（Moses）或暗示他见到摩西的那些时刻时，

sentences.en: that he does find him very impressive and that he is falling under the spell a little bit.
sentences.zh: 他确实觉得他非常令人印象深刻，而且他有点被他迷住了。

sentences.en: And maybe it's only the knowledge of the people that he's met whose lives were affected by him that pulls him back.
sentences.zh: 也许只有了解那些他所遇见、生活受他影响的人，才能让他清醒过来。

sentences.en: He talked to us about having the same experience that you had where Moses is showing him, you know, through the windows, Long Island.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我们，他有和你一样的经历，摩西向他展示，你知道，透过窗户看长岛。

sentences.en: He's saying, don't you believe there should be a road right there?
sentences.zh: 他说，你不觉得那里应该有一条路吗？

sentences.en: And he's like, uh-huh, uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 然后他回答说，嗯，嗯。

sentences.en: And then he walks, he's leaving.
sentences.zh: 然后他走开了，他要离开了。

sentences.en: He's like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 他心想，等一下。

sentences.en: That's not a good place for a road.
sentences.zh: 那地方不适合修路。

sentences.en: And I wonder if it is only that ability to hold on to that compassion for the people he's talked to who he does believe have been wronged that helps him to pull back.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，是否正是那种能够对他所交谈过、他认为受到不公正对待的人保持同情的能力，才帮助他抽离出来。

sentences.en: Do you ever feel like that where it's you kind of have to make the choice of who is worth maintaining that sympathy towards in your writing?
sentences.zh: 你有没有那种感觉，就是你必须在写作中做出选择，决定值得对谁保持那种同情？

sentences.en: Usually the ones that deserve that, that remains, right?
sentences.zh: 通常那些值得同情的人，那种感觉会留下来，对吧？

sentences.en: Past the car, like you get home and you're like, oh, I still feel this way.
sentences.zh: 过了车子那关，比如你回到家，你会想，哦，我还是这种感觉。

sentences.en: But, you know, people are intoxicating.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，人是令人陶醉的。

sentences.en: People with power are incredibly intoxicating.
sentences.zh: 有权力的人令人难以置信地陶醉。

sentences.en: And so you get drawn up in that orbit, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以你会被卷入那个轨道，你知道。

sentences.en: And I appreciated the building of him, only if it was that much further for him to fall.
sentences.zh: 我很欣赏对他形象的塑造，哪怕只是为了让他跌落得更惨。

sentences.en: But I appreciated all the physical descriptions of him, you know, swimming across the ocean.
sentences.zh: 但我很欣赏所有关于他的身体描述，你知道，横渡大洋。

sentences.en: And I'm like, his like booming voice, I'm like, this is a guy.
sentences.zh: 我心想，他那洪亮的声音，我心想，这才是个人物。

sentences.en: Like he has got it.
sentences.zh: 就像他真的很有本事。

sentences.en: And so I imagine when you're in his presence, you would feel that way too.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以想象，当你身处他面前时，你也会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Again, I feel that way all the time.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我一直都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: I'm a girl from Florida, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我是一个来自佛罗里达、佐治亚州的女孩。

sentences.en: Like I went to a state school.
sentences.zh: 我上的是州立大学。

sentences.en: Two different states in one place, yeah.
sentences.zh: 两个不同的州，同一个地方，是的。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: But like, you know, I'm not a New York City elite, despite what the folks who read my work
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我不是纽约市的精英，尽管那些读我作品的人

sentences.en: sometimes would have you believe.
sentences.zh: 有时会让你相信我是。

sentences.en: So I'm constantly impressed by people and things.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是对人和事感到印象深刻。

sentences.en: I went to visit this very fancy lawyer once.
sentences.zh: 我曾经去拜访过一位非常时髦的律师。

sentences.en: And he invited me into his office across from Lincoln Center.
sentences.zh: 他邀请我到他林肯中心对面的办公室。

sentences.en: And you went in, and the whole building was floor to ceiling marble and gold.
sentences.zh: 你走进去，整栋建筑从地板到天花板都是大理石和黄金。

sentences.en: And I was just like, this is so fancy.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，这太时髦了。

sentences.en: And I said that, and he's like, don't say that.
sentences.zh: 我说了出来，他说，别这么说。

sentences.en: Like, oh, okay, I will not.
sentences.zh: 就像，哦，好的，我不会了。

sentences.en: So I try to like temper some of my bumpkin tendencies.
sentences.zh: 所以我试着克制我的一些乡巴佬倾向。

sentences.en: But generally, like, I am impressed by so much.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，我很容易被很多东西打动。

sentences.en: And I do think, thank God that we have that time so much to go home and recalibrate and
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，感谢上帝，我们有那么多时间回家重新调整，

sentences.en: say, wait a minute, like, you know, you do not have to be in this person's spell.
sentences.zh: 然后说，等一下，你知道，你不必沉迷于这个人的魅力中。

sentences.en: I think the thing is, is that there are folks in my profession who never get that moment or
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于，我的同行中有些人从来没有那一刻，或者

sentences.en: never take that moment to say, pause, like, who am I serving with my journalism?
sentences.zh: 从来没有花时间去问：暂停一下，我的新闻工作是在为谁服务？

sentences.en: You know, am I writing about the right thing?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我写的东西对吗？

sentences.en: Am I writing this the right way?
sentences.zh: 我写的方式对吗？

sentences.en: Am I questioning power?
sentences.zh: 我是在质疑权力吗？

sentences.en: Or am I helping prop it up?
sentences.zh: 还是在帮它撑腰？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you cover conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 所以你报道阴谋论。

sentences.en: And a lot of that is to illuminate this world that is happening to people like me who don't
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分是为了向像我这样不相信这些阴谋论的人阐明这个世界正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: buy into those conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 但我从你的一些作品中感觉到，你试图向那些信徒呈现真实的世界，

sentences.en: But I get a sense of some of your work that you are trying to present the world as it is,
sentences.zh: 或者正如你所报道的那样，只是为了让他们从舒适区稍微挪动一下。

sentences.en: or as you report it, to those believers to just kind of maybe move them off of their comfortable
sentences.zh: 当涉及到某种，你知道，让他们离开内心深处真正相信的东西时，改变人们想法的方法是什么？

sentences.en: spot a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我不知道如何改变人们的想法。

sentences.en: And what are the methods to change people's minds when it comes to sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想我知道如何为那些可能会徘徊，或者可能会浅尝辄止于某种特定阴谋论的人写作和报道，毕竟每个人都相信某种阴谋论。

sentences.en: moving them off things that they really believe in their soul?
sentences.zh: 比如，我在聚会上最喜欢的话题——虽然我现在不怎么去聚会了，但

sentences.en: I don't know how to change people's minds.
sentences.zh: 就是问：你相信什么阴谋论？

sentences.en: I think I know how to write and report for people who may wander or may dip a toe into
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，每个人，我想我还没见过一个人是不相信某种可能不真实的东西的。

sentences.en: a specific conspiracy theory, which everybody believes a conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 比如，很多人相信，你知道，你的手机会导致耳癌。

sentences.en: Like, my favorite conversation at parties, which I don't go to very much anymore, but
sentences.zh: 很多人相信肯尼迪遇刺案，可能是最多人相信的。

sentences.en: is to ask, what conspiracy theory do you believe in?
sentences.zh: 我见过一些非常理智的人，他们的孩子和我的孩子一起玩，他们相信我们没有登上月球。

sentences.en: And, you know, everybody, I have yet, I think, to meet one person who doesn't believe something
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，有很多这样的人。

sentences.en: that is probably not true.
sentences.zh: 如果你想改变一个已经相信某种东西的人的想法，我认为那几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: Like, lots of people believe that, you know, your cell phone is giving you ear cancer.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有效的方法——这只是轶事，所以也许某处会有相关研究，但我不知道——是报道阴谋论背后的人。

sentences.en: Lots of people believe the Kennedy assassination, probably the most people.
sentences.zh: 所以，要么是那些从阴谋论中获利的人，要么是那些创造了阴谋论的人。

sentences.en: I've met some very reasonable people whose children play with my children who believe
sentences.zh: 所以，你就会有个概念，如果我只是告诉人们，你知道，疫苗不会导致自闭症，他们不相信。

sentences.en: that we did not land on the moon.
sentences.zh: 如果我报道显示疫苗不会导致自闭症的研究，他们也不相信。

sentences.en: So, I mean, there are, I just think that there's a lot of folks out there.
sentences.zh: 但如果我报道一个住在德克萨斯州奥斯汀的叫德尔·比格特里（Del Bigtree）的人，他靠这种反疫苗言论赚取了巨额财富，散布这个谎言，这是他用这些钱买的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: How you change someone's mind if they already believe something, I think that's almost impossible.
sentences.zh: 这是他和妻子住的房子，这是关于这个人的故事，他到处旅行去削弱疫苗法。

sentences.en: What I do think works, and this is only anecdotal, so maybe there will be some research on it
sentences.zh: 这是他戴着大卫之星，试图把自己比作大屠杀期间的犹太人。

sentences.en: somewhere, but I don't know of it, but is reporting on the people behind a conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 就像，这里所有的东西都能让你看着这个人说，我不相信他。

sentences.en: So, either the people who are profiting from that conspiracy theory, the people who have
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我发现的似乎很有影响力的事情。

sentences.en: created the conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像你是在用另一种阴谋论来为某人接种疫苗，以对抗那个阴谋论，而那种阴谋论是一种死胡同式的阴谋论。

sentences.en: So, you get an idea of, if I just tell people that, you know, vaccines aren't causing autism,
sentences.zh: 你知道，它没有那么大的破坏性。

sentences.en: they can't believe that.
sentences.zh: 你会说，并没有什么医疗组织、医疗机构，无论他们是谁，在联合起来对你撒谎。

sentences.en: If I report on research that shows vaccines don't cause autism, they don't believe that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由这家伙和其他靠这些谎言赚钱的人策划的阴谋。

sentences.en: But if I report on a man named Del Bigtree, who lives in Austin, Texas, and he makes an
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许这很有效，因为人们会想，现在我有了新的讨厌对象，你知道，我不知道。

sentences.en: exorbitant amount of money off of this anti-vax rhetoric, spreading this lie, and here's what
sentences.zh: 这不是阴谋。

sentences.en: he buys with that, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个计划。

sentences.en: Here's the house that he lives in with his wife, and here are the stories about this person
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像。

sentences.en: who, you know, goes and travels all over the country to weaken vaccine laws.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And here is him wearing a Star of David, trying to liken himself to Jews during the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像奥卡姆剃刀的方法，为什么你需要有这些复杂的转折，你知道，关于谁获利，谁做这个，为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: Like, here are all the things that can make you look at this man and say, I don't believe
sentences.zh: 而当最简单的动机是一个人靠撒谎致富时，这是一个相当好的相信理由，而且，你知道，这是我们人类历史上的一篇基础文本。

sentences.en: him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以。

sentences.en: So, that's something that I've found that I think is, seems to be impactful.
sentences.zh: 是的，作为一名记者，这是一个很容易找到的故事。

sentences.en: It's almost like you are, you are vaccinating someone against that conspiracy theory with
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: another conspiracy that is kind of a dead conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 那个靠一群相信谎言的人而致富的单身汉。

sentences.en: You know, it's not as, as damaging.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: You're like, there isn't some big conspiracy by the medical organization, the medical, whoever
